foci.d: Since 1966 Alexander Schalck-Golodkowski's Commercial Coordination has earned the hard currency the plan cannot. Now the MfS officer who keeps the republic's foreign-exchange books runs the republic itself - and every decision is weighed in D-Mark.
foci.o: Alt-hist: KoKo never governed; Schalck fled to West Berlin on 3 December 1989. Pro-Western but authoritarian: no free elections in this tree.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Hard-Currency Plan": Civilian industry tax +5 %, Trade opinion +5 %, Resource export revenue +5 %, Corruption costs +5 %
foci.d: In 1970 the republic owes Western banks some two billion Valuta marks, and every machine bought in the West raises the bill. Schalck's line replaces the planners' slogans: every Kombinat earns hard currency first - and the firm takes its cut.
foci.o: KoKo's economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: the firm's accounts are nobody's business (corruption costs). Choice hub: the fork below decides who the republic's best customer will be.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian factory productivity +3 %
foci.d: The richest customer lives next door. Inner-German trade knows no customs border, and every West German order is paid in D-Mark - in goods, transit fees and, sooner or later, political goodwill.
foci.o: Money and machines now; Moscow watches the republic slide towards Bonn (Moscow's Trust).

e: The Socialist Camp: Support campaigns (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: Machine tools for India, trucks for Iraq, optics for France, cranes for the Soviet Union: a customer in every market, so that no single customer - least of all Bonn - holds the republic's purse strings.
foci.o: Less money, more independence; the deals with the Third World's regimes raise tension.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): Bonn guarantees a bank credit of one billion D-Mark. If Bonn accepts: we receive treasury +1.5 % of GDP as debt and the course moves +0.10 towards Rapprochement; Bonn receives the dismantling of the SM-70 spring guns on the inner-German border and easier visits for families; Moscow's Trust -3 when the credit is signed. If Bonn refuses: nothing
foci.d: In 1983 Franz Josef Strauss, the republic's loudest enemy in Bonn, brokered a billion-mark credit with Schalck as his partner. Here the deal is struck a decade earlier (alt-hist).
foci.o: Our side on sending: the banks refinance on better terms the moment the talks are known (interest); the credit itself only comes if Bonn accepts.

e: The Planned Economy: Arms market income +6 %, Military industry tax +3 %
Unlocks decisions: Arms exports for hard currency (KoKo/IMES; Hard Currency category)
foci.d: IMES, Commercial Coordination's arms-trading house (historically founded 1981), sells rifles, ammunition and trucks from a depot at Kavelstorf near Rostock - in the 1980s to both sides of the Iran-Iraq War.
foci.o: Price: the church condemns arms sales into war zones; tension rises.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Republic as a Firm": Civilian industry tax +7 %, Trade opinion +5 %, Resource export revenue +5 %, Max factory efficiency +3 %, Corruption costs +10 %
Programme "The Hard-Currency Regime": Civilian factory output +3 %
foci.d: Profit centres instead of ministries, a balance sheet instead of a Five-Year Plan and an MfS officer as managing director: the workers' state becomes a company - with no shareholders' meeting and no elections.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "The Hard-Currency Plan". Price: the firm's managers supply Wandlitz - and themselves (corruption costs +10 %).

foci.d: The Intershops sell Jacobs coffee, jeans and Western cigarettes for D-Mark; through Genex, relatives in the West buy Trabants and even prefabricated houses for their families in the East. Whoever holds Western money lives better.
foci.o: Historically citizens were allowed to hold Western money from February 1974. The apparatus dislikes the Western shop windows.

foci.d: From 1974 every citizen may hold D-Mark and spend it in the Intershop: the republic collects the money Western relatives send. Whoever has an aunt in Hamburg now lives better than a factory director.
foci.o: Hard money in, a two-class society out (stability).

e: The Planned Economy: Consumer goods -2 %, Civilian factory productivity +3 %
foci.d: Since 1962 the Exquisit boutiques and since 1966 the Delikat shops sell Western-style goods for Marks of the GDR at steep prices. They soak up savings without handing a single citizen a D-Mark.
foci.o: Domestic alternative: no Western currency in private hands; the workers pay the Delikat prices (FDGB).

foci.d: Since 1963 Bonn has bought political prisoners out of East German jails - in the end some 34,000 people, paid for in oil, copper and coffee delivered through the churches. The republic exports its dissidents and imports hard currency.
foci.o: Same practice as the German Question focus "Freikauf" (which unlocks the decision); here it pays in goods (oil: fuel gain).

foci.d: From 1973 the state art-trading firm (Kunst & Antiquitäten GmbH) empties attics, manor houses and church lofts for Western dealers; collectors who refuse to sell are assessed for back taxes until they give in.

e: Shield and Sword: Intel network gain +10 %, Civilian intel +5 %
foci.d: The managers of Commercial Coordination remain 'officers on special duty' of the MfS, reporting to Erich Mielke. The firm and the Ministry are one - its trading houses in the West double as listening posts.
foci.o: The Ministry's firm: intelligence pays, the Kombinat directors resent the Stasi minders in every trade delegation.

foci.d: Schalck cuts the line to Normannenstraße: the firm answers to no ministry, only to its balance sheet. The directors cheer; Mielke keeps the files and waits.
foci.o: Political side of the fork: power for the firm (the tree's second PP), paid with the MfS's enmity.

foci.d: Founded in June 1945 by Andreas Hermes and Jakob Kaiser, purged by the Soviet administration in 1947 and tamed under Otto Nuschke and Gerald Götting, the East CDU rediscovers the Christian democracy it was founded for.
foci.o: Alt-hist: Götting stayed loyal to the SED until November 1989, when Lothar de Maizière replaced him.

foci.d: No more single lists: the Union leaves the National Front and stands on its own programme for the first time since 1950.
No more pressure to choose the Jugendweihe over confirmation, no more careers lost to faith: the churches may teach, publish and build again.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Christian Social Economy": Monthly population +0.03, Civilian factory productivity +3 %, Civilian industry tax +2 %, Social costs +5 %
foci.d: The 'Socialist Spring in the Countryside' of 1960 forced the last free farmers into the LPG, and thousands fled west. The Union's economics are Catholic social teaching and Protestant thrift: the family, the workshop and the farm come first.
foci.o: CDU's economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: family allowances and church welfare (social costs). Choice hub: who keeps the land.

foci.d: In September 1989 four East CDU members wrote to their own leadership demanding honesty and reform. Here the letter is written twenty years earlier - and the leadership answers it.

e: Adds "Church and State Reconciled": Stability +3 %, Western drift +0.01
foci.d: The Federation of Evangelical Churches (1969) is invited into the government's councils, and the state asks forgiveness for the persecution of the Junge Gemeinde in 1953 and the demolition of Leipzig's University Church in 1968.

e: The Planned Economy: Health costs -10 %, Social costs -6 %
foci.d: Since 1964 conscientious objectors may serve unarmed as 'construction soldiers' - and are barred from university for it. The Union offers a real civilian service in hospitals and care homes, as Dresden's church groups proposed.

e: Social spending +1 step (a family allowance for parents at home)
The Planned Economy: Monthly population +0.04, Workforce -2 %
foci.d: 86 % of the republic's women work, and the state raises the children in crèches. The Union pays mothers and fathers who want to stay at home - more children, fewer hands in the factories.
foci.o: Price: the labour shortage worsens (workforce cost line) and the social budget rises.

foci.d: Every LPG member may leave with his fields, his cattle and his share of the machines. The old farming families return to their yards - and the cooperatives lose their best land.
foci.o: Private farms: more income per field; the LPG members who stay behind pay (farmers).

e: The Planned Economy: Agriculture tax +8 %, Workforce +2 %
foci.d: The LPG stays, but membership becomes voluntary and the members elect their own chairmen. The cooperative farmers keep their security; the countryside changes slowly.
foci.o: Security for the villages; the farmers who wanted their own land back are disappointed (craftsmen and private farmers).

e: The Economic Line becomes "A Christian Social Market": Monthly population +0.03, Civilian factory productivity +5 %, Civilian industry tax +3 %, Civilian factory output +3 %, Social costs +8 %
foci.d: 'Property entails obligations', says the Basic Law: private initiative under a Christian social order. Prices are freed step by step, the family firms get credit, and the Kombinate must compete for the first time.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "The Christian Social Economy". Price: higher social costs; the Kombinat directors lose their monopoly.

foci.d: A people's party open to Protestants and Catholics, farmers and engineers: the Union stops being a bloc party and becomes a party of government that must answer the German question.
foci.o: Hub of the political fork: one Germany through Bonn, or a Christian republic of its own in the West.

foci.d: The sister party leads the opposition in Bonn and will govern again. Christian Democrats on both sides of the border prepare one party, one programme and one Germany - and the West German Union pays for the campaign.
foci.o: Western money and science now; Moscow's Trust falls.

e: Adds "A Christian Republic": Stability +3 %, Education costs -3 %, Bureaucracy costs +3 %
foci.d: Two German states, both Christian-democratic, both with the West: the republic keeps its own flag and its own seat, as Austria shows a German-speaking state can.
foci.o: A state of its own needs its own ministries (bureaucracy costs); the review layer adds SED Nomenklatura -5.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): Accession of the five restored states to the Federal Republic under Article 23 of the Basic Law. If Bonn accepts: an accession treaty - the republic is peacefully integrated into the Federal Republic after a one-year transition (the Soviet garrison is settled in a separate treaty). If Bonn refuses: course +0.10, stability -3 % - IF ACCEPTED, THE GDR CEASES TO EXIST: the game as the GDR ends.
foci.d: Article 23 of the Basic Law lets 'other parts of Germany' join the Federal Republic. Mecklenburg, Brandenburg, Saxony-Anhalt, Saxony and Thuringia - abolished as states in 1952 - apply to join; the decision lies in Bonn.
foci.o: Nothing happens to us or to Bonn before Bonn accepts (multiplayer rule).

e: Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): A phased withdrawal of the Group of Soviet Forces in Germany over three years. If Moscow accepts: "The Group of Soviet Forces in Germany" is removed when the withdrawal ends, we pay the Soviet Union 1 % of GDP for housing the returning officers (as Bonn did in 1990), tension -2. If Moscow refuses: tension +2, Moscow's Trust -10
The National People's Army: Defence on core territory +5 %, Recruitable population +2 %
foci.d: Twenty Soviet divisions stand between the Elbe and the Oder. A Christian republic that looks west cannot host them for ever: the government asks Moscow, politely and publicly, to bring its soldiers home.
foci.o: The garrison ladder belongs to the foreign section; here it is only asked for (offer). Moscow's answer carries the price.

e: Programme "Rule of Law and Free Enterprise": Civilian factory productivity +2 %
foci.d: The party of Wilhelm Külz - of craftsmen, doctors and shopkeepers - called its newspaper The Morning. Manfred Gerlach now promises the republic its liberal morning.
foci.o: Gerlach (chairman 1967-1990) was the first bloc leader to break with the SED in 1989; here he does it twenty years earlier.

foci.d: Independent judges, public trials and defence lawyers who actually defend: the state is bound by its own laws - the Ministry for State Security included.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Social Market Economy": Civilian factory productivity +5 %, Civilian industry tax +5 %, Social costs +5 %
foci.d: Gerlach's economists rewrite the economic line: prices that carry information, firms that may fail, and a social safety net beneath both. Two blueprints compete for the way there - Erhard's of 1948 and Budapest's of 1968.
foci.o: LDPD's economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: the safety net (social costs). Choice hub for the economic model.

foci.d: The press office of the Council of Ministers stops issuing instructions. Neues Deutschland gets competitors, and the journalists start with the privileges of the functionaries.

e: Adds "The Constitutional Court": Stability +3 %, Corruption costs -5 %, Western drift +0.01
foci.d: The republic never had one: the Volkskammer judged its own laws. Modelled on Karlsruhe, a constitutional court in Leipzig - the old seat of the Reich Court - now guards the citizens' rights.
foci.o: The court moves into the old Reich Court building (one office, paid).

foci.d: In 1950 the Waldheim trials sentenced some 3,400 people in minutes each; thousands more were broken in Bautzen and Hohenschönhausen. The new courts reopen the files and rehabilitate the victims.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian factory productivity +5 %, Civilian factory output +3 %
foci.d: On 20 June 1948 Ludwig Erhard freed West German prices overnight. The LDPD does the same: the subsidies go, the shelves fill - and the factories that cannot compete close their gates.
foci.o: Shock therapy: full shelves and the subsidy money now; open unemployment (stability) and Moscow's anger.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian industry tax +3 %, Max factory efficiency +3 %, Consumer goods +2 %
foci.d: Since 1968 Kádár's Hungary has used prices, profits and private plots without leaving the Warsaw Pact. Slower than Erhard - but Moscow can live with it.
foci.o: Market socialism inside Comecon: steadier gains, the shortages last longer (consumer goods). The review layer adds Moscow's Trust -2 and SED Nomenklatura -5.

e: The Planned Economy: Corporate tax revenue +2 %, Civilian factory output +3 %
Sets flag COLDWAR_DDR_ldpd_firms_returned (the 1972 nationalisation is undone or blocked)
foci.d: In 1972 the SED nationalised some 11,000 semi-state firms, private factories and craft cooperatives within months. The LDPD returns them to their owners - or, if it has not happened yet, stops the nationalisation for good.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Convertible Mark": Civilian factory productivity +5 %, Civilian industry tax +5 %, Investment cost for foreigners here -10 %, Return on investment +2 %, Social costs +5 %, Interest rates +3 %
Western credit: treasury +1.5 % of GDP, debt +1.5 % of GDP
Programme "Rule of Law and Free Enterprise": Civilian factory output +3 %
foci.d: The Mark of the GDR trades at one to four on the black market and buys nothing abroad. Gerlach makes it convertible: Western goods and investors arrive - and so does the truth about its value.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "The Social Market Economy". Price: a currency reserve borrowed in the West (debt, interest) and Moscow's Trust.

e: The Planned Economy: Social costs +6 %, Workforce +3 %
foci.d: The republic has not known open unemployment since the early 1950s; the market reform brings it back. Labour offices, retraining and unemployment pay cushion the blow - at a price.
foci.o: Welfare cost line (social costs); retraining brings people back to work (workforce).

foci.a: `western_liberals_are_in_power`; a border regime spirit is active (any step of the border ladder); the Western outlook focus "Tear Down the Wall" has not been completed (`NOT = { has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_we_tear_down_the_wall }`)
e: Ends The border regime in every form
foci.d: Every citizen receives a passport valid for all countries. The death strip is cleared and the order to shoot revoked - the Antifascist Protection Rampart has no purpose left.
foci.o: Removes the Rampart only if it still stands (owner of the ladder: border section; Western party trees may remove it). Visitors bring D-Mark; the young and skilled leave (workforce), Moscow's Trust falls.

foci.d: Courts, press and property are free. Now the liberals must answer the question every German liberal has asked since 1848: unity and freedom - in which order?
foci.o: Hub of the political fork: confederation or accession.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): A German confederation: customs and currency union and a joint council of ministers; both states keep their governments and alliances. If Bonn accepts: course +0.30 for us and the idea "The German Confederation" for both (trade opinion +15 %, research +3 %). If Bonn refuses: course +0.05
Programme "Rule of Law and Free Enterprise": Research sharing +5 %
foci.d: Two states, one market, one currency union and a joint council of ministers: unity in steps, with the republic's own institutions intact.
foci.o: Unity in steps: our scientists work with the West at once (research sharing); Moscow distrusts the joint council.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): Accession to the Federal Republic. If Bonn accepts: the republic joins the Federal Republic after a one-year transition (peaceful integration; the Soviet garrison is settled in a separate treaty). If Bonn refuses: stability -3 % - IF ACCEPTED, THE GDR CEASES TO EXIST: the game as the GDR ends.
foci.d: No half measures: the republic applies to join the Federal Republic, its Basic Law and its Mark. The liberals of 1848 would approve; the Kombinat directors and Moscow do not.
foci.o: Hope at home (stability); the craftsmen want the D-Mark, the Kombinat directors fear the West German competition.

foci.d: On 21 April 1946 the eastern SPD was merged into the SED with a handshake in the Admiralspalast. Friedrich Ebert, son of the first president of the Weimar Republic and a party to that merger himself, now leads the social democrats back out of it (alt-hist).
foci.o: Historically Friedrich Ebert Jr. (1894-1979) stayed in the SED Politburo; the SDP was only founded on 7 October 1989.

e: Social Democratic Party in the GDR popularity +3 %
foci.d: The Free German Trade Union Federation is free in name only: it hands out holidays and production pledges, not strikes. 17 June 1953 began as a workers' protest against higher norms - the social democrats have not forgotten.
foci.o: Hub of the union fork: reform the FDGB or allow unions beside it.

foci.d: In Bonn Willy Brandt's social-liberal coalition practises 'change through rapprochement'. In East Berlin a social-democratic government finally answers in the same language - and inner-German trade grows.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Social State": Workforce +2 %, Civilian factory productivity +3 %, Monthly population +0.02, Social costs +5 %
Social Democratic Party in the GDR popularity +3 %
foci.d: Social democracy promised more than full employment and cheap bread: decent pensions, shorter hours and a voice for the workers in their own factories. Ebert's economists write it into the economic line.
foci.o: SPD's economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: social costs. Choice hub: welfare first or growth first.

e: Social Democratic Party in the GDR popularity +2 %
foci.d: Free elections for every union post and the right to bargain over wages and norms: the old federation is turned from a transmission belt into a real union.
foci.o: One big union, democratised: the workers stay united; the SED loses its transmission belt (Nomenklatura).

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian factory productivity +3 %
Social Democratic Party in the GDR popularity +4 %
foci.d: Let the workers found their own unions, as the shipyard workers of Gdańsk will in 1980. The FDGB loses its monopoly - and its functionaries their power.
foci.o: Competing unions push productivity and the party's popularity; the old federation (FDGB) is the loser.

e: Social spending +1 step (pensions at a living wage)
Social Democratic Party in the GDR popularity +3 %
foci.d: Pensions barely cover rent and bread, and pensioners are the only citizens allowed to visit the West - the state does not mind if they stay there. The social democrats raise pensions to a living wage - on credit.
foci.o: Welfare first: stability and loyalty now; the bill is borrowed (interest rates).

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian industry tax +3 %, Civilian factory output +3 %
foci.d: Helmut Schmidt's rule - 'today's profits are tomorrow's investments and the day after tomorrow's jobs' - comes to East Berlin: first the roads, the plants and the export earnings, then the pensions.
foci.o: Growth first: investment and money now; the unions wanted the pensions (FDGB).

e: Social Democratic Party in the GDR popularity +3 %
The Planned Economy: Workforce -2 %, Monthly population +0.02
foci.d: Since 1967 the five-day week has had 43 and three-quarter hours. The social democrats bring in the forty-hour week - more life, less output.
foci.o: Price: fewer working hours (workforce cost line).

e: The Economic Line becomes "Co-Determination": Workforce +3 %, Civilian factory productivity +5 %, Monthly population +0.02, Max factory efficiency +2 %, Social costs +5 %
Social Democratic Party in the GDR popularity +2 %
foci.d: The West German coal and steel law of 1951 gave the workers half the seats on the supervisory boards. In the people's own enterprises the works councils now sit beside the director - and share the responsibility for the plan.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "The Social State". Price: the Kombinat directors share their power (faction).

foci.a: `western_social_democrats_are_in_power`; a border regime spirit is active (any step of the border ladder); the Western outlook focus "Tear Down the Wall" has not been completed (`NOT = { has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_we_tear_down_the_wall }`)
e: Ends The border regime in every form
Social Democratic Party in the GDR popularity +3 %
foci.d: Brandt's 'policy of small steps' began with passes for West Berliners at Christmas 1963. The social democrats finish the walk: citizens travel west without permission, and the Rampart's guns are withdrawn.
foci.o: Removes the Rampart only if it still stands. Price: the young and skilled leave (workforce), Moscow's Trust.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): A second Erfurt summit between two social-democratic governments. If Bonn accepts: course +0.10 for us, and both states receive the timed idea "The Erfurt Partnership" (trade opinion +10 %, research +2 % for 730 days). If Bonn refuses: nothing
Social Democratic Party in the GDR popularity +2 %
foci.d: On 19 March 1970 Erfurt cheered 'Willy, Willy' under the windows of the Erfurter Hof - the wrong Willy, as far as the SED was concerned. Ebert invites Brandt back, this time as a partner.

e: Social Democratic Party in the GDR popularity +4 %
foci.d: In 1959 the western SPD renounced Marxism at Bad Godesberg and became a people's party. The eastern party must decide what it is for: a better GDR, or one Germany.
foci.o: Hub of the political fork.

e: Adds "Democratic Socialism": Stability +3 %, Monthly population +0.02, Social costs +5 %
foci.d: Keep the people's own enterprises, the crèches and the polyclinics, add free elections and free unions: the republic becomes the social-democratic state the Weimar left never built.
foci.o: Political side: the party keeps the state (power) and pays for its polyclinics and crèches (social costs).

e: Social Democratic Party in the GDR popularity +4 %
foci.d: Kurt Schumacher's dream of 1946: a united Germany under social democracy. Ebert's party campaigns for unity with Brandt's Federal Republic - the strongest argument against it is quartered in Wünsdorf.
foci.o: Unity side: Western money and science now; Moscow's Trust falls.

e: Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): A staged withdrawal of the Group of Soviet Forces in Germany under a treaty of friendship and non-aggression; the republic stays in Comecon. If Moscow accepts: "The Group of Soviet Forces in Germany" is removed when the withdrawal ends, we pay the Soviet Union 1 % of GDP for barracks and housing, tension -2. If Moscow refuses: tension +1, Moscow's Trust -5
The National People's Army: Defence on core territory +5 %, Recruitable population +2 %
foci.d: A social-democratic GDR wants friendship with Moscow, not occupation. Ebert proposes a staged withdrawal of the Soviet divisions, guaranteed by a treaty of friendship.
foci.o: The garrison ladder belongs to the foreign section; here it is only asked for (offer). Moscow's answer carries the price.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): A treaty of unity: both states merge into one federal republic with a new constitution under Article 146. If Bonn accepts: unification after a one-year transition; the social rights of the GDR are kept for five years. If Bonn refuses: course +0.05, stability -2 % - IF ACCEPTED, THE GDR CEASES TO EXIST: the game as the GDR ends.
Social Democratic Party in the GDR popularity +4 %
foci.d: Two parliaments, one treaty: the social democrats in East Berlin and Bonn negotiate a union of equals under a new all-German constitution (Article 146 of the Basic Law) - not an accession.

e: Programme "The National Programme": Civilian industry tax +2 %
foci.d: Founded in 1948 with the SED's blessing to give former Wehrmacht officers, nominal Nazi party members and the national middle class a political home, Lothar Bolz's NDPD was meant to keep nationalism on a leash. Now it holds the leash.
foci.o: Alt-hist: Bolz (chairman 1948-1972) was a loyal bloc politician and the GDR's Foreign Minister 1953-1965.

e: The Economic Line becomes "A National Economy": Civilian factory productivity +3 %, Civilian industry tax +3 %, Sanction resistance (Imperia) +5 %, Trade opinion -3 %
foci.d: The NDPD always spoke for the shopkeepers, master craftsmen and small manufacturers. Its economics are simple - German work for German welfare, bought at home where possible - but who pays for the welfare?
foci.o: NDPD's economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: national preference costs trade goodwill. Choice hub: thrift or bread.

foci.d: Potsdam and Dresden, Frederick the Great and Augustus the Strong: the two great traditions of the republic's lands are restored to honour - palaces, regiments and all.

e: The National People's Army: Defence on core territory +5 %
foci.d: In the Görlitz Agreement of 6 July 1950 the GDR recognised the Oder-Neisse line as the 'border of peace and friendship'. The Silesians and East Prussians in the NDPD never quite accepted it - the party must now say what it thinks.
foci.o: Choice hub: confirm the border or leave the question open. No claims are created and no war is possible from this fork.

e: The Party State: Bureaucracy costs -7 %, Corruption costs -3.5 %
foci.d: Frederick William I, the 'soldier king', left a full treasury and no debts. The NDPD cuts subsidies and administration alike - honest budgets, thinner pay packets.
foci.o: Austerity: money now, the people pay (stability).

foci.d: Cheap bread, cheap rents and a national bonus for every family with three children: the NDPD buys the loyalty of the nation - and the bill comes later.
foci.o: Populism: stability now, the state pays (social costs).

e: The Planned Economy: Consumer goods -2 %, Corporate tax revenue +1 %
foci.d: NDPD members own the bakeries, butcher shops and small factories the state has been squeezing. Their firms get tax relief, credit and the right to hire.

e: The Economic Line becomes "German Quality Work": Civilian factory productivity +5 %, Civilian industry tax +5 %, Sanction resistance (Imperia) +5 %, Max factory efficiency +3 %, Trade opinion -5 %
Programme "The National Programme": Civilian factory output +3 %
foci.d: 'Deutsche Wertarbeit' was the boast of Saxony's toolmakers and Thuringia's glassblowers long before the Kombinate. The national government stakes the economy on it: fewer, better products, made at home and sold on quality.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "A National Economy". Price: national preference costs more trade goodwill.

foci.d: Dresden's opera house has stood in ruins since the firestorm of February 1945; historically it was rebuilt from 1977 to 1985. Here it is the first act of a national government - an expensive one.
foci.o: Dresden's craftsmen get the contracts; the treasury pays (0.5 % of GDP).

e: The National People's Army: Recruitable population +3 %, Training time -5 %
foci.d: Every young German serves the nation for a year - in the NVA, in the hospitals or on the building sites. Prussia's 'school of the nation' reopens, without the drill sergeant's cane.
foci.o: Price: a year of every young worker's life (workforce).

foci.d: The nation is whole within its borders: the NDPD confirms Görlitz without reservation. Warsaw is relieved, Moscow satisfied, and the expellee associations in the West call it treason.
foci.o: Friends in Warsaw and Moscow; the party's own nationalists turn away (popularity).

foci.d: Bonn has kept the border question open 'pending a peace treaty' - why should East Berlin not? No claim is made and no soldier moves, but the words alone chill Warsaw and alarm Moscow.
foci.o: Our opinion of Poland falls and tension rises; nothing is claimed, nothing is executed in Poland.

foci.d: Ulbricht's constitution of 1968 called the GDR 'a socialist state of the German nation'. The NDPD drops the adjective and keeps the noun: two states, one nation, one future.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): A national confederation: common citizenship and a joint national assembly; each state keeps its army and its alliance. If Bonn accepts: course +0.30 and the idea "The National Confederation" for both (trade opinion +10 %, stability +2 %). If Bonn refuses: Nationalist outlook popularity +3 % for us (wounded pride)
foci.d: A common citizenship, a joint national assembly and an open inner-German border, each state keeping its own army: the NDPD asks Bonn whether national democrats can be partners.
foci.o: Different from the outlook focus "The German Question Is Open" (joint council): this offer adds a common citizenship and assembly.

e: Programme "Rule by Decree": Military factory productivity +3 %
Elections are abolished; the Volkskammer is dissolved
foci.d: A council of officers, functionaries and agitators without names seizes the collapsing state. It promises order and national rebirth; it delivers decrees, curfews and fear (alt-hist).
foci.o: Player only. Sober depiction of a dictatorship: every gain is paid for in isolation, faction ruin, stability or Moscow's Trust.

e: The Party State: Ideology drift defence +10 %
foci.d: Lists are drawn up in every ministry, Kombinat and barracks. Whoever served the old order must prove his loyalty to the new one - or disappear.
foci.o: Choice hub: which pillar of the old state is broken.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Autarky": Sanction resistance (Imperia) +8 %, Military factory productivity +5 %, Fuel gain +5 %, Consumer goods +8 %, Trade opinion -10 %
foci.d: No Western credit, no Comecon delegation, no foreign journalist: the council closes the country more tightly than the Wall ever did. Whatever the republic needs, it must now make itself - the shelves empty first.
foci.o: NRF's economic identity (Economic Line). Price: empty shelves and no trade (consumer goods, trade opinion); Moscow's Trust falls towards "The Brezhnev Doctrine".

foci.d: The SED's two million members are ordered to hand in their cards; district secretaries are arrested at their desks. The apparatus that ran the republic for twenty years is gone - and with it the people who knew how.
foci.o: Political side: the council takes the party's power (the tree's second PP); the Nomenklatura is destroyed.

e: Shield and Sword: Intel network gain +10 %, Civilian intel +5 %, Encryption +10 %
foci.d: The council fears Mielke's 43,000 officers more than any party. The Ministry for State Security is stormed, its officers interned - and its files and its Guards Regiment handed to the council's own secret police.
foci.o: The council inherits the files and the Guards Regiment; the MfS officers who survive will never forgive.

e: The Planned Economy: Workforce +3 %, Fuel gain +5 %
foci.d: Ration cards return for the first time since 1958. Lignite, potatoes and labour brigades are to replace what Comecon and the West no longer deliver; Schwarzheide and Leuna turn brown coal into petrol.
foci.o: Labour service and synthetic fuel; the workers pay with ration cards and compulsory shifts.

e: The National People's Army: Recruitable population +4 %, Defence on core territory +5 %
foci.d: A militia company in every factory, a shooting range in every school, a minefield on every border: the council arms seventeen million people against enemies on all sides - most of them imagined.
foci.o: Arms instead of goods (consumer goods); Moscow and the West both watch the armed camp.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Fortress Economy": Sanction resistance (Imperia) +8 %, Military factory productivity +8 %, Fuel gain +5 %, Consumer goods +10 %, Trade opinion -10 %
foci.d: Five years behind closed borders: every factory works to a war plan, every field to a ration, and the republic needs nothing from anyone - except the things it can no longer have.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "Autarky". Price: consumer goods +10 %, trade opinion -10 %, the FDGB.

e: Programme "Order and Readiness": Military factory productivity +3 %
foci.d: Colonel General Heinz Keßler, Chief of the NVA's Main Staff - a Wehrmacht soldier who crossed over to the Red Army in 1941 - heads a council of generals in Strausberg. The party has failed; the army takes over, 'temporarily'.
foci.o: Alt-hist: historically Keßler became Minister of National Defence in 1985 and never broke with the SED.

e: Elections are suspended under martial law
The Party State: Ideology drift defence +5 %
The National People's Army: Army personnel costs +5 %
foci.d: Curfews, military tribunals and soldiers at the gates of the Kombinate. The streets are quiet; the queues outside the shops are not.
foci.o: Price: army personnel costs (soldiers on the streets).

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Barracks Economy": Military factory productivity +5 %, Recruitable population +2 %, Military factory construction +5 %, Consumer goods +5 %
foci.d: Explosives from Schönebeck, rifles from Suhl, W50 trucks from Ludwigsfelde, landing ships from Wolgast: the generals take personal charge of the factories that equip them - and write the plan as a staff order.
foci.o: The junta's economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: consumer goods. Choice hub: whom the arsenal serves.

e: The National People's Army: Training time -5 %
foci.d: The Warsaw Pact plans to carry any war to the Rhine within days, with the NVA in its first strategic echelon. The council must decide whether the army exists for the alliance or for the homeland.
foci.o: Choice hub: forward defence or defence of the homeland.

e: The National People's Army: Recruitable population +2 %
foci.d: The Combat Groups of the Working Class - several hundred thousand men in factory overalls - answer to the SED district leaderships and the Interior Ministry. The council puts them under NVA command as a territorial army.

e: The Party State: Bureaucracy costs -7 %, Corruption costs -3.5 %
foci.d: Colonels replace the state secretaries: the ministries are run like a staff, with orders, deadlines and reports - and no patience for the planners' excuses.

e: The Planned Economy: Arms market income +5 %, Military industry tax +3 %
foci.d: Kalashnikovs from Wiesa, trucks from Ludwigsfelde, patrol boats from Wolgast - sold to Baghdad, Tripoli and Addis Ababa for hard currency. The generals become arms dealers; their own regiments wait.
foci.o: Money first; the officers who wanted the new equipment for themselves grumble.

e: The National People's Army: Equipment costs -5 %, Licence production speed +5 %
foci.d: Every rifle the republic makes stays with the NVA: licence production of Soviet tanks and guns at full speed, and a modern army that the shops pay for.
foci.o: A better-equipped army; the price is paid in the shops (consumer goods).

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Arsenal Economy": Military factory productivity +8 %, Recruitable population +2 %, Military factory construction +5 %, Equipment costs -3 %, Consumer goods +8 %
foci.d: 'Special production' is the plan's word for weapons. The council doubles it: licence-built Kalashnikovs, ammunition and armoured personnel carriers - and fewer washing machines.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "The Barracks Economy". Price: consumer goods +8 %.

e: The National People's Army: Army attack +5 %, Army speed +5 %

Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): A joint Warsaw Pact exercise on our soil, like "Brotherhood in Arms 70" in October 1970. If Moscow accepts: army experience +25 for both, Moscow's Trust +5 for us, tension +1. If Moscow refuses: nothing
foci.d: The NVA trains to reach the Rhine: two armies of six divisions, ready to cross the inner-German border on the first day. Moscow approves; the West notices.
foci.o: Moscow approves (trust); Cold War tension rises.

e: The National People's Army: Defence on core territory +5 %, Recruitable population +3 %
foci.d: No divisions for the Rhine: the NVA digs in between the Elbe and the Oder with reservists, fortified towns and the Combat Groups. The West relaxes a little; Moscow's planners do not.
Martial law was declared 'until order is restored', and order is restored. Now the generals must say how long 'until' lasts - and what the army's budget will be.
foci.o: Hub of the political fork.

foci.d: The council promises to step down within three years and hand the state to an elected civilian government - as Portugal's captains will do after 1974.
foci.o: Political side: legitimacy and public goodwill (the tree's second PP); the colonels who wanted to stay are disappointed.

e: Adds "The Generals' Republic": Political power gain +5 %, War support +5 %, Stability -3 %
Programme "Order and Readiness": Military factory productivity +2 %
Military Council of the NVA popularity +3 %
foci.d: There will be no return to the party and no elections. The council becomes the state, and its chairman wears the uniform of an Army General.

e: Elections are allowed: the council hands power to the winner of the next election
Unlocks decisions: "Return to Civilian Rule": the most popular non-military party takes over after the election
foci.d: Free elections under the army's guard; the winner forms a civilian government, and the generals return to Strausberg with their honour and their budget intact.
foci.o: Hand-back is a decision of our own country (no other country affected).

e: The National People's Army: Training time -5 %, Daily army experience +0.05
foci.d: Officer schools train the administrators, a general runs every district and the GST is the only youth organisation: the republic is reorganised as one great military district.

e: Programme "The Prussian Restoration": Civilian industry tax +2 %
foci.d: Louis Ferdinand, Prince of Prussia - grandson of the last Kaiser, once a worker on Henry Ford's assembly line in Detroit, head of the House of Hohenzollern since 1951 - is invited from Bremen back to Potsdam (alt-hist). Sanssouci, the New Palace and Cecilienhof become the seat of the crown; the open question is what kind of crown.
foci.o: Player only. Hub of the crown fork ("The Return to Potsdam" was merged into this root on 18.10.).

e: The Economic Line becomes "Prussian Thrift": Bureaucracy costs -5 %, Corruption costs -5 %, Civilian industry tax +3 %, Consumer goods +2 %
foci.d: Duty, thrift and incorruptibility: Frederick William I balanced his budget to the last thaler and hanged a corrupt official at the gate of Königsberg castle. The crown's economics fit on a parade ground - and pinch every household.
foci.o: The crown's economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: thrift empties the shelves (consumer goods). Choice hub: estates or manufactories.

e: The Party State: Ideology drift defence +5 %
foci.d: 'Suum cuique' was the motto of the Order of the Black Eagle; Frederick's Prussia took in Huguenots, Salzburg Protestants and Bohemian weavers. The crown protects the churches, the Sorbs and every honest dissenter.
foci.o: Tolerance first: the officers wanted a crown of the barracks (NVA Command).

e: The National People's Army: Army morale +5 %, Army organisation +3 %
foci.d: The NVA's stone-grey uniforms and parade step are already Prussian. Now its regiments take back the old names and colours, and the officers swear an oath to the crown.

e: The Planned Economy: Agriculture tax +5 %, agriculture_district_income_tax_modifier +5 %
foci.d: The land reform of 1945 took every estate over 100 hectares from the Junkers. The crown returns the manor farms to the old families as model estates - and the cooperative farmers lose their best fields.
foci.o: The estates pay taxes and feed the towns; the LPG farmers pay with their land.

e: Programme "The Prussian Restoration": Civilian factory productivity +3 %, Civilian factory output +3 %
foci.d: Frederick the Great founded the Royal Porcelain Manufactory in Berlin and filled Prussia with silk, glass and cloth works. The crown does the same with state money: new manufactories under royal warrant.
foci.o: Industry under royal warrant; the treasury pays (0.5 % of GDP).

e: Elections are allowed: constitutional monarchy with a responsible government
Adds "A Crown Under the Law": Stability +3 %, Western drift +0.01, Political power gain -5 %
foci.d: A king who reigns but does not rule: a parliament elected by all and a prime minister responsible to it - the model of London and Stockholm, not of 1914.
foci.o: The crown gives up power (political power gain -5 % in the idea); the officers wanted a real king.

e: The National People's Army: Army organisation +3 %
foci.d: The king appoints the government and commands the army; parliament may advise. It is the Prussia of 1850 and its three-class franchise - with few friends abroad and many enemies at home.
foci.o: Political side: the crown rules (the tree's second PP); the people are not asked (stability).

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): The return of the coffins of Frederick the Great and Frederick William I from Hohenzollern Castle to Potsdam. If Bonn accepts: stability +3 %, political power +100 and course +0.05 for us; our opinion of Bonn +20. If Bonn refuses: Nationalist outlook popularity +2 % for us
foci.d: The coffins of Frederick the Great and his father have rested at Hohenzollern Castle in Württemberg since 1952; historically Frederick was laid to rest at Sanssouci, as he had wished, only in 1991. The crown asks Bonn to let him come home now.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Prussian State Economy": Bureaucracy costs -7 %, Corruption costs -5 %, Civilian industry tax +5 %, Civilian factory output +3 %, Consumer goods +3 %
foci.d: Frederick the Great founded the Seehandlung in 1772 - a royal trading house that became Prussia's state bank and financed its mills, canals and salt works. The crown revives it: a royal treasury that lends to the estates and the manufactories and runs a surplus.
foci.o: Economic capstone: upgrades "Prussian Thrift". Price inside the idea: consumer goods.

e: New name and flag: Kingdom of Prussia (cosmetic tag COLDWAR_DDR_kingdom_of_prussia)
Adds "The Kingdom of Prussia": Stability +5 %, Ideology drift defence +5 %
foci.d: Proclaimed in the Marble Hall of the New Palace, the Prussian state that the Allies abolished in 1947 returns as a kingdom on the Spree and the Havel. Whether anyone beyond its borders will recognise it is another matter.
foci.o: Political capstone (no PP). The cosmetic tag is written as custom() because md_check does not know the DSL kind 'cosmetic' (E-kind error); the generator should emit set_cosmetic_tag = COLDWAR_DDR_kingdom_of_prussia.

e: Programme "The Rule of the Planners": Economic cycle law costs -1 %
foci.d: Gerhard Schürer, chairman of the State Planning Commission since 1965, takes the government: the plan, not the Politburo's slogans, now decides.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Honest Plan": Civilian factory productivity +5 %, Economic cycle law costs -5 %, Interest rates -3 %, Bureaucracy costs +5 %
foci.d: In October 1989 Schürer told the Politburo that the republic lived on Western credit and could not pay. Here the report is written in 1970 - and published, and the economic line is rewritten to fit the numbers.
foci.o: Alt-hist: the real report of 30 October 1989 moved two decades earlier. The planners' economic identity (Economic Line); price inside the idea: more planners (bureaucracy costs). Choice hub: austerity or growth.

foci.b: `has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_micro_the_eser_computers` (the ESER computers - no double reward)
e: The Planned Economy: Max factory efficiency +2 %
foci.d: Comecon's Unified System of Electronic Computers: Robotron in Dresden builds the EC 1040, and the planners finally get machines to count with.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian industry tax +3 %, Consumer goods +2 %
foci.d: Every Kombinat gets a hard-currency export target. What the West will buy is no longer sold in the shops at home.
foci.o: Price: the best goods leave the shops (consumer goods). Choice hub: where the republic sells.

foci.d: Engineers, economists and Kombinat directors replace the party secretaries in the Council of Ministers. The Central Committee's economic departments lose their right to give orders.
foci.o: Political side: the planners take the power (the tree's second PP); the Nomenklatura is shut out.

foci.d: Schürer governs with the party, not against it: the SED keeps its seats and its cadre lists, and the planners get the apparatus's loyalty in return - and its habits.
foci.o: Stability and Moscow's goodwill; the price is the apparatus's privileges (corruption).

e: Programme "The Rule of the Planners": Sanction resistance (Imperia) +5 %
The Planned Economy: Interest rates -8 %, Construction speed -5 %
foci.d: Live within our means: fewer Western imports, no more prestige projects, every surplus Deutschmark goes to pay back the debt.
foci.o: Cheaper money and independence; fewer building sites (construction speed).

e: Western credit: treasury +1.5 % of GDP, debt +1.5 % of GDP
The Planned Economy: Civilian factory construction +5 %, Civilian factory productivity +3 %
foci.d: Borrow now, grow later: Western credits buy the machines, and the machines will earn the hard currency to repay them.
foci.o: New plants on credit (debt); Moscow distrusts the Western banks.

foci.d: Rents frozen at the level of 1936, bread rolls at five pfennigs: the price subsidies swallow billions every year. Schürer cuts them.

e: Western credit: treasury +2 % of GDP, debt +2 % of GDP
The Planned Economy: Max factory efficiency +3 %
foci.d: Frankfurt, Vienna and Tokyo lend to the most reliable debtor in the East. The new plants open on time - the interest falls due on time too.
foci.o: The review layer adds Moscow's Trust -3.

foci.d: Every district gets a computing centre; the plan figures of thousands of enterprises travel to Berlin on punched cards.
foci.o: The district computing centres (one office, paid).

e: The Planned Economy: Economic cycle law costs -3 %, Civilian factory output +3 %
foci.d: Linear programming on the EC 1040: Kantorovich's mathematics balances what no ministry ever could - and the apparatus's instinct is no longer needed.

e: The Socialist Camp: Research sharing +5 %, Trade opinion -3 %
foci.d: The Comprehensive Programme of 1971: the republic builds the machine tools, ships and computers of the socialist camp and is paid in roubles.
foci.o: Steady orders and shared research in the camp; Western customers drift away (trade opinion).

e: The Socialist Camp: Trade opinion +5 %, World-market exposure (Cold War) +10 %
Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): Bonn raises the interest-free 'swing' overdraft of inner-German trade; if accepted: income +0.5 % of GDP and Inner-German course +0.05 for us
foci.d: Machine tools from Karl-Marx-Stadt, optics from Jena, potash from the Werra - sold for Deutschmarks and dollars, not transferable roubles.
foci.o: Hard currency now; the republic becomes exposed to the world market's crises.

e: The Planned Economy: Interest rates -4 %, Civilian industry tax +3 %
foci.d: For the first time the plan balances imports and exports in both currencies - roubles and Deutschmarks - and nobody hides the gap.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Plan Without Lies": Civilian factory productivity +5 %, Economic cycle law costs -5 %, Max factory efficiency +3 %, Corruption costs -5 %, Bureaucracy costs +5 %
Programme "The Rule of the Planners": Civilian factory output +3 %
foci.d: True numbers, computed plans, no more 'plan fulfilled 101 %': the planners' republic has a budget it can show to anyone.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "The Honest Plan" (no PP).

e: Programme "A Church for Others": Monthly population +0.02
foci.d: Bishop Albrecht Schönherr, Bonhoeffer's student, leads a government of the church: not against socialism, not beside it, but within it.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Economy of Care": Stability +2 %, Monthly population +0.02, Health costs -5 %, Civilian industry tax -2 %
foci.d: The church runs dozens of hospitals and hundreds of homes for the old and the disabled - the care the state forgot. Now the care becomes the economic line: people before plan figures.
foci.o: The church's economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: less revenue from industry. Choice hub: hospitals or ploughshares.

e: The Planned Economy: Health costs -5 %, Energy use -3 %
foci.d: The church's research home in Luther's town publishes what the state statistics hide: the air, the water, the forests. Environmental circles meet in the parish halls.
Since June 1969 the eight regional churches of the GDR stand together in their own federation, separate from the West German EKD.

e: Offer to POL (they decide; no advance reward): A treaty of reconciliation: church partnerships, joint youth work camps and open crossings on the Oder; if Poland accepts: opinion +25 on both sides and trade opinion +5 % for both
foci.d: Action Reconciliation sends young East Germans to work at Auschwitz and in Polish hospitals. The government takes up the work of atonement.

e: The Planned Economy: Health costs -10 %, Monthly population +0.04
foci.d: The state hands its polyclinics and care homes to the Inner Mission and the Caritas, and pays for them: nurses, deaconesses and doctors who stay instead of leaving for the West.
foci.o: Care first: the treasury pays (0.3 % of GDP and a higher health budget).

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian factory output +3 %, Civilian factory construction +5 %, Military factory productivity -3 %
foci.d: The badge shows the Soviet statue in front of the UN - a man forging a sword into a ploughshare. Here it is state policy: arms plants make tractors.
foci.o: Alt-hist: the badge of 1980-82, which the state historically banned, becomes the government's programme. Price: the arms industry (faction, military factory productivity).

e: The Economic Line becomes "Justice, Peace and the Integrity of Creation": Stability +3 %, Monthly population +0.03, Health costs -8 %, Civilian factory productivity +2 %, Civilian industry tax -3 %
foci.d: The Conciliar Process of the churches - historically the ecumenical assemblies of Dresden and Magdeburg in 1988-89 - becomes the programme of government: justice for the weak, peace without weapons and an economy that spares creation.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "The Economy of Care" (no PP).

e: Adds "The Peace Republic": Stability +5 %, Non-aligned drift +0.03, War support -10 %, Consumer goods -3 %
Defence spending is cut one step
foci.d: A republic that refuses the logic of deterrence: fewer soldiers, no nuclear weapons on its soil, neutrality as a Christian duty.

e: Adds "The Christian Republic": Stability +3 %, Western drift +0.01, Education costs -3 %
foci.d: The Ten Commandments replace Ulbricht's Ten Commandments of Socialist Morality: confirmation instead of the state youth ceremony, and an open hand to the Christian Democrats in the West.
foci.o: A Christian state with friends in the West; Moscow distrusts it (Moscow's Trust).

foci.d: The churches may run schools again, and Christian pupils may study at university without a party card.

e: Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): The Group of Soviet Forces in Germany withdraws within five years; if Moscow accepts: "The Group of Soviet Forces in Germany" is removed, tension -2, Moscow's Trust -10
foci.d: Twenty Soviet divisions stand between the Elbe and the Oder. The Peace Republic asks the Kremlin, politely and in public, to take them home.
foci.o: Garrison ladder belongs to the foreign agent: this path only asks Moscow (offer); nothing is removed before the Soviet Union accepts.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): West German churches and Bonn pay in goods and hard currency for the church's hospitals and homes in the East; if Bonn accepts: income +0.5 % of GDP and Inner-German course +0.10 for us
foci.d: The churches of East and West were one until 1969. Now the Christian Republic asks Bonn to fund the church's work openly - and to talk to its government.
Since 1964 young men who refuse the weapon serve with a spade - the only unarmed service in the Warsaw Pact. The church's government honours them.

foci.b: `has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_kg_the_social_peace_service` (the social peace service - no double reward)
foci.d: The Dresden proposal, made law: conscientious objectors serve in hospitals, homes and on the land instead of the army.
foci.o: Historically proposed by Dresden church circles in 1981 (Sozialer Friedensdienst) and rejected by the state. The NVA loses recruits.

e: The Planned Economy: Workforce +3 %, Civilian factory productivity +2 %
foci.d: Eighteen months of compulsory service end: the NVA becomes an army of volunteers, and the factories get their young men back.

e: Programme "The Directors' Charter": Civilian factory output +2 %
foci.d: The general directors of the Kombinate - Wolfgang Biermann of Carl Zeiss Jena at their head - stop asking the ministries and start running the state.
A hundred general directors form the real cabinet; the ministers become their clerks.
foci.o: Hub of the political fork: what to do with the party.

foci.d: Seats on the Kombinat boards for district secretaries, hunting lodges and Volvos for the Politburo: the party is bought, not fought.
foci.o: The apparatus works for the directors - Moscow is reassured; the price is corruption.

e: The Party State: Bureaucracy costs -10 %, Corruption costs -3.5 %
The Planned Economy: Civilian factory productivity +3 %
foci.d: The industrial departments of the Central Committee and half the ministries are dissolved; the directors answer to their balance sheets alone.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Self-Financing of the Kombinate": Civilian industry tax +5 %, Civilian factory output +3 %, Max factory efficiency +2 %, Corruption costs +5 %
foci.d: The Kombinate keep what they earn and invest it themselves - Ulbricht's reform of the 1960s, taken to its end and written into the economic line.
foci.o: The directors' economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: nobody audits the directors (corruption costs). Choice hub: who owns the Kombinate.

e: Adds "Kombinat Holdings": Max factory efficiency +4 %, Civilian factory productivity +3 %, Corruption costs +5 %
Programme "The Directors' Charter": Civilian factory output +2 %
foci.d: The Kombinate become state holding companies: the directors own the management and a share of the profits, the state owns the shares - for now.
foci.o: Shares for the directors: their own money in the game - and in their own pockets (corruption costs).

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): West German firms may hold up to 49 % in joint ventures with the Kombinate; if Bonn accepts: two civilian factories are built in the republic at the investors' cost and Inner-German course +0.10
The Planned Economy: Licence production speed +5 %
foci.d: Krupp, Siemens and Volkswagen in Zwickau and Jena: half the shares, half the profits - and all the know-how the embargo lists forbid.
foci.o: Alt-hist: the GDR never allowed Western equity; it only produced under licence. Moscow distrusts Western owners.

e: Programme "The Directors' Charter": Max factory efficiency +2 %
The Planned Economy: Civilian factory output +3 %
foci.d: Twenty giant concerns swallow the rest of industry - and the last private and semi-state suppliers with it.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian industry tax +4 %, Consumer goods +2 %
foci.d: Swedish furniture, West German shoes and mail-order catalogue goods are made in Kombinat workshops for Western brands - the best goods leave the country.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Kombinat Republic": Civilian industry tax +7 %, Civilian factory output +5 %, Max factory efficiency +3 %, Corruption costs +10 %
foci.d: The red barons own the republic in all but name: efficient, rich - and every director has his dacha, his car and his hard-currency account.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "Self-Financing of the Kombinate" (no PP). Price: corruption costs +10 %, the FDGB.

e: The Planned Economy: Resource export revenue +3 %
foci.d: The directors build new export halls with their own money and keep a share of the hard currency they earn - the workers get the overtime.
Biermann's own house: cameras, microscopes, planetaria and space cameras for Soviet spacecraft - the flagship sells to the whole world and builds the republic's first chip lines.
foci.o: Biermann led Carl Zeiss Jena from 1975; here he brings the Kombinat into government.

e: Programme "The Craftsmen's Charter": Civilian industry tax +2 %
foci.d: No single leader: master craftsmen, shopkeepers and the owners of the semi-state firms govern as a council - an alt-hist union of the middle class.

e: The Planned Economy: Consumer goods -2 %, Civilian factory productivity +3 %
Union of Crafts and Trade popularity +2 %
foci.d: In spring 1972 the SED took the last 11,000 private and semi-state firms - the makers of furniture, toys, textiles and spare parts. The council gives them back.
foci.o: Alt-hist from 1970: the nationalisation is undone (or never completed) before it happens. Choice hub: who gets the firms.

e: The Planned Economy: Corporate tax revenue +1 %
Union of Crafts and Trade popularity +2 %
foci.d: The firms go back to the families that founded them - some heirs live in Stuttgart and Munich and come back with Western money.
foci.o: Owners and Western money; Moscow sees capitalists return.

e: Union of Crafts and Trade popularity +3 %
foci.d: The firms become workers' companies: every employee holds a share, the master craftsman keeps the management.
foci.o: Workers' companies; the old owners get nothing back (craftsmen).

e: The Economic Line becomes "Free Enterprise": Consumer goods -3 %, Civilian industry tax +5 %, Civilian factory productivity +2 %, Stability -2 %
Union of Crafts and Trade popularity +2 %
foci.d: The Office for Prices stops fixing what a chair, a cake or a car repair may cost: the market sets the price, and the council writes free enterprise into the economic line.
foci.o: The craftsmen's economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: prices rise before the shelves fill (stability). Choice hub: free trade or the guilds.

e: Adds "Free Trade": Trade opinion +5 %, Civilian industry tax +3 %, World-market exposure (Cold War) +10 %
foci.d: Open the market: private firms may import, export and compete with the Kombinate - and with the West.
foci.o: Open markets and money; world-market exposure and Moscow's distrust.

e: Adds "The Guild Economy": Max factory efficiency +3 %, Stability +3 %, Trade opinion -5 %
Programme "The Craftsmen's Charter": Civilian factory productivity +2 %
foci.d: The old craft order returns: guilds set standards, train apprentices and protect their members from the Kombinate and from foreign competition.
foci.o: Quality and security behind the guild walls; foreign customers are kept out (trade opinion).

foci.n: The Leipzig Fair All Year Round
e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): Inner-German trade without quotas and with free private contracts; if Bonn accepts: trade opinion +10 %, income +0.5 % of GDP and Inner-German course +0.10 for us
The Planned Economy: Resource export revenue +5 %
foci.d: Since the Middle Ages Leipzig has been the fair between East and West. Now its halls stay open all year, and private firms sign their own contracts.
The master's certificate, the journeyman's years, the chamber's seal: a craft education again worth its name.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Republic of Craftsmen": Consumer goods -4 %, Civilian industry tax +7 %, Civilian factory productivity +3 %, Workforce +2 %, Stability -2 %
Programme "The Craftsmen's Charter": Civilian factory output +2 %
foci.d: Half the republic's workers are employed by firms of fewer than five hundred people - the most Western economy east of the Elbe.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "Free Enterprise" (no PP).

e: The Planned Economy: Infrastructure construction +3 %, Workforce +2 %
foci.d: The craftsmen's cooperatives, forced on the trades since 1958, become voluntary: whoever wants to work alone may.

e: Union of Crafts and Trade popularity +2 %
foci.d: The private baker, butcher and repair shop return to every street - the end of the queue and of goods sold under the counter.
Reimar Gilsenbach and the nature circles of the Kulturbund govern the smog republic - an alt-hist green government long before any in the West.
The Council of Ministers wanted to make every figure on air and water a state secret. The Green League prints them in every newspaper.
foci.o: Historically the environmental data were classified in November 1982. Choice hub: who carries the movement.

e: The Party State: Foreign influence defence -3 %
foci.d: In the cellar of the Zion Church, historically from 1986, independent groups print what nobody else may - the government lets them grow into the movement that carries it. Western television reports every word.
foci.o: Independent and credible; the republic opens itself to Western media (foreign influence defence).

foci.n: The Society for Nature and Environment
foci.d: The Kulturbund's own Society for Nature and Environment (historically founded 1980) organises the clean-up Saturdays: orderly, under party guidance - and without the angry young people from the church cellars.
foci.o: Order and the apparatus's goodwill; the activists turn away from the League (popularity).

foci.n: Clean the Elbe and the Saale
e: The Planned Economy: agriculture_district_income_tax_modifier +3 %, Health costs -8 %
Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): A joint Elbe commission: Hamburg pays part of the sewage plants upstream; if Bonn accepts: income +0.5 % of GDP and Inner-German course +0.05 for us
foci.d: Leuna and Buna drain into the Saale, the pulp mills into the Elbe; the fish are dying as far as Hamburg. Sewage plants for the chemical belt.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Ecology Against Lignite": Health costs -5 %, Monthly population +0.02, Energy use -3 %, Energy production -5 %
foci.d: Two hundred and fifty million tonnes of lignite a year, villages swallowed by the pits, sulphur over every town: the League counts what King Lignite really costs and rewrites the economic line - less power, more life.
foci.o: The League's economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: less energy production. Choice hub: what replaces coal.

e: The Planned Economy: Nuclear energy output +2 %, Health costs -5 %, Sanction resistance (Imperia) -5 %
foci.d: Soviet pressurised-water reactors replace the dirtiest pits: clean air - and a new dependence on Moscow's fuel.
foci.o: Clean power from Soviet fuel (sanction resistance falls). The review layer adds Green League -2 % and Protestant Church -5.

e: Builds 1 renewable energy plant (paid: 0.91 % of GDP)
The Planned Economy: Energy use -4 %, Renewable energy output +7 %, Factory efficiency growth -2 %
foci.d: No new pits and no reactors: save energy, burn less, build wind and water power - and accept colder winters and slower factories.
foci.o: Price: slower factories (efficiency growth).

e: The Planned Economy: Nuclear reactor construction +10 %
foci.d: The Bruno Leuschner plant at Lubmin grows block by block, Stendal is begun early: half the republic's electricity without smoke.

e: The Planned Economy: Energy use -2 %, Infrastructure construction +3 %
foci.d: Insulated prefabricated blocks, district heat from the power stations, wind turbines on Rügen and a Trabant that burns less.

e: Ends King Lignite in every form
The Economic Line becomes "The Green Economy": Health costs -8 %, Monthly population +0.03, Energy use -3 %, Civilian factory productivity +2 %, Energy production -8 %
foci.d: The last open-cast mines close, the briquette factories fall silent, and Leipzig sees a blue sky in winter.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "Ecology Against Lignite" (no PP). Ladder owner is the economy agent; this capstone only ends it. With King Lignite its energy bonus goes too. If the economy ladder has already turned it into "Coal Instead of Oil", that successor idea is removed instead.

e: Offer to CZE (they decide; no advance reward): A Clean Air Treaty for the Ore Mountains: both sides fit desulphurisation to their border power stations; if Prague accepts: stability +2 % and agricultural productivity +2 % for both
foci.d: Sulphur from the power stations of Saxony and Bohemia kills the spruce of the Erzgebirge. The League replants and asks Prague for filters.
Bitterfeld, Wolfen and the poisoned Silver Lake: the chemical triangle gets filters, treatment plants and a budget.
foci.o: Choice hub: who pays for the clean-up.

foci.d: Every tonne of sulphur and every litre of phenol in the river now costs the polluting Kombinat a fine.

e: The Planned Economy: Health costs -10 %, Civilian factory productivity +2 %
foci.d: The clean-up comes out of the state budget: no fines, no quarrel with the Kombinate - just less money for everything else.
Ernst Goldenbaum has led the Farmers' Party since 1948. Freed from the bloc, it speaks for the villages that feed the republic.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Cooperative Farms": agriculture_district_income_tax_modifier +5 %, production_speed_agriculture_district_factor +8 %, Consumer goods -2 %, Civilian factory output -2 %
foci.d: The cooperative members elect their chairmen again - not the district party secretary - and the farmers' party writes the village into the economic line.
foci.o: The farmers' economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: investment goes to the villages, not the factories. Choice hub: the future of the land.

e: Adds "Cooperative Socialism": Agricultural productivity +3 %, Stability +2 %, Bureaucracy costs +3 %
foci.d: The LPG stays - but as a true cooperative: the members own it, elect it and share its profit.
foci.o: The cooperatives stay - with their boards and accountants (bureaucracy costs).

e: Adds "The Family Farm": Agricultural productivity +6 %, Agriculture tax -5 %
foci.d: The land reform of 1945 gave the land to the farmers, collectivisation took it back. Whoever wants may leave the LPG with his fields.
foci.o: Alt-hist: decollectivisation as in Poland, where most land stayed private. Price: lower agriculture tax, Moscow's Trust.

e: The Economic Line becomes "A Republic of Villages": agriculture_district_income_tax_modifier +7 %, production_speed_agriculture_district_factor +8 %, Sanction resistance (Imperia) +10 %, Consumer goods -3 %, Civilian factory output -3 %
foci.d: Bread, milk and meat from the republic's own fields: the farmers' state feeds itself and no longer depends on grain ships.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "Cooperative Farms" (no PP).

foci.d: The planners want to split every village into a crop cooperative and a livestock cooperative. The farmers' government stops it: fields and stables stay together.
foci.o: Historically the separation of crop and livestock production was pushed through in the 1970s and cost the LPGs dearly.

e: The Planned Economy: Sanction resistance (Imperia) +5 %, Agriculture tax +5 %
foci.d: Every tonne of grain bought from Canada or the Soviet Union costs hard currency or loyalty. New fields, new silos, new seed.
foci.o: Choice hub: where the meat goes.

foci.d: Pork and beef go to West Berlin and the Soviet Union for hard currency; at home the queues at the butcher grow.

e: The Planned Economy: Consumer goods -3 %, Agriculture tax -3 %
foci.d: Every pig stays in the republic: sausage on every table - and no hard currency in the till.
Roads, schools, doctors and a culture house for every village: the young no longer have to leave for the cities.
The combine harvesters from Singwitz and the tractors from Schönebeck go to the cooperatives first, not to export.

e: Offer to CAN, USA (they decide; no advance reward): A five-year grain supply contract at world-market prices; if accepted: stability +2 % and agricultural productivity +3 % for us, trade opinion +5 % for them
foci.d: A long-term contract with the prairie farmers: grain at world prices, delivered every autumn, whatever the harvest at home.
foci.o: Buying from the class enemy: Moscow's Trust falls a little.

e: Programme "The Special German Road": Civilian factory output +2 %, Non-aligned drift +0.03
foci.d: In 1956 Wolfgang Harich wrote a programme for a special German road to socialism and got ten years in prison for it. Now he governs.
Walter Janka, Gustav Just and the other comrades of Harich's circle are freed of their convictions and return to their posts.

e: The Party State: Bureaucracy costs -7 %, Corruption costs -5 %
foci.d: Khrushchev's secret speech was read in Berlin in 1956 and then filed away. The Third Way finishes it: no cult, no purges, no leader for life.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Neutral Trading State": Trade opinion +5 %, Sanction resistance (Imperia) +5 %, Civilian factory productivity +3 %, Research sharing -3 %

Offer to SER (they decide; no advance reward): A partnership of two socialist states outside the blocs: advisers on self-management and preferential trade; if Belgrade accepts: trade opinion +5 % and research +2 % for both
foci.d: Belgrade has run its factories through workers' councils since 1950 and trades with both blocs while belonging to neither. The Third Way asks Tito's men to teach - and rewrites the economic line on their model.
foci.o: The Third Way's economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: Comecon's research programmes close their doors (research sharing).

e: Adds "Council Democracy": Stability +3 %, Workforce +2 %, Bureaucracy costs +10 %
foci.d: Power to the councils: every factory, district and university elects its council, and the councils elect the republic.
foci.o: Every council needs its secretaries (bureaucracy costs); the old apparatus is dissolved.

e: Adds "Parliamentary Socialism": Stability +4 %, Monthly population +0.02, Political power gain -10 %
foci.d: Socialism by the ballot: several socialist parties compete in free elections, and the Volkskammer becomes a real parliament.
foci.o: The government must now win majorities (political power gain -10 %); Moscow distrusts free elections.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian factory productivity +3 %, Workforce +2 %
foci.d: The general director answers to the elected council of his workers - Belgrade's model in Leuna and Eisenhüttenstadt.
Every party, union and university may publish its own paper. Socialism has to win the argument now.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Third Way Economy": Trade opinion +5 %, Sanction resistance (Imperia) +8 %, Civilian factory productivity +5 %, Workforce +2 %, Research sharing -3 %
Programme "The Special German Road": Civilian factory output +3 %
foci.d: Neither Stalin's state nor Bonn's market: a democratic, neutral socialism that trades with everyone and that the rest of Europe watches with astonishment.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "The Neutral Trading State" (no PP).

foci.d: Harich's plan of 1956 was a reunification negotiated with the SPD. The Third Way government sends its envoys to Bonn.
foci.o: Choice hub: the form of the German offer.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): A treaty of neutrality: both German states leave NATO and the Warsaw Pact, foreign troops leave, a joint commission prepares all-German elections; if Bonn accepts: Inner-German course +0.30 and tension -3 for us

Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): The Group of Soviet Forces in Germany withdraws in step with the Western armies; if Moscow accepts: "The Group of Soviet Forces in Germany" is removed and tension -2
Programme "The Special German Road": Non-aligned drift +0.03
The Party State: Foreign influence defence -5 %
foci.d: Austria bought its freedom in 1955 with neutrality. Both German states leave their blocs, and the foreign armies go home.
foci.o: Garrison ladder belongs to the foreign agent: this path only asks Moscow (offer). Own side: hope at home (stability), the blocs' agents move in (foreign influence defence), Moscow's Trust.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): A confederation of the two German states with a joint council, free movement and a common market; if Bonn accepts: Inner-German course +0.20 and trade opinion +10 % for us
foci.d: Two states, one confederation: a joint council, free movement and a common market - each keeps its own social order.
foci.o: Own side: inner-German trade grows at once (trade opinion, income); Moscow's Trust falls.

foci.a: `neutrality_neutral_communism_are_in_power`; a border regime spirit is active (any step of the border ladder)
e: Ends The border regime in every form
foci.d: A socialism that must wall in its people has already lost. The Third Way opens the crossings and bets that people will stay.
foci.o: Western/Non-Aligned trees may remove the rampart. If the border section has swapped it ("The Perfected Border" / "The Iron Border"), the current version is removed. Visitors bring D-Mark; the first months are chaotic (stability).

e: Programme "Dialectics without Dogma": Civilian factory productivity +2 %
foci.d: Robert Havemann - antifascist, chemist, expelled from the party in 1964 for his lectures 'Dialectics without Dogma' - leads Prague's spring in Berlin, two years late.
The Press Office closes; every newspaper, Neues Deutschland included, prints what its editors decide.
Banned from every stage since 1965, Wolf Biermann plays the Friedrichstadt-Palast - live on television.
foci.o: Choice hub: what becomes of the Stasi.

foci.n: Dissolve the Ministry for State Security
e: Police spending is cut one step
foci.d: Forty-three thousand officers go home, the files are opened, the informers lose their power.
The Ministry stays, but a Volkskammer committee reads its files, and decomposition is forbidden by law.
foci.o: The officers keep their jobs but lose their methods (MfS opinion).

foci.d: Bautzen and Hohenschönhausen open their gates: dissidents and those jailed for trying to flee the republic walk free.
Like Prague's Action Programme of April 1968: freedom of assembly, rehabilitations, economic reform - adopted by the Central Committee in one night.
foci.o: Hub of the political fork: Kádár's way or Dubček's.

foci.d: Kádár's lesson from Budapest: reform at home, loyalty abroad, and never a word about leaving the Warsaw Pact.
foci.o: Moscow's goodwill and the camp's science; the reformers who wanted more are disappointed (popularity).

e: Event: Warsaw Pact Manoeuvres on the Border (30 days later): Soviet, Polish and Czechoslovak divisions exercise along our borders. Concede (Moscow's Trust +10, stability -5 %) or stand firm (war support +5 %, tension +3; if Moscow's Trust is below 20 the Soviet Union receives the decision "Fraternal Assistance" - its own choice)
foci.d: Dubček's road to its end: several parties, free unions, a free press - and the risk of Soviet tanks on Unter den Linden.
foci.o: The Dubček risk: the event is the price, Moscow decides itself whether to act.

e: Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): The republic stays in the Warsaw Pact and Comecon, Moscow tolerates the internal reforms; if Moscow accepts: Moscow's Trust +10 for us
foci.d: A pledge to Brezhnev: the republic stays in the Pact and in Comecon, and Moscow tolerates what happens inside it.
For the first time since 1946 the people choose between parties, not between yes and no to a single list.

e: The National People's Army: Defence on core territory +5 %, Recruitable population +2 %
Offer to SER, ROM (they decide; no advance reward): Belgrade and Bucharest publicly guarantee the Berlin Spring; if they accept: opinion +25 on both sides and tension +1
foci.d: The factory combat groups swear to defend the reforms, and Belgrade and Bucharest - who condemned the invasion of 1968 - are asked to stand by Berlin.
The FDGB elects its own leaders and may strike - free unions in the East, ten years before Gdańsk.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Enterprises Without Masters": Civilian factory productivity +5 %, Workforce +2 %, Civilian industry tax +2 %, Stability -2 %
foci.d: Prague's Ota Šik and Budapest's reformers agree on one thing: the enterprise, not the ministry, must decide. The League writes self-management into the economic line - prices that tell the truth, profit as the measure.
foci.o: The League's economic identity (Economic Line). Price inside the idea: the reform unsettles (stability). Choice hub: who runs the enterprise.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian factory productivity +2 %, Workforce +2 %
foci.d: Every enterprise elects a workers' council that hires the director and divides the profit - Havemann's 'socialism with freedom' in the factory.
foci.o: The workers decide; the Kombinat directors lose their power (faction).

e: The Planned Economy: Consumer goods -3 %, Civilian industry tax +3 %
foci.d: Hungarian style: more consumer goods, private plots and small shops, a refrigerator in every flat - and nobody asks about politics.
foci.o: Market socialism: full shelves and taxes; Moscow distrusts the market (trust).

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Self-Managed Republic": Civilian factory productivity +7 %, Workforce +3 %, Civilian industry tax +3 %, Monthly population +0.02, Stability -2 %
foci.d: Ten years after the Berlin Spring the enterprises belong to those who work in them, and the plan is a contract between free producers - the socialism Havemann lectured about in 1963.
foci.o: Capstone: upgrades "Enterprises Without Masters" (no PP).

e: Programme "The Legacy of Ernst Thälmann": Military factory productivity +2 %
