foci.d: Alt-history: the Dresden district secretary who backed Robotron and the microelectronics centre.

foci.a: `emerging_communist_state_are_in_power`; Günter Mittag is First Secretary (`COLDWAR_DDR_first_sec_mit`); Egon Krenz is alive and not First Secretary; date from 22.05.1976
e: Designated heir: Egon Krenz takes over on death or retirement
foci.d: The FDJ generation: a safe pair of hands for the apparatus - and for Moscow.

e: Programme "The Guardian of Doctrine": Ideological defence (Cold War) +5 %, Stability from party popularity +3 %
Our leader gains the trait "Keeper of the Doctrine"
foci.d: Kurt Hager: Spain veteran, professor, the Politburo's guardian of science, culture and doctrine since 1963. Under him the party line becomes the republic's whole horizon.
foci.o: Alt-hist leader (candidacy in the Central Committee).

e: Programme "The Guardian of Doctrine": Factory efficiency growth +3 %
foci.d: Otto Reinhold, rector of the party's academy, writes the theory: the GDR exists only as a socialist state - a capitalist GDR would have no reason to exist. His economists plan accordingly, and the last private workshops have no place in it.

e: Adds "Ragwitz's Index" for 730 days: Stability from party popularity +3 %, Western drift -0.02, Research speed -2 %
foci.d: Ursula Ragwitz, head of the Central Committee's culture department, reads every manuscript and every stage play before the public does. The young stop reading.

e: The Party State: Stability from party popularity +5 %
foci.d: Joachim Herrmann, editor of Neues Deutschland and later secretary for agitation, decides each night which photograph of the leadership opens the front page. The workers read the sports page.

e: Adds "Demarcation to the Maximum" for 1095 days: Western drift -0.02, Ideological defence (Cold War) +5 %, Trade opinion -5 %
foci.d: Marxism-Leninism as taught in Moscow, without Prague's human face or Belgrade's self-management - and demarcation pushed as far as it will go: 'German' vanishes from institutions' names, Western guests from conferences.
foci.o: Takes over "Demarcation to the Maximum". Hub of the doctrine column and of the economic doctrine.

foci.a: `emerging_communist_state_are_in_power`; Kurt Hager is First Secretary (`COLDWAR_DDR_first_sec_hag`); date from 11.03.1985
e: Adds "No New Wallpaper" for 1095 days: Western drift -0.03, Stability +2 %, Research sharing -5 %
Programme "The Guardian of Doctrine": Stability from party popularity +5 %
foci.d: April 1987, to the magazine Stern: 'If your neighbour puts up new wallpaper, would you feel obliged to repaper your flat too?' Perestroika stops at the Oder - and so does Soviet goodwill.
foci.o: The one step Gorbachev's Moscow resents.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Socialist Thrift": Consumer goods -3 %, Interest rates -5 %, Sanction resistance (Imperia) +5 %, Stability -3 %, Trade opinion -5 %
foci.d: Hager's economics: the needs of socialist man are shaped by socialism, not by the West German shop window. Thrift is a virtue, imports are a weakness, and a republic without debts is a free republic.
foci.o: Doctrine entry: replaces whichever economic line is active.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Party Asceticism": Consumer goods -4 %, Corruption costs -5 %, Bureaucracy costs -5 %, Sanction resistance (Imperia) +5 %, Stability -2 %
foci.d: Alt-history: Wandlitz and the special shops for functionaries are closed - the party lives like the workers, and the money saved goes back into the plan. The Nomenklatura is furious; the FDGB is delighted.
foci.o: Model fork A1: a cheap state and a clean party; price: SED Nomenklatura -10, stability -2 % in the doctrine.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Mass Initiative": Workforce +3 %, Civilian factory productivity +3 %, Consumer goods -2 %, Stability -3 %
foci.d: Socialist competition in every works and the 'Make our towns and villages more beautiful - join in!' campaign in every street: brigades, banners and Saturday shifts build playgrounds, clubhouses and new roads. More output for the same wages - the red pennant hangs over the lathe, the overtime goes unpaid.
foci.o: Model fork A2 (historical): workforce and output; price: stability -3 % in the doctrine, FDGB -5.

e: The Planned Economy: Max factory efficiency +3 %
foci.d: The Academy of Sciences, the universities and the research institutes plan their work with the party - and from 1976 the Academy of Social Sciences at the Central Committee defines what Marxism-Leninism means in practice. What is researched is decided by its use to socialism.
foci.o: Flagship project (takes over "The Academy of Social Sciences" and "The Scientific Worldview").

foci.a: `emerging_communist_state_are_in_power`; Kurt Hager is First Secretary (`COLDWAR_DDR_first_sec_hag`); date from 01.01.1977
e: Programme "The Guardian of Doctrine": Economic cycle law costs -1 %
foci.d: 1977: world coffee prices explode. The 'Kaffee-Mix' - half coffee, half roasted rye and chicory - saves 300 million valuta marks. The people call it 'Erich's Krönung' and grumble loudly.
foci.o: Short/long fork B1: hard currency and solvency; price: stability -2 %, FDGB -5.

foci.a: `emerging_communist_state_are_in_power`; Kurt Hager is First Secretary (`COLDWAR_DDR_first_sec_hag`); date from 01.01.1977
e: The Socialist Camp: Assistance effectiveness (Cold War) +3 %
foci.d: Trucks, machines and advisers for Ethiopian and Vietnamese coffee - solidarity that fills the cups. The bill is paid in IFA trucks the republic would rather have kept.
foci.o: Short/long fork B2: calm and solidarity, Moscow likes it; price: 0.3 % of GDP.

e: Programme "The Guardian of Doctrine": Interest rates -5 %, Sanction resistance (Imperia) +5 %, Civilian factory output +2 %
foci.d: Alt-history: Hager's republic pays back the West German and Swiss banks and lives on what it makes. No new credits, no new dependence - and a lot less trade.
foci.o: Capstone of the doctrine branch. Price: trade opinion -5 %.

foci.d: Printing licences, paper quotas, the publishing office in the Ministry of Culture - and the MfS's Department M opens the letters: whoever writes, paints or sings in the republic does so by permission.

e: Adds "A Little Freedom" for 365 days: Stability +4 %, Foreign influence defence -5 %, Monthly population +0.02
foci.d: Hager lets the artists breathe: Christa Wolf, Heiner Müller and Volker Braun publish with cuts but publish; the rock bands play; the church youth meets. Loyalty is bought with a little freedom - and the West listens in.
foci.o: Soft line: stability, popularity, the church; price: foreign influence defence -5 % for a year, Moscow's Trust -3.

e: Adds "The Frost" for 365 days: Stability -4 %, Foreign influence defence +5 %, Western drift -0.02, Police costs +5 %
foci.d: As after the Eleventh Plenum of 1965: banned films, pulped books, expelled writers. In 1979 the Writers' Union expels nine members; the rest learn silence.
foci.o: Hard line (historical; takes over "The Writers' Union Congress"): security, the MfS and Moscow pleased; price: stability -4 % and police costs +5 % for a year.

foci.d: The ideologist wants an heir who will keep the doctrine pure - and whom Moscow will trust with it.

foci.a: `emerging_communist_state_are_in_power`; Kurt Hager is First Secretary (`COLDWAR_DDR_first_sec_hag`); Werner Krolikowski is alive and not First Secretary; date from 19.06.1971
e: Designated heir: Werner Krolikowski takes over on death or retirement
Programme "The Guardian of Doctrine": Fuel gain +3 %
foci.d: Moscow's man in the Politburo: orthodox, loyal, and in daily contact with the Soviet embassy.

foci.a: `emerging_communist_state_are_in_power`; Kurt Hager is First Secretary (`COLDWAR_DDR_first_sec_hag`); Egon Krenz is alive and not First Secretary; date from 22.05.1976
e: Designated heir: Egon Krenz takes over on death or retirement
foci.d: The FDJ generation, raised on the doctrine Hager wrote.

e: Adds "The Ideological Fortress": Western drift -0.03, Ideological defence (Cold War) +5 %, Stability from party popularity +5 %, Research speed -3 %
foci.d: Hager's republic: a fortress of doctrine where every school, stage and institute speaks with one voice - secure against the West, loyal to Moscow, and slowly suffocating.
foci.o: Capstone: needs the culture fork and the doctrine branch. Research pays for the purity.

e: Programme "Hoffmann's Defence Republic": Political power gain +3 %, Recruitable population +2 %
Our leader gains the trait "Army General"
foci.d: Heinz Hoffmann fought in Spain, trained in Moscow and has run the Ministry of National Defence in Strausberg since 1960. Now the general sits at the head of the party.
foci.o: Alt-history: Hoffmann (Politburo from 1973) never led the party. Historical death 2 December 1985 (concept event).

foci.d: Colonel General Heinz Keßler, Chief of the Main Staff since 1967, turns the general's orders into plans for six divisions - and the Central Committee's apparatus learns that Strausberg no longer asks it first.

e: The National People's Army: Mobilisation speed +5 %
foci.d: Fritz Streletz, secretary of the National Defence Council from 1971, ties party, army, Stasi and economy into one chain of command. Every Kombinat gets a mobilisation plan - and a new set of orders from the barracks.

e: The Party State: Ideological defence (Cold War) +5 %
The National People's Army: Army morale +3 %
foci.d: Admiral Waldemar Verner's Political Main Administration puts a party secretary beside every commander: an army that thinks right fights right. The commanders call it supervision.

e: The National People's Army: Recruitable population +2 %, Training time -5 %
foci.d: Eighteen months of service for every young man: the NVA is to teach discipline, technology and class consciousness to a whole generation.
foci.o: Hub: defence lessons, or the army fork (The Garrison State / The Professional Army).

foci.b: `has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_kg_military_education_in_schools` (military education in schools - no double reward)
e: The National People's Army: Recruitable population +2 %
The Party State: Ideological defence (Cold War) +3 %
foci.d: Military instruction becomes a school subject for ninth and tenth graders, as it did in September 1978. The Protestant churches protest; the ministry insists.

foci.b: `has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_kg_pre_military_training` (GST pre-military training - no double reward)
foci.d: The GST trains half a million young people in shooting, gliding, diving and radio - pre-military training dressed up as a hobby.

e: Programme "Hoffmann's Defence Republic": Recruitable population +2 %, Military factory construction +10 %, Consumer goods +3 %
foci.d: Everything for defence: a nation in arms with reserve divisions in every district, more arms plants, more exercises - and fewer cars, fridges and oranges in the shops. Moscow counts the divisions and is pleased.
foci.o: Mass: recruitable population, arms plants and Moscow's favour; price consumer goods +3 % on the programme.

e: The National People's Army: Equipment costs -5 %
foci.d: Strausberg gets what it asks for: new arms plants, depots for thirty days of war, hardened command posts and a country that lives on permanent alert.

e: Programme "Hoffmann's Defence Republic": Army personnel costs -10 %
foci.d: Fewer divisions, better soldiers: long-serving NCOs, modern equipment, and the conscripts back in the factories where the plan needs them. Moscow counts divisions and is not pleased.
foci.o: Quality: cheaper soldiers and workers for the plan; price Moscow's Trust -3.

foci.d: Every NVA general passes through the Frunze and Voroshilov academies in Moscow: the best-trained officer corps of the Pact after the Soviets.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Defence Economy": Military factory productivity +5 %, Military factory construction +5 %, Civilian-to-military conversion cost -10 %, Consumer goods +3 %, Civilian factory productivity -2 %
foci.d: The general's economics: the NVA is the plan's first customer, the shops its second. Arms plants get their steel before the furniture Kombinate do.
foci.o: Doctrine entry E: replaces whichever Economic Line is active.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Arms for Hard Currency": Military industry tax +5 %, Arms market income +10 %, Military factory productivity +5 %, Consumer goods +3 %, World-market exposure (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: The state arms exporter ITA sells rifles from the Erzgebirge, ammunition and W50 trucks to Syria, Ethiopia, Mozambique and Nicaragua - partly for hard currency, partly for coffee and goodwill.
foci.o: Hard currency and arms income; price consumer goods +3 %, world-market exposure, Cold War tension +1.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Arsenal of the NVA": Equipment costs -5 %, Licence production speed +10 %, Military factory productivity +3 %, Consumer goods +4 %, Civilian factory construction -5 %
foci.d: Soviet licences go to the republic's own works - Kalashnikovs from Wiesa, ammunition from Schönebeck, W50 trucks from Ludwigsfelde - and everything they make stays with the NVA. Moscow likes an ally that equips itself.
foci.o: Cheap equipment, Moscow pleased; price consumer goods +4 %, civilian factory construction -5 %.

foci.d: The Ernst Thälmann works in Suhl and their sister plants turn out small arms, ammunition and spare parts for the NVA and for export.
foci.o: Flagship project P of the doctrine.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian factory construction +5 %
foci.d: Whole NVA units are lent to the lignite pits, the harvest and the building sites; in the winter of 1978/79 the army digs out the frozen coal trains. The officers grumble that soldiers are not labourers.
foci.o: Labour and construction now; price NVA Command -5.

foci.d: Hoffmann holds the Pact's standard: 85 per cent of the NVA ready for combat at all times. No soldier in the coal pits - and the plan misses the hands.
foci.o: Readiness; price workforce -2 %.

e: Programme "Hoffmann's Defence Republic": Military factory productivity +5 %, Military industry tax +3 %
foci.d: The Ministry of National Defence becomes the plan's most demanding customer: trucks from Ludwigsfelde, warships from Wolgast, rifles from Suhl - and an arms industry that pays its own way.
foci.o: Doctrine capstone C.

e: Our leader gains the trait "Marshal of the GDR"
foci.d: In March 1982 the Volkskammer created the rank of Marshal of the GDR and never awarded it. Alt-history: the general takes the baton - and must now name who comes after him.
foci.o: Succession hub: needs the army fork, the GST column and the doctrine's flagship.

e: Event: At Hoffmann's death the Central Committee is asked to elect Heinz Keßler; if it refuses, the Military Council of the NVA under Keßler may take power ("The Generals Step In" opens without its opinion condition)
If the Central Committee refuses Keßler after Hoffmann's death, the Military Council of the NVA (party 22) may claim power: "The Generals Step In" accepts this flag instead of NVA Command opinion 75
Military Council of the NVA popularity +3 %
foci.d: Heinz Keßler, an officer of the NVA since its founding in 1956, is to follow the general. If the Central Committee balks, the Military Council of the NVA stands ready.
foci.o: Keßler (1920-2017) was Minister of National Defence 1985-89 after Hoffmann's death; he also leads the junta party 22.

e: Designated heir: Egon Krenz takes over on death or retirement
foci.d: Egon Krenz, the FDJ man, is to inherit: the army keeps its budget, the party keeps its leading role.

e: Adds "The Armed Republic": War support +5 %, Army morale +5 %, Military programme costs (Cold War) -15 %, Consumer goods +2 %
foci.d: The best-armed state per head in the Warsaw Pact: respected in Moscow, feared in Bonn - and tired at home.
foci.o: Capstone. Consumer goods +2 % is the price of the armed republic.

e: Programme "Lamberz's Modern Socialism": Political power gain +3 %, Monthly population +0.02
foci.d: Werner Lamberz, born 1929, the youngest man in the Politburo and the party's best speaker, now leads it: a socialism that smiles on television.
foci.o: Alt-history. His candidacy (cc_lam) sets COLDWAR_DDR_lamberz_stays_in_berlin: the Libyan helicopter crash of 6 March 1978 does not happen.

e: The Party State: Ideological defence (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: Heinz Adameck has run East German television since 1954; with Lamberz's backing the DFF is to win back the evening from ARD and ZDF - with new studios and colour programmes the budget can barely carry.

e: Our influence in SYE, ETH, ANG +2 %
foci.d: Paul Markowski's department for international relations knows every liberation movement from Luanda to Aden - and travels wherever Lamberz goes. Washington notices where the GDR's friends are.
Joachim Herrmann, editor of Neues Deutschland since 1971, is told to make the party paper readable: fewer congratulatory telegrams, more news. The district secretaries miss their names on page one.

e: Our leader gains the trait "The GDR's Kennedy"
foci.d: Western journalists call him the GDR's Kennedy: tall, witty, at ease with steelworkers and foreign presidents alike. The party finally has a face people want to see - and trade partners want to meet.
Ein Kessel Buntes brings Western stars and Eastern hits to the DFF from 1972. If the people watch our channel on Saturday, they watch our news on Sunday. The Western stars are paid in hard currency.
December 1971: 'no taboos' for artists who stand firmly on socialism. How far that breadth may reach is now Lamberz's decision.
foci.o: Hub of the media fork: Reform from the Top (opening) or Modern Orthodoxy (control).

e: Press law: one step less censorship
Programme "Lamberz's Modern Socialism": Civilian factory productivity +3 %
foci.d: The First Secretary himself opens the windows: honest statistics, live phone-ins, readers' letters printed uncut, a government spokesman who answers questions and factory managers who may contradict. Moscow raises an eyebrow.
foci.o: Opening: stability, popularity and honest numbers; price Moscow's Trust -3 and a drift to Rapprochement. Absorbs the former 'The Open Microphone'.

e: The Party State: Ideological defence (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: The message stays the same; only the packaging changes - new studios in Adlershof, a younger Aktuelle Kamera, slick posters for the old certainties. Moscow approves; the young switch over to the West after the news.
foci.o: Control: ideological defence and Moscow's favour; price SED popularity -2 %. Absorbs the former 'Agitation in Colour'.

e: Adds "The Africa Commission": Assistance capacity (Cold War) +1, Military programme costs (Cold War) -10 %
foci.d: Lamberz chairs a Politburo commission for Africa: advisers, trucks, printing presses and security instructors for the new socialist states.
foci.o: Hub of the Africa fork (Ethiopia or Mozambique). Capacity +1 sits in an idea.

foci.a: `emerging_communist_state_are_in_power`; Werner Lamberz is First Secretary (`COLDWAR_DDR_first_sec_lam`); Ethiopia exists and is governed by an Emerging party (the Derg from September 1974)
foci.b: `has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_sol_the_ethiopian_revolution` (the Ethiopian commitment - no double reward)
e: Offer to ETH (they decide; no advance reward): Treaty of friendship: GDR security advisers and IFA trucks for Ethiopia. If Ethiopia accepts: it gains a timed idea (army organisation +3 %, police costs -10 %); we get Ethiopian coffee at friendship prices (timed idea: consumer goods -2 %, stability +2 %) and our opinion +15
The Socialist Camp: Assistance effectiveness (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: Mengistu's Derg turns to the socialist camp. Lamberz flies to Addis Ababa himself: security advisers and IFA trucks for a country at war in the Ogaden, coffee for the GDR.
foci.o: The 1977 coffee crisis was eased by bartering East German weapons for Ethiopian coffee. Security partner; price Cold War tension +1.

foci.a: `emerging_communist_state_are_in_power`; Werner Lamberz is First Secretary (`COLDWAR_DDR_first_sec_lam`); Mozambique exists (independent from 25 June 1975)
foci.b: `has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_sol_frelimos_mozambique` (the Mozambican commitment - no double reward)
e: Offer to MOZ (they decide; no advance reward): Treaty of friendship: GDR engineers for the Moatize coal mines and teachers for FRELIMO schools. If Mozambique accepts: it gains a timed idea (education costs -10 %, resource gain +5 %); we get contract workers (timed idea: workforce +2 %) and our opinion +15
foci.d: FRELIMO's Mozambique needs engineers, teachers and miners; the GDR needs workers and hard coal. A treaty would bring Mozambican contract workers to Saxony - and the engineers for Moatize are paid from Berlin.
foci.o: Trade partner; price 0.3 % of GDP for the engineers.

e: Our influence in ANG, ETH, MOZ +2 %
foci.d: FDJ Friendship Brigades of young engineers, nurses and teachers go south. This time Lamberz flies home from his African journeys - no helicopter waits for him in the Libyan desert.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Modern Consumer Socialism": Consumer goods -3 %, Stability +2 %, Trade opinion +5 %, Interest rates +5 %, World-market exposure (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: Lamberz the agitator knows that a full shop window convinces better than a banner: colour television, rock records and oranges sell socialism - if the republic can pay for them.
foci.o: Doctrine entry E: replaces whichever Economic Line is active.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Oil for Trucks": Fuel gain +10 %, Resource export revenue +5 %, Trade opinion +3 %, World-market exposure (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: 1977-78: IFA trucks, cement works and engineers for Iraqi and Libyan crude outside the Soviet quota - the deals Lamberz was flying to Tripoli to close in March 1978. Moscow dislikes oil it does not deliver itself.
foci.o: Fuel and export income; price Moscow's Trust -2 and world-market exposure.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Goods from the Tropics": Consumer goods -4 %, Stability +2 %, Civilian industry tax -3 %
The Socialist Camp: Assistance effectiveness (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: Barter instead of hard currency: Ethiopian and Angolan coffee, Ghanaian cocoa and Cuban oranges for IFA trucks, teachers and printing presses. The shelves fill; the factories that build the trucks earn nothing.
foci.o: Full shelves and solidarity; price civilian industry tax -3 % and 0.3 % of GDP.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian factory productivity +3 %
foci.d: The DFF has broadcast in colour since 1969, but a colour set from Staßfurt costs half a year's wages. Lamberz wants one in every living room before the Western sets get there.
foci.o: Flagship project P of the doctrine (replaces the former 'Agitation in Colour').

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian industry tax +3 %
foci.d: Salamander shoes, Schiesser underwear and Nivea cream are made in GDR factories under Western licence - most of it for the West, some for the Exquisit shops. Money now, and a dependence Moscow notes.
foci.o: Short term: hard currency now; price Moscow's Trust -3 and a drift to Rapprochement.

e: Programme "Lamberz's Modern Socialism": Civilian factory productivity +3 %
The Planned Economy: Civilian factory output +3 %
foci.d: Every Kombinat, even in steel and chemicals, must make consumer goods: saucepans from the rolling mill, tents from the fibre works. The general directors call it a waste of their plants.
foci.o: Long term: own production; price Kombinat Directors -5.

e: Programme "Lamberz's Modern Socialism": Trade opinion +5 %, Civilian industry tax +3 %
foci.d: Leipzig's fair, Berlin's Alexanderplatz and the department stores of every district town become the republic's shop window - for its own citizens first.
foci.o: Doctrine capstone C.

e: The Party State: Ideological defence (Cold War) +3 %
foci.d: Lamberz is barely fifty, but he knows how quickly a Politburo ages. The next leader must come from his own generation - and know how to talk to the cameras.
foci.o: Succession hub: needs the media fork, the Saturday evening and the Africa fork.

e: Designated heir: Hans Modrow takes over on death or retirement
foci.d: Hans Modrow, the modest district secretary of Dresden, shares Lamberz's taste for open debate - and the old guard's distrust of it.

foci.n: Pass the Torch to the FDJ
e: Designated heir: Egon Krenz takes over on death or retirement
foci.d: Egon Krenz, the FDJ chief, is young, disciplined and liked in Moscow - continuity with a younger face.

e: Adds "A Socialism Worth Living": Stability +3 %, Monthly population +0.03, Trade opinion +5 %, Social costs +5 %
foci.d: A republic whose young people watch its television, dance to its bands and believe its leader: the dream of 1971, almost within reach.
foci.o: Capstone. Higher social costs are the price of popularity.

e: Programme "Eternal Friendship with the Soviet Union": Political power gain +3 %, Sanction resistance (Imperia) +5 %
Our leader gains the trait "Moscow's Man"
foci.d: Werner Krolikowski, Dresden's party chief until 1973 and Politburo member since 1971, reports to the Soviet embassy behind his comrades' backs. Now the Kremlin's confidant runs the party.
foci.o: Alt-history. Krolikowski was First Deputy Chairman of the Council of Ministers 1976-88.

e: Programme "Eternal Friendship with the Soviet Union": Max factory efficiency +3 %
foci.d: Willi Stoph shares Krolikowski's contempt for Mittag's economic conjuring; together they run the government by the book - the Soviet book. Mielke's ministry is told to keep out of the ministries.

e: Shield and Sword: Intel network gain +10 %, Decryption +3.5 %
foci.d: Erich Mielke's ministry and the KGB in Karlshorst share files, informers and suspicions: the Stasi becomes Moscow's eyes in every office - including the offices of the comrades.

e: The Party State: Ideological defence (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: Every favour from Moscow is paid in national pride: Soviet slogans, Soviet holidays, Soviet orders. How far will the republic bend?
foci.o: Hub of the loyalty fork: The Loyal Satellite or the alt-history Closest Union.

e: Adds "The Loyal Satellite": Stability +3 %, Sanction resistance (Imperia) +5 %, Trade opinion -5 %
foci.d: The Soviet Union's most reliable ally: every Comecon vote, every manoeuvre, every line of Pravda followed to the letter. The republic keeps its own state - and loses its Western customers.
foci.o: Bend in everything, keep the state: stability and protection; price trade opinion -5 % in the idea.

e: Adds the Cold War idea "Soviet Advisers" for 365 days
The Planned Economy: Max factory efficiency +3 %
foci.d: Soviet specialists sit in the Planning Commission, the ministries and the Kombinate. Things work - in Russian. The general directors seethe.

e: Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): A confederation of the GDR with the Soviet Union: joint foreign and defence policy and a joint currency board for the transferable rouble; the GDR keeps its own government. If the Soviet Union accepts: Moscow's Trust +25 and the idea "The Union Treaty" for us (stability +5 %, political power +10 %, energy +10 %); if it declines: Moscow's Trust +5 for the gesture
The National People's Army: Equipment costs -5 %
foci.d: Alt-history: Krolikowski proposes what no German communist ever dared - a confederation of the GDR with the USSR. The Kremlin decides; the NVA's generals would serve under Soviet command.
foci.o: Player only. The Soviet player (or AI) decides in its own event; nothing is executed in the Soviet scope here. Bend all the way: Soviet equipment and the Chekists' favour; price NVA Command -10.

e: Adds "Russian as a State Language": Licence production speed +10 %, Ideological defence (Cold War) +5 %, Stability -3 %
foci.d: Russian becomes the second official language and Soviet officers sit in the Volkskammer as observers. Many East Germans quietly despair.
foci.o: Alt-history; continues whether or not Moscow accepted the confederation.

foci.d: Six million members, Russian lessons from the fifth grade, friendship trains to Moscow: the DSF becomes the republic's second party.
Every Politburo protocol reaches the Soviet ambassador before the ink is dry. Moscow is never surprised again - and the comrades never trust each other again.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Soviet Yardstick": Research sharing +5 %, Licence production speed +10 %, Energy use -3 %, Trade opinion -5 %, Civilian factory productivity -2 %
foci.d: Krolikowski despises Mittag's conjuring with numbers: plans are drawn up as Gosplan does - balanced in tonnes, checked in Moscow, fed by Druzhba oil at Comecon prices and closed to Western whims.
foci.o: Doctrine entry E: replaces whichever Economic Line is active. Absorbs the former 'Raw Materials at Friendship Prices'.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Specialisation by Gosplan": Civilian factory output +5 %, Dockyard output +5 %, Research sharing +5 %, Civilian factory productivity -3 %, Research speed -2 %
foci.d: Moscow decides who builds what: the republic gets ships, rail cars, machine tools and chemicals for the whole bloc - and hands its own car and computer ambitions to its neighbours.
foci.o: Capacity and the bloc's orders; price own productivity -3 % and research -2 %. Absorbs the former 'The Comecon Division of Labour'.

foci.n: No Debts to the Class Enemy
e: The Economic Line becomes "Out of the Western Debt": Interest rates -6 %, World-market exposure (Cold War) -10 %, Consumer goods +4 %, Stability -2 %
foci.d: Alt-history: what Krolikowski wrote to Moscow in secret from 1980 becomes policy - no new credit from Bonn's and Vienna's banks, repayment before consumption, and an end to Mittag's embellished statistics.
foci.o: Solvency and honest numbers; price consumer goods +4 %, stability -2 %, Kombinat Directors -5.

foci.d: After the Polish crisis the republic and the Soviet Union build their own bridge: a rail ferry from Mukran on Rügen to Klaipėda, opened in 1986. Soviet goods no longer cross Poland.
foci.o: Flagship project P of the doctrine (replaces 'Comecon Joint Projects', which duplicated the Warsaw Pact section's joint investment).

e: Programme "Eternal Friendship with the Soviet Union": Civilian factory output +3 %
foci.d: Rail cars from Ammendorf, ships from Warnemünde, machine tools from Karl-Marx-Stadt: Moscow's orders come first, are paid in transferable roubles and keep every plant busy for years.
foci.o: Long term: secure orders and Moscow's favour; price Kombinat Directors -5 (no hard currency).

foci.d: Even Moscow's man counts the debt: what the West pays for in marks goes west first, and the Soviet orders wait.
foci.o: Short term: hard currency now; price Moscow's Trust -3.

foci.n: One Economy with the Soviet Union
e: Programme "Eternal Friendship with the Soviet Union": Research sharing +5 %, Energy use -3 %
foci.d: Joint plans, joint research institutes, joint power grids: the republic's economy becomes a western province of the Soviet one.
foci.o: Doctrine capstone C.

e: Programme "Eternal Friendship with the Soviet Union": Civilian factory output +3 %
foci.d: The Soviet ambassador lets it be known which comrades Moscow trusts - and which Kombinate can expect Soviet orders. Krolikowski only has to listen.
foci.o: Succession hub: needs the loyalty fork and the doctrine's flagship.

e: Designated heir: Egon Krenz takes over on death or retirement
Programme "Eternal Friendship with the Soviet Union": Monthly population +0.02
foci.d: Egon Krenz is young, loyal and known in Moscow from a hundred FDJ delegations: the Kremlin's choice for the next generation.

e: Designated heir: Kurt Hager takes over on death or retirement
Programme "Eternal Friendship with the Soviet Union": Interest rates -3 %
foci.d: Kurt Hager, the chief ideologist, guarantees that nothing will change - which is exactly what Krolikowski wants.

e: Adds "The Eternal Alliance": Stability +3 %, Civilian factory output +3 %, War support +3 %, Trade opinion -5 %
foci.d: The GDR is now the Soviet Union's most dependable ally - richer in orders, poorer in pride. Moscow will never let this republic fall.
foci.o: Capstone.

e: Programme "Continuity and Renewal": Political power gain +3 %, Workforce +2 %
Our leader gains the trait "The FDJ Generation"
foci.d: Egon Krenz, born 1937, FDJ chief from 1974 and the first leader who was a child when the war ended: continuity, the party promises, with a younger face.
foci.o: Historical: First Secretary 18 October - 3 December 1989. Here possible from 1976.

e: The Party State: Ideological defence (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: Günter Schabowski, editor of Neues Deutschland and later Berlin's party boss, becomes the voice of the new leadership - quick, eloquent, occasionally careless. One wrong sentence can open a border.

e: Shield and Sword: Intel network gain +5 %
foci.d: Wolfgang Herger, Krenz's comrade from the FDJ, heads the Central Committee's security department: army, police and Stasi report through him - and the church groups feel it first.

Eberhard Aurich, Krenz's successor at the head of the FDJ, mobilises two million blue shirts for the leader who once wore theirs - and hundreds of thousands march past the tribune at the Whitsun meeting, at the state's expense.
foci.o: Absorbs the former 'The Whitsun Meeting'.

foci.d: Former FDJ secretaries take over district offices and ministries: a generation that learned to organise rallies now organises the state. Rallies become ministries.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Youth Brigades in Every Kombinat": Workforce +3 %, Infrastructure construction +5 %, Monthly population +0.02, Consumer goods +2 %, Interest rates +3 %
foci.d: Krenz's economics are the FDJ's: 'Jugendobjekte' in every Kombinat, youth brigades on every priority site, and a young workforce that is promised flats in return.
foci.o: Doctrine entry E: replaces whichever Economic Line is active.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Young Families First": Monthly population +0.05, Stability +3 %, Social costs +5 %, Interest rates +5 %
Western credit: treasury +1 % of GDP, debt +1 % of GDP
foci.d: The FDJ's demand becomes law: young couples move to the front of the housing queue, the interest-free marriage loan grows and shrinks with every child ('abkindern'), every child gets a crèche place - paid partly on credit.
foci.o: Births and calm; price social costs +5 %, interest +5 %, debt.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Central Youth Projects": Civilian factory construction +5 %, Infrastructure construction +5 %, Workforce +3 %, Consumer goods +3 %, Stability -2 %
foci.d: The FDJ Central Committee assigns whole brigades to the republic's priority sites - power stations, chemical plants, railway lines. The building goes fast; the young builders wait for their own flats.
foci.o: Construction and workforce; price consumer goods +3 %, stability -2 %.

foci.d: Youth brigades from every district build Marzahn and Hellersdorf: tens of thousands of flats for the capital - and resentment in the provinces that lose their builders.
foci.o: Flagship project P of the doctrine.

e: Western credit: treasury +1.5 % of GDP, debt +1.5 % of GDP
foci.d: Krenz asks Bonn for credit to fill the shops before the next winter, as Schalck-Golodkowski did in the autumn of 1989.
foci.o: Short term: calm now; price debt, Moscow's Trust -3 and a drift to Rapprochement.

e: Programme "Continuity and Renewal": Interest rates -5 %, Civilian industry tax +3 %
foci.d: Gerhard Schürer's analysis tells the Politburo what it never wanted to hear - as on 31 October 1989: without cuts the republic cannot pay its Western debts. Krenz publishes it.
foci.o: Long term: solvency and honesty; price stability -2 %.

e: Programme "Continuity and Renewal": Monthly population +0.03, Workforce +2 %
foci.d: The generation that grew up behind the Wall now runs the republic it was raised for - steadier than the old men feared, younger than the West hoped.
foci.o: Doctrine capstone C (spec c: the former leader capstone moves into the doctrine; the heir picks close the succession).

foci.d: 'With today's session we will introduce a turn' - Krenz's own words of October 1989. Which turn is the question every comrade asks; the first step is to talk to the church.
foci.o: Hub of the reform fork: Open the Gates (historical) or the player-only Chinese Solution.

e: Adds "The Travel Law": Stability +3 %, Western drift +0.02, Workforce -2 %
foci.d: A new travel law: every citizen may apply for a passport and a visa to the West. The pressure valve opens - Bonn and Moscow hold their breath.
foci.o: Reform: stability now; price workforce -2 % in the idea and Moscow's Trust -3. The Antifascist Protection Rampart stays (its ladder belongs to the Border Troops section); the travel law lives beside it.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): West Germany finances a travel-currency fund and a large credit line; every GDR citizen may travel to the West. If Bonn accepts: treasury +1 % of GDP as a credit (debt +1 %), Inner-German course +0.10, our opinion +15; if it declines: course -0.05
foci.d: Schalck-Golodkowski carries the offer to Bonn, as in November 1989: open borders for every citizen, if the Federal Republic pays for the travel currency and a new credit line.

foci.a: `emerging_communist_state_are_in_power`; Egon Krenz is First Secretary (`COLDWAR_DDR_first_sec_kre`); date from 04.06.1989 OR stability below 35 %
e: Adds "Order Restored": Stability +3 %, Ideological defence (Cold War) +8 %, Police costs +20 %, Trade opinion -15 %, Research speed -3 %
Press law: one step more censorship
foci.d: June 1989: the Volkskammer applauds the massacre on Tiananmen Square and Krenz carries the congratulations to Beijing. Alt-history: the republic answers its own streets the same way.
foci.o: Player only, drastic. Gated to after Tiananmen or an open crisis. Repression: stability; price police costs, trade, research, church -25.

foci.d: The Stasi's crisis plans list thousands of 'hostile-negative' citizens for internment in an emergency. The plans leave the safe and become orders.
foci.o: Player only. Based on the MfS 'Vorbeugekomplex' internment plans.

e: Shield and Sword: Intel network gain +5 %, Decryption +3.5 %
foci.d: As Central Committee secretary for security Krenz supervised the Stasi, the police, the army and the courts; as First Secretary he keeps the portfolio.
Krenz chaired the commission that announced 98.85 % for the National Front in May 1989. Church groups counted too - and found the lie.
For years Krenz was called the crown prince. Now he must name one of his own - from a generation that has started families of its own.
foci.o: Succession hub: needs the reform fork and the doctrine's flagship.

e: Designated heir: Hans Modrow takes over on death or retirement
foci.d: Hans Modrow, the reformer from Dresden, is to follow - the party's insurance against the street.
foci.o: Historically Modrow became head of government under Krenz in November 1989.

e: Designated heir: Werner Krolikowski takes over on death or retirement
Programme "Continuity and Renewal": Civilian factory output +2 %
foci.d: Werner Krolikowski, Moscow's man for twenty years, is to follow - the Soviet embassy will not object.

e: Programme "Renewal from Below": Civilian factory productivity +2 %, Infrastructure construction +3 %
Our leader gains the trait "The Dresden Reformer"
foci.d: Hans Modrow, Dresden's district secretary since 1973, lives in a rented flat, queues like everyone else and was kept out of the Politburo for sixteen years. Now the party asks the outsider.
foci.o: Alt-history: Modrow entered the Politburo only on 8 November 1989 and headed the government until April 1990.

foci.d: Wolfgang Berghofer, the young pragmatist who would run Dresden's city hall, brings managers who measure success in flats repaired, not banners - and sends the banner-makers home.

e: Programme "Renewal from Below": Civilian industry tax +3 %
foci.d: Christa Luft and the economists of the Berlin-Karlshorst college of economics may finally say aloud what their models have shown for years. The truth unsettles.

e: Shield and Sword: Intel network gain +10 %, Decryption +3.5 %
foci.d: Markus Wolf, the spymaster of the HV A, has read the West's files on the republic - and believes in a reformed socialism. His counsel comes with his network; Moscow's old guard frowns.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Districts Plan Themselves": Civilian factory productivity +3 %, Infrastructure construction +5 %, Bureaucracy costs -5 %, Political power gain -3 %
foci.d: Modrow ran Dresden for sixteen years with what Berlin left him. Now the district becomes the unit that plans: local budgets, local building plans, local craftsmen.
foci.o: Doctrine entry E: replaces whichever Economic Line is active.

e: The Economic Line becomes "Power to the Districts": Infrastructure construction +8 %, Civilian factory construction +5 %, Bureaucracy costs -7 %, Political power gain -5 %, Corruption costs +3 %
foci.d: The fifteen district councils get their own budgets and building plans: Berlin sets the frame, Dresden, Rostock and Suhl fill it. The central apparatus loses its grip - and some district bosses build themselves kingdoms.
foci.o: Construction and cheap administration; price political power -5 %, corruption costs +3 %, Nomenklatura -5.

e: The Economic Line becomes "The Craftsmen Return": Consumer goods -3 %, Civilian industry tax +5 %, Civilian factory productivity +3 %, Western drift +0.01, Political power gain -2 %
foci.d: The 11,000 semi-state firms, private factories and craft cooperatives nationalised in 1972 are handed back to their owners - as Modrow's government allowed in March 1990, here years early. Prices that cover costs, small trades licensed again.
foci.o: Consumer goods and tax income; price Nomenklatura -10, Moscow's Trust -2. Absorbs the former 'Market Elements in the Plan'.

foci.d: Robotron's headquarters and the microelectronics centre ZMD make Dresden the 'Silicon Saxony' of the East - with a district secretary who fights for every hall.
foci.o: Flagship project P of the doctrine.

e: Adds "Joint Ventures" for 730 days: Investment cost for foreigners here -10 %, Extra investment slots (Imperia) +1, World-market exposure (Cold War) +10 %
The Planned Economy: Return on investment +2 %
foci.d: Western firms may take stakes in East German enterprises - the joint-venture law of Modrow's 1990 government, here years early.
foci.o: Short term: Western capital; price Moscow's Trust -3 and world-market exposure +10 %.

foci.d: Robotron builds mainframes for the whole bloc and Dresden trades chips for Soviet raw materials - safe partners, no Western strings, and no Western machines for the general directors either.
foci.o: Long term: safe partners and shared research; price Kombinat Directors -5.

e: Programme "Renewal from Below": Civilian industry tax +3 %, Civilian factory productivity +3 %
foci.d: Plan where it must, market where it can: the districts build, the craftsmen sell, the Kombinate keep part of their profit.
foci.o: Doctrine capstone C.

e: Press law: one step less censorship
foci.d: October 1989 in Dresden: the city meets the 'Group of 20' chosen by the demonstrators. Here the party talks to its critics before they take to the streets.
foci.o: Hub of the reform fork: Reformed Socialism (stay SED, reform slowly) or Hand Over to the Democratic Communists (fast).

foci.d: The SED stays, but changes: secret ballots inside the party, term limits for functionaries, an end to the privileges of Wandlitz.
foci.o: Slow reform: the party stays in power and gets cleaner; price Nomenklatura -10.

foci.d: An extraordinary party congress elects a new Central Committee by secret ballot. Half of the old guard is gone; the members are proud of their party again.

Party, bloc parties, church and the democratic communists of Robert Havemann's circle sit at one table in the Dietrich Bonhoeffer House - as in December 1989, years earlier. Modrow concludes that the SED cannot reform itself.
foci.o: Player only. Opens the hand-over below. Fast reform: stability and the church; price Nomenklatura -10 and Moscow's Trust -2.

foci.n: Hand Over to the Democratic Communists
e: Ruling party becomes League of Democratic Communists (Left-Wing); new head of state Robert Havemann - the SED hands over power peacefully
Adds "Transition of Power" for 180 days: Stability -10 %, Political power gain -15 %
foci.d: Modrow steps aside: the League of Democratic Communists forms the government, the SED becomes one party among others.
foci.o: Player only. The only First Secretary focus that changes the ruling party - Modrow's tree closes afterwards.

foci.d: Every 13 February young Christians gather with candles at the ruins of the Frauenkirche. Modrow sends no police - he goes to talk to Bishop Hempel.

e: Adds "Travel Relief": Stability +3 %, Western drift +0.01, Workforce -1 %
foci.d: Pensioners already travel west; now family visits, honeymoons and study trips are approved by the district, not by the Stasi. Most come back.
foci.o: Price: a few do not come back (workforce -1 % in the idea).

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): A Treaty Community of the two German states: joint commissions for economy, transport, environment and culture and a long-term trade and credit agreement. If Bonn accepts: Inner-German course +0.20, treasury +1 % of GDP as a credit (debt +1 %), timed idea trade opinion +15 %; if it declines: course -0.05
foci.d: 17 November 1989: Modrow offered Bonn a 'treaty community' of the two German states. Here the offer comes while the Wall still stands firm.
The outsider who was never admitted fills the Politburo with district secretaries, scientists and women - and asks who should carry the reform on.
foci.o: Succession hub on the reform branch (the round-table branch ends with the hand-over); needs the doctrine's flagship. The Politburo never had a female full member.

e: Designated heir: Egon Krenz takes over on death or retirement
foci.d: Egon Krenz, the FDJ's former chief, promises to keep the apparatus loyal to the reform - if he inherits it.

e: Designated heir: Werner Lamberz takes over on death or retirement

e: Adds "The Reformed Republic": Stability +3 %, Civilian factory productivity +3 %, Monthly population +0.03, Ideology drift defence -10 %
foci.d: A socialist republic that talks to its church, lets its people travel and trades with Bonn as an equal: the Dresden model has become the state.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian industry tax +2 %
foci.d: Some 11,000 private, semi-state and craft-cooperative firms - many with a state share since 1956 - still make furniture, textiles, toys and spare parts. The party asks how long it will tolerate them.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian factory output +5 %, Max factory efficiency +3 %
foci.d: 1979-81: the industrial associations are dissolved. Some 130 central Kombinate - each with its own research, suppliers and export trade - answer directly to the ministries.
foci.o: The last independent suppliers are swallowed by the Kombinate (craftsmen -5).

e: Unlocks decisions: The Five-Year Plans: priority for 1981-85 (150 PP, valid until 31.12.1985)
The Planned Economy: Energy use -5 %, Economic cycle law costs -1 %
foci.d: The X Party Congress of April 1981 orders 'comprehensive intensification': more output from less energy, less material and fewer hands - just as the Western debt falls due.

foci.a: Planned economy: trade law is not Mixed, Consumption or Globalized Trade Economy (`NOT = { has_idea = mixed_economy has_idea = semi_consumption_economy has_idea = consumption_economy has_idea = globalized_trade_economy }`)
e: Adds "The Intensification Drive": Civilian factory productivity +4 %, Max factory efficiency +4 %, Energy use -5 %, Consumer goods +2 %
foci.d: The formula of the 1980s: growth no longer from new factories but from science, robots and savings - the planned economy's last answer to the world market.
foci.o: Plan capstone (no PP). Norm increases and wage discipline cost the FDGB's goodwill; the drive starves the shops (consumer goods +2 %).

e: The Planned Economy: Resource export revenue +5 %
foci.d: Only the Ministry of Foreign Trade may buy or sell abroad: every rouble of Comecon trade and every Western Mark passes through its hands.
foci.o: The Kombinate may not sell abroad themselves (directors -5).

e: Unlocks decisions: Hard Currency: Intershop, Genex gift service, art and antiques sales, arms exports (needs "Imes"), prisoner ransom
foci.d: Alexander Schalck-Golodkowski's KoKo, founded in 1966 under the wing of the MfS, earns hard currency by any means - art and antiques, arms, blood plasma and prisoners.
foci.o: Unlocks the KoKo decision category of d_concept ("Hard Currency"). The price of the money is corruption.

foci.d: Furniture for IKEA, cameras for Quelle, petrol for West Berlin: whatever the West will buy is sold, even when the shops at home stay empty.
foci.o: Hard currency now; the shops pay (consumer goods +3 %).

foci.d: By 1981 the republic owes Western banks more than ten billion dollars, and Schürer warns that it will soon borrow only to pay the interest.
foci.o: Hub of the credit-or-austerity choice (spec d T2). The honest balance sheet is the reward, not political power.

e: Western credit: treasury +2 % of GDP, debt +2 % of GDP
foci.d: Consortia of Western banks in Vienna, London and Frankfurt roll over the republic's debts - at a price in interest and in Moscow's suspicion. (Government-guaranteed credits from Bonn are an offer in the German Question and in Honecker's tree.)
foci.o: Credit side (spec d T2): money, a factory and cheaper refinancing now; the price is the debt itself and Moscow's Trust. Market credit (MD debt mechanic, affects no other country).

e: Fund a treasury-backed repayment up to3%GDP; matching debt reduction, -0.25pp interest730days, +8%sanction resistance and +5Moscow Trust on settlement.
foci.d: Every debt payment competes with investment, imports and the goods households expect to find in the shops. The government will reserve liquid funds for a measurable reduction in outstanding principal rather than another expansion financed from abroad. A stronger balance sheet promises greater freedom of action, but the resources committed to repayment cannot build the next factory.
foci.o: Paid implementation and one-time settlement are maintained in dg_quality.py runtime sources.

foci.d: A bread roll costs five pfennigs, as in 1950, and a tram ticket twenty. Every year the gap between price and cost grows - and with it the state's bill.
foci.o: Hub of the price choice.

e: Adds "Stable Consumer Prices": Stability +3 %, Monthly population +0.02, Social costs +10 %
foci.d: The promise of 1971: bread, rents, fares and children's clothes will not cost a pfennig more - whatever it costs the budget.
foci.o: Calm and loyalty; social costs +10 % for good.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian industry tax +5 %, Civilian factory productivity +4 %
foci.d: The planners' heresy: let prices tell the truth. Wasteful factories are exposed - and so are the households, after twenty years of fixed prices.
foci.o: Revenue and efficiency; stability -2 % and the FDGB pay.

foci.n: Chemistry Gives Bread, Prosperity and Beauty
foci.d: The slogan of the 1958 chemistry programme still hangs over Leuna: a republic without oil fields will build its wealth on coal, Soviet oil and its chemists.
The new petrochemical half of the Leuna works runs on Soviet oil instead of coal: ethylene, methanol and polyethylene for the whole republic.
The Buna works' billboard on the transit motorway promises plastics for every household: PVC, synthetic rubber and carbide chemistry from Schkopau.

e: The Planned Economy: synthetic_refinery_productivity_modifier +3 %, Health costs +5 %
foci.d: Halle, Merseburg and Bitterfeld make a third of the republic's chemicals - and most of its smog.
foci.o: The smog is the price (health costs +5 %).

e: The Planned Economy: Fuel gain +5 %, Energy use -3 %
foci.d: At the end of the Druzhba pipeline the petrochemical Kombinat on the Oder refines Soviet crude - for the republic's tractors and for West Berlin's petrol stations.

e: The Planned Economy: Resource export revenue +5 %
foci.d: The most profitable trade the republic has: Soviet crude at friendship prices goes out again as diesel and heating oil for Western Marks.
foci.o: Moscow notices that its subsidised oil is resold for dollars (trust -2 is the political price of the income).

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian factory construction +5 %
foci.d: Machine tools from Karl-Marx-Stadt, cranes from Leipzig, printing presses from Radebeul: the republic is Comecon's workshop.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian factory output +3 %
Brandenburg: +4 steel while owned and controlled
foci.d: The 'first socialist city' on the Oder finishes its cold rolling mill in 1974: sheet steel for cars, fridges and washing machines from Soviet ore and Polish coke.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian factory construction +5 %
Brandenburg: +6 steel while owned and controlled
foci.d: Eisenhüttenstadt still has no hot rolling mill: its slabs travel to the Soviet Union and back. Alt-history: the gap is closed in the 1970s, not in 1997.
foci.o: Alt-history leaf (historically built only in 1997 by EKO Stahl); not on the historical path, so the AI may skip it.

e: The Planned Economy: Resource export revenue +3 %
foci.d: The Kombinate 'Fritz Heckert' and '7 October' sell lathes and machining centres from Moscow to Milan - the republic's best ambassadors in the West.

e: The Labour Shortage eases by one step (whichever step is active)
The Planned Economy: Civilian factory productivity +4 %
foci.d: Expensive Western machines must never stand still: through the 1970s the Kombinate move ever more workers into round-the-clock shifts.
foci.o: Labour ladder (owned by the economy): The Labour Shortage -> The Labour Shortage (Easing) -> The Last Vacancies -> removed. The three easing foci (The Three-Shift System, Crèches for Every Child, Robots for the Kombinate) each ease the ACTIVE step by one, in any order: if has the_labour_shortage -> swap to labour_shortage_2; else_if labour_shortage_2 -> swap to labour_shortage_3; else_if labour_shortage_3 -> remove. Guarded swaps only, never an else-add (nothing happens if the shortage is already gone). The contract-worker offer (foreign agent) does not touch this ladder.

foci.d: The Trabant P601 of 1964 is still the people's car - two-stroke engine, plastic body, a wait of twelve years. Zwickau has successors on the drawing board; the Politburo hesitates.
foci.o: Hub of the car choice; the factory is Sachsenring Zwickau.

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian factory productivity +3 %
foci.d: No Western licence, no new car: the P601 is improved bolt by bolt and built until the end of time. The hard currency stays at home.
foci.o: Self-reliance and saved currency; the people keep waiting for a car from the 1960s (stability -2 %).

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): A four-stroke engine plant in Karl-Marx-Stadt under Volkswagen licence, paid in counter-trade: if Bonn accepts, we build one civilian factory (paid) and Inner-German course +0.05; they gain influence in our country +3 % and the counter-trade deliveries
foci.d: 1984: Volkswagen sells the licence for its Polo engine. The Wartburg 1.3 and the Trabant 1.1 get four-stroke engines - paid for with parts delivered to Wolfsburg.
foci.o: Western licence = Moscow's Trust cost. The offer is the deal with the Federal Republic; our own reward does not depend on it.

foci.d: Trabant, Wartburg, the W50 lorry and the Multicar: the IFA Kombinat builds everything that moves on the republic's roads - and for half of Comecon.
Warnemünde and Rostock build freighters, trawlers and fish-factory ships - most of them for the Soviet Union, paid in oil and timber.

e: Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): A long-term order for trawlers and freighters: if they accept, we gain Moscow's Trust +5 and dockyard output +5 % (The Planned Economy); they gain a timed naval production bonus (their own event effect)
foci.d: Every second ship from the Baltic yards sails east: the Soviet fishing fleet is the republic's best customer - and its most demanding.
Founded in Dresden in 1969: typewriters, calculators, data processing - the republic's answer to IBM, with almost 70,000 employees by the 1980s.
Twenty thousand researchers in Berlin-Adlershof, Jena and Dresden; since the academy reform of 1969 they work to contracts with the Kombinate instead of to their curiosity.

foci.d: Comecon's Unified System copies IBM's 360: Robotron's EC 1040 of 1973 becomes the bloc's most successful mainframe, sold from Havana to Novosibirsk.

foci.d: 'Rationalisation by our own means': every Kombinat must build its own robots and automatic lines - tens of thousands of 'industrial robots' by 1985, many of them simple manipulators.

e: The Planned Economy: microchip_plant_productivity_modifier +5 %, Consumer goods +2 %
foci.d: June 1977: the Politburo orders a microelectronics industry built from scratch - billions of Marks and tens of thousands of engineers, all under the Western COCOM embargo.
foci.o: The money for chips is missing in the shops (consumer goods cost line). Hub of the chip choice.

e: The Planned Economy: Sanction resistance (Imperia) +5 %, Research speed +2 %
foci.d: Every chip designed in Dresden and Erfurt, every machine built at home: slower and dearer, but nobody in the West can switch it off.
foci.o: Independence and own research; the price is money (0.5 % of GDP).

e: The Planned Economy: microchip_plant_productivity_modifier +5 %, Sanction resistance (Imperia) -5 %
foci.d: The MfS sector for science and technology smuggles Western chips, wafer steppers and machines through front companies - and Dresden copies them transistor by transistor.
foci.o: Cheap and fast, but the West notices: sanction resistance -5 % (COCOM).

foci.d: From 1980 the Centre for Microelectronics Dresden is the heart of the chip programme - from 16-kilobit to 256-kilobit memory chips.
September 1988: Dresden presents a 1-megabit memory chip - years behind the West, and each one costs 534 Marks to make while the world market pays a few dollars.
foci.o: Capstone (no PP): prestige at home, the shops pay.

foci.d: From 1985 the KC 85 and later Robotron's school computer enter the classrooms - eight bits, cassette drives and a generation that learns to program.
The optics Kombinat of Jena grinds lenses for planetaria, microscopes, the NVA and the Soviet space programme - and sells them for hard currency.
foci.o: Cameras and microscopes go west for hard currency; the shops at home wait (consumer goods +1 %).

e: The Planned Economy: Military factory productivity +3 %
foci.d: Night sights, rangefinders, tank periscopes and reconnaissance cameras: Jena equips the Warsaw Pact's front line.

foci.b: `has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_navy_air_cameras_from_jena` (the MKF-6 camera - no double reward)
foci.d: September 1976: Zeiss's multispectral camera photographs the earth from Soyuz 22 and later from the Salyut stations - the republic's eye in orbit.

e: Builds 1 fossil power plant (paid: 0.35 % of GDP)
The Planned Economy: Fossil power plant output +5 %
foci.d: Lusatia and the Leipzig basin hold the republic's only real raw material: 250 million tonnes of lignite a year, dug by excavators taller than a church.
Near Hoyerswerda the world's largest briquette and town-gas works turns lignite into gas, coke and briquettes for every stove in the republic.

e: The Planned Economy: Energy use -5 %, Fuel gain +3 %
foci.d: Autumn 1981: Brezhnev cuts the republic's oil from 19 to 17 million tonnes a year - Moscow needs the dollars more than its ally needs the oil.
foci.o: Hub of the oil choice: saving is the only immediate answer.

foci.d: Alt-history: the republic keeps its oil-fired plants and buys the missing two million tonnes in Rotterdam - with money it does not have.

e: The Planned Economy: Energy use -6.5 %, fossil_pp_fuel_consumption_modifier -5 %
foci.d: Every Kombinat gets an energy quota: street lights are dimmed, shop windows go dark and the planners count kilowatt-hours like bread.

e: Builds 2 fossil power plants (paid: 0.69 % of GDP)
foci.d: From 1971 the lignite giant of Upper Lusatia grows to 3,520 megawatts - the largest power station of the republic.

e: Builds 2 fossil power plants (paid: 0.69 % of GDP)
The Planned Economy: Fossil power plant output +8 %, Health costs +5 %
foci.d: Six 500-megawatt blocks near Cottbus (1976-89) burn eighty thousand tonnes of coal a day - and the open-cast mines swallow the Sorbian villages around them.
foci.o: The smoke is the price (health costs +5 %).

e: The Planned Economy: Nuclear energy output +1 %
foci.d: Lignite alone cannot carry an industrial state: the planners look east for natural gas and to the atom for the future.

The Planned Economy: Nuclear reactor construction +5 %
foci.d: At Lubmin on the Baltic, Soviet VVER-440 reactors go online from 1973 to 1979 - 1,760 megawatts, a tenth of the republic's electricity.
foci.o: Lignite ladder (owned by the economy), heaviest to lightest: Coal Instead of Oil -> King Lignite -> Lignite Still Reigns -> Lignite Among Other Fuels. e: King Lignite eases by one step (whichever step is active)
foci.d: On the Elbe near Stendal four VVER-1000 reactors are to make the republic's largest power station - if the money and the Soviet parts arrive.
foci.o: Lignite ladder (owned by the economy), heaviest to lightest: Coal Instead of Oil -> King Lignite -> Lignite Still Reigns -> Lignite Among Other Fuels. Guarded swaps only, never an else-add (Green and church paths may have removed lignite entirely). Atom side: two reactors and one more lignite step eased; the price is 0.5 % of GDP on top of the reactors.

e: Builds 1 fossil power plant (paid: 0.35 % of GDP)
foci.d: Alt-history: after Chernobyl the church circles ask what the cloud from Kiev would have done over Magdeburg, the planners ask what the reactors cost - and Stendal is halted.
foci.o: Calm and the church; the lignite keeps burning (a fossil plant instead of the reactors) and Moscow loses its prestige project (Moscow's Trust -3).

e: Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): We build our section of the Orenburg pipeline in return for natural gas: if they accept, we gain Moscow's Trust +5 and energy production +5 % (The Planned Economy) and set COLDWAR_DDR_soyuz_gas; they gain construction speed +5 % for two years from our builders (their own effect)
foci.d: 1974-79: from Orenburg to the Soviet western border, built by all of Comecon - the republic's section in Ukraine, the FDJ's 'Druzhba' route, is its largest youth project.
foci.o: Matches the Soviet tree's own invitation (COLDWAR_SOV_the_soyuz_pipeline -> event COLDWAR_SOV.118 to DDR): accepting that invitation should set the same flag COLDWAR_DDR_soyuz_gas. The foreign section's Orenburg mention should hook here via `av`, not duplicate it.

e: King Lignite eases by one step (whichever step is active)
foci.d: From 1979 Orenburg gas reaches the republic; the lignite town gas of Berlin, Leipzig and Dresden gives way.
foci.o: Lignite ladder (owned by the economy), heaviest to lightest: Coal Instead of Oil -> King Lignite -> Lignite Still Reigns -> Lignite Among Other Fuels. Easing foci (Greifswald, Build Stendal, Oil on the World Market, Natural Gas for the Cities) move the ACTIVE step one to the right, in any order: if has energy_coal_instead_of_oil -> swap to king_lignite; else_if king_lignite -> king_lignite_2; else_if king_lignite_2 -> king_lignite_3; at king_lignite_3 nothing. Guarded swaps only, never an else-add (Green and church paths may have removed lignite entirely). Cleaner air in the cities (health costs -3 %).

e: The Planned Economy: Agricultural productivity +3 %, Agriculture tax +5 %
foci.d: Since the 'socialist spring' of 1960 every farmer belongs to an agricultural production cooperative; nearly a million people work the land of a small, crowded country.
From the early 1970s the cooperatives hand their fields to crop units of four to six thousand hectares; the animals stay behind in the village cooperatives.
foci.o: Hub of the farm choice. The farmers lose their animals to the separation (LPG farmers -5).

e: The Planned Economy: Agricultural productivity +6 %, Agriculture tax +10 %
foci.d: Fields as wide as the horizon, crop-spraying aircraft, combine harvesters in columns: the farm becomes a factory and the farmer a worker in green.
foci.o: KAP side: output, tax and full shops; the cooperative farmers become wage workers (LPG farmers -10).

e: The Planned Economy: agriculture_district_income_tax_modifier +5 %, Health costs +3 %
foci.d: Eberswalde fattens almost two hundred thousand pigs a year, Ferdinandshof thousands of bulls - meat for the people, for export and liquid manure for the groundwater.
foci.o: The liquid manure is the price (health costs +3 %).

e: The Planned Economy: Agricultural productivity +3 %, Monthly population +0.03
foci.d: Alt-history: crops and animals are reunited in the village cooperative - smaller, slower, closer to the soil, and the young farmers stay.
foci.o: Cooperative self-government side: content villages and families; less output than the KAP, and the cadres lose control (-5).

foci.d: The cooperative's general assembly again decides what is sown and when; the Democratic Farmers' Party finally speaks for the villages.

e: The Planned Economy: Agriculture tax +10 %, Consumer goods +1 %
foci.d: Every year the republic buys millions of tonnes of grain and fodder in the West for hard currency; self-sufficiency would save hundreds of millions.
foci.o: The saved hard currency is the income; less imported fodder means less meat in the shops (consumer goods +1 %).

foci.d: Ammonia and urea from Piesteritz on the Elbe: new plants in the 1970s double the fertiliser for the cooperatives' fields.
Agrochemical centres spread fertiliser and pesticides by lorry and aircraft - efficient, and fatal for rivers and wells.
foci.o: Rivers and wells pay (health costs +3 %).

foci.d: Drainage and irrigation on a million hectares: the FDJ drained the great Friedland meadows in the 1950s, now the cooperatives do it on every wet field.
The cooperative farmer's half hectare, the city allotment and the rabbit hutch supply much of the fruit and eggs - bought up by the state above the shop price.

e: The Planned Economy: agriculture_district_income_tax_modifier +5 %, Consumer goods +2 %
foci.d: Pork and beef go west for hard currency while the butchers at home sell out by noon.

e: Unlocks decisions: The Housing Programme: yearly building drives (Plattenbau) - stability up, construction capacity bound (same category as Honecker's programme; whichever focus comes first unlocks it)
foci.d: Every district gets a housing construction Kombinat with its own panel factory; from 1973 they are to solve 'the housing question as a social problem' by 1990.
foci.o: Construction side of the 1973 housing programme. Honecker's leader tree carries the political programme; both unlock the same category.

e: The Planned Economy: Construction speed +3 %, Infrastructure construction +5 %
foci.d: From 1972 one standard panel system for the whole republic: six storeys, central heating, a bath and a fitted kitchen - luxury for families from crumbling tenements.
The chemical workers' city west of the Saale, begun in 1964, grows to ninety thousand people - the model for every new town of the republic.

e: The Labour Shortage eases by one step (whichever step is active)
The Planned Economy: Monthly population +0.04, Social costs +5 %
foci.d: Crèche, kindergarten, after-school care and the 'baby year' of 1976: nine in ten women of working age can work - and do.
foci.o: Labour ladder (owned by the economy): The Labour Shortage -> The Labour Shortage (Easing) -> The Last Vacancies -> removed. The three easing foci (The Three-Shift System, Crèches for Every Child, Robots for the Kombinate) each ease the ACTIVE step by one, in any order: if has the_labour_shortage -> swap to labour_shortage_2; else_if labour_shortage_2 -> swap to labour_shortage_3; else_if labour_shortage_3 -> remove. Guarded swaps only, never an else-add (nothing happens if the shortage is already gone). The contract-worker offer (foreign agent) does not touch this ladder.

foci.d: From 1977 the largest building site of the republic: some sixty thousand flats on the eastern edge of Berlin, a new city in ten years.
July 1988: the party celebrates the three-millionth flat since 1971 in Marzahn - while the old towns of Leipzig and Görlitz crumble behind the cameras.
foci.o: Housing capstone (no PP).

foci.d: Bread, rents and brown coal are cheap; tights, car parts and bananas are sold under the counter to friends.
foci.o: The factory makes consumer goods.

foci.n: Too Much Money, Too Few Goods
foci.d: Wages rise and the savings books swell - well over a hundred billion Marks by the 1980s - but the shelves do not fill.
foci.o: Hub of the consumer choice: the savings fund the budget, the empty shelves cost stability.

e: Adds "The Second Pay Packet": Stability +4 %, Monthly population +0.02, Consumer goods +2 %, Social costs +5 %
foci.d: Rents at pre-war levels, bread at 1950 prices, children's shoes below cost: by the late 1980s subsidies swallow a fifth of the budget.
foci.o: Subsidy side: lasting calm and loyalty; the price sits in the idea (consumer goods +2 %, social costs +5 %).

e: The Planned Economy: Civilian industry tax +5 %, Consumer goods -3 %
foci.d: Exquisit for fashion, Delikat for fine food: the republic sells cheap basics and expensive 'luxury' side by side - and soaks up the money that has nothing to buy.
foci.o: Revenue side: money and a lighter consumer bill; two classes of shoppers cost stability (-2 %).

foci.a: Planned economy: trade law is not Mixed, Consumption or Globalized Trade Economy (`NOT = { has_idea = mixed_economy has_idea = semi_consumption_economy has_idea = consumption_economy has_idea = globalized_trade_economy }`)
e: The Planned Economy: Consumer goods -3 %, Civilian factory construction +3 %
foci.d: Every heavy-industry Kombinat must also make consumer goods: the chemical works sell garden hoses, the arms factories bicycles.
Order a car at eighteen, collect it at thirty: millions of orders wait in Zwickau and Eisenach, and a used Trabant costs more than a new one.
foci.o: Car prices far above cost fill the budget; the queue costs the FDGB's patience.

foci.d: From 1974 citizens may legally hold Western money - and spend it in the Intershops, where the republic sells Western goods for Western Marks.
foci.o: Two classes of citizens: those with Western relatives and those without (stability -1 % is the political price).

e: Offer to VIE (they decide; no advance reward): A coffee partnership: we finance plantations in Dak Lak and are paid in coffee - if they accept, consumer goods -2 % for us (The Planned Economy) and our opinion of them +15; they gain agricultural productivity +5 % for three years (their own event effect)
foci.d: After the coffee crisis of 1977 and the hated mixed blend nicknamed 'Erichs Krönung', the republic invests in Vietnamese plantations: from the 1980s GDR experts grow coffee in Dak Lak.

foci.d: 1978: the state imports a million pairs of Levi's for hard currency - the queues outside the department stores are longer than for any party rally.
foci.o: Paid in hard currency (0.3 % of GDP).

e: The National People's Army: Army organisation +3 %, Planning speed +0.05

e: The National People's Army: Army morale +3 %

e: The National People's Army: Planning speed +0.05, Army organisation +3 %
foci.d: Alt-history: the generals ask for what every Western army has - command without a political deputy looking over the shoulder. Hoffmann's staff draft a professional officer corps.
foci.o: Professional cadres instead of a conscript army under commissars. Moscow's own army has a Main Political Directorate - a GDR without commissars looks suspicious in Karlshorst.

e: The National People's Army: Recruitable population +3 %
foci.d: The 1982 law confirms eighteen months of service for every man - and, in a state of defence, makes women liable too. 'Women for Peace' circles answer with open letters.

e: The National People's Army: Mobilisation speed +5 %
foci.d: After their service, soldiers stay reservists until fifty; every year tens of thousands are called back for weeks of exercises - in a crisis the NVA can double in days.
foci.o: Price: the factories lose workers to every reserve call-up (the labour shortage).

foci.d: October 1970: the armies of the Warsaw Pact manoeuvre on GDR soil, commanded by the republic's own Minister of National Defence, Army General Heinz Hoffmann.

e: The National People's Army: Defence on core territory +5 %
foci.d: In war the NVA's six divisions advance together with the Group of Soviet Forces in the first wave - the front line of the socialist camp runs through Thuringia and Mecklenburg.
foci.o: Hub of the doctrine choice.

foci.o: Moscow wants an offensive ally, not a hedgehog (Moscow's Trust -3).

e: The National People's Army: Max planning +5 %
foci.d: The plan for West Berlin: NVA units, border troops and combat groups would take the half-city within days of a war. Medals of the Blücher Order, created for wartime only, already lie in the depots.
foci.o: War plans only - no effect on Berlin or any other country.

e: The National People's Army: Defence on core territory +5 %, Army personnel costs -3 %

e: The National People's Army: Planning speed +0.05

foci.o: Hub of the equipment choice.

e: The National People's Army: Special forces cap +0.05

foci.d: The Volksmarine's combat swimmers train to mine harbours, locks and bridges from Kiel to the Danish straits.

e: Shield and Sword: Civilian intel +5 %, Intel network gain +5 %
foci.d: Marienborn, Checkpoint Charlie, the 'Palace of Tears' at Friedrichstraße: the passport controllers are Stasi officers in border-troop uniform.

e: The National People's Army: Army personnel costs -5 %
foci.d: From 1975 the 'Border Wall 75' replaces the improvised walls: 45,000 L-shaped concrete segments, 3.6 metres high, topped with a smooth pipe no hand can grip.

e: Replaces "The Perfected Border" with "The Iron Border": Stability +6 %, Police costs +10 %, Army personnel costs +3 %, Foreign influence defence +20 %, Ideology drift defence +10 %, Defence on core territory +5 %, Trade opinion -20 %, Western drift +0.02

e: Replaces "The Perfected Border" with "The Border with Gates": Stability +1 %, Police costs +5 %, Army personnel costs +2 %, Foreign influence defence +5 %, Trade opinion -3 %, Western drift +0.02
foci.d: Alt-history: more crossing points, and visits to the West widened from pensioners to working people. The border still stands, but it opens its gates a little - and Bonn notices.
foci.o: Ladder step 2b (soft, Rapprochement): cheaper and less isolating, but Western drift +0.02. Income = minimum exchange of the extra visitors; price: Moscow's Trust.

foci.d: 25 March 1982: for the first time a law, not just an order, regulates the border regime - including the use of firearms in its paragraph 27.

e: The Party State: Foreign influence defence +5 %
foci.d: No written order uses the word, but every guard knows it: a successful escape on his watch ends his career, a shot 'border violator' earns him a medal and leave.
foci.o: Hub of the order-to-shoot choice.

foci.d: 3 May 1974: Honecker tells the National Defence Council that firearms must be used 'ruthlessly' against anyone who tries to break through. The order stays.
foci.o: Nobody gets out (workforce +3 %); the bodies on the death strip cost the republic's image in the West (trade opinion -3 %).

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): Bonn answers the end of the shootings with a goodwill trade credit: if they accept, we gain +0.5 % of GDP as income and the Inner-German course moves +0.05 towards Rapprochement
foci.d: Alt-history: the guards are ordered to fire into the air and arrest, not to kill - no more bodies on the death strip for Western cameras.
foci.o: Price: stability -2 % (the guards and the hardliners lose their certainty).

e: The National People's Army: Army personnel costs -3 %
foci.d: From 1971 some 60,000 directional mines are fixed to the border fence - until Michael Gartenschläger dismantles two in 1976 and shows them to the West German press.
From 1972 citizens below pension age may apply to visit the West for weddings, funerals and jubilees - tens of thousands a year, and almost all of them come back.
foci.o: Historical policy, here reached through the softer border course. Price: Western drift +0.01.

foci.d: 1983-84: as part of the price for Strauss's billion-mark credits the self-firing devices and the minefields disappear from the inner-German border.
foci.o: The credit itself belongs to the foreign section; this focus pays the border side of the bargain.
