e: The National People's Army: Naval coordination +5 %, Air defence +5 %
foci.d: The republic's northern flank is the Baltic coast from Wismar to Usedom; its sky lies minutes from NATO's airfields. The Volksmarine and the Air Forces/Air Defence guard both.
Some 16,000 sailors with headquarters in Rostock: frigates, minesweepers, landing ships and fast attack craft.
foci.o: Hub of the naval choice.

e: The National People's Army: Naval organisation +5 %, Equipment costs -2 %
foci.d: The Volksmarine stays what the Pact wants: minesweepers, landing ships and fast boats for the western Baltic and the straits.
foci.o: Cheap and well drilled; the shipyards get no big orders (Baltic Shipyards -5).

e: The National People's Army: Naval range +10 %
foci.d: Alt-history: frigates for the North Sea, port calls in Luanda and Havana - the flag of the republic seen beyond the Baltic.
foci.o: Moscow assigned the Volksmarine to the Baltic; ambitions beyond it raise eyebrows.

foci.d: On Rügen the 6th Flotilla keeps the fast torpedo and missile boats, ready to strike at shipping in the Danish straits.

e: The National People's Army: Naval coordination +3 %
foci.d: From 1983 mobile launchers with anti-ship missiles hide behind the dunes - no landing fleet would reach Rügen unseen.

e: The National People's Army: Dockyard output +4 %
foci.d: At Wolgast the Peene shipyard builds the Volksmarine's own warships - in the 1980s its Parchim-class corvettes are even ordered by the Soviet Navy.

e: The National People's Army: Naval coordination +5 %
foci.d: In war the Volksmarine, the Polish Navy and the Soviet Baltic Fleet sail as one force under a Soviet admiral - their target is the Danish straits.

e: The National People's Army: Air accidents -5 %
foci.d: The LSK/LV is wired into the Pact's unified air defence: its fighters stand on 'duty system' alert under Soviet command, day and night.
The MiG-21, in a dozen variants, is the backbone of the fighter wings of the 1st and 3rd Air Defence Divisions.
foci.o: Hub of the air-force choice.

e: The National People's Army: Air defence +10 %, Air superiority efficiency +5 %
foci.d: The LSK/LV stays what it was built to be: an air-defence force that keeps NATO bombers out of the republic's sky, interceptors on five-minute alert.
foci.o: Defensive side: the sky stays closed; round-the-clock alert costs 0.3 % of GDP.

e: The National People's Army: CAS efficiency +5 %
foci.d: Fighter-bombers join the LSK/LV - first the MiG-23BN, later the Su-22: the air force learns to strike ahead of the tank divisions of the first echelon.
foci.o: Offensive side: strike power for the first echelon; NATO answers in kind (tension +1).

e: The National People's Army: Air superiority efficiency +5 %
foci.d: From 1978 the MiG-23 arrives - the first fighter of the republic with variable-sweep wings and a real search radar.
Mi-8 transports and, from 1978, Mi-24 gunships form the combat helicopter wings - flying artillery for the tank divisions.

e: The National People's Army: Air superiority efficiency +5 %, Air accidents -5 %
foci.d: 1988: Fighter Wing 3 at Preschen receives the MiG-29 - a fighter as good as anything NATO flies, bought as the republic's money runs out.

e: The National People's Army: Air defence +10 %, Static AA damage +10 %
foci.d: Rings of S-75 Dvina and S-125 Neva batteries cover Berlin, the industrial south and the coast, fed by the radar chain from the Baltic to the Fichtelberg.

Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): A GDR cosmonaut flies on a Soyuz mission of the Interkosmos programme (historically Sigmund Jähn, Soyuz 31, 26 August 1978). If the Soviet Union accepts: our event "Our Man in Space" (stability +3 %, SED popularity +2 %, Moscow's Trust +3); the Soviet Union gains opinion of us +15. If it refuses: Moscow's Trust -2 for us, nothing for them
foci.d: Two air-force pilots, Sigmund Jähn and Eberhard Köllner, train at Star City. If Moscow agrees, the first German in space will be a citizen of the GDR.
foci.o: Offer, not an executed effect: nothing happens in the Soviet Union before it decides.

e: The National People's Army: Defence on core territory +5 %
foci.d: The combat groups' real task is the home front: guarding plants, securing streets and crushing 'counter-revolutionary' unrest - a party militia against another 17 June.

e: The National People's Army: Recruitable population +3 %, Mobilisation speed +5 %
foci.d: Alt-history: the combat groups join the NVA's territorial defence - a trained reserve of hundreds of thousands under military, not party, command.

foci.o: Price: fewer conscripts (recruitable population -2 %), and the Church in Socialism party gains.

e: The National People's Army: Mobilisation speed +5 %

e: Shield and Sword: Resistance suppression +12.5 %, Counter-intelligence +15 %, Police costs +3 %
foci.d: Some 100,000 unofficial collaborators in 1970, 180,000 by 1975: colleagues, neighbours, pastors and spouses who report to a handling officer.
foci.o: Hub of the repression choice. MD standard price: police costs +3 %.

e: Adds "Silent Decomposition": Resistance suppression +10 %, Enemy operative capture chance +5 %, Police costs +5 %
foci.d: Directive 1/76: instead of arrests, quiet destruction - Zersetzung: rumours, lost jobs, broken marriages, failed exams. Opponents fall apart without a single trial for the West to see.
foci.o: Quiet: no damage to the republic's image, but the method needs ever more officers (police costs +5 %).

e: Shield and Sword: Enemy operative capture chance +5 %, Western drift +0.01
foci.d: Alt-history: the methods of the 1950s return - show trials, mass arrests, open intimidation. The streets fall silent, and the whole world watches.
foci.o: Loud: stability now, but Western drift +0.01 (the martyrs) and trade opinion -5 %.

e: Shield and Sword: Resistance suppression +12.5 %, Enemy operative capture chance +4 %
foci.d: The remand prison in Berlin-Hohenschönhausen, missing from every city map, and the special prison Bautzen II for the state's most prominent enemies - some of whom Bonn will later buy free.
The MfS's own motorised regiment, named after the founder of the Cheka, guards the Politburo's settlement at Wandlitz, the ministries and - in a crisis - the streets of Berlin.
Main Department II hunts the agents of the BND and the CIA - and turns the ones it catches into double agents.
Bugs, steamed letters, hidden cameras and jars of scent samples for the dogs: the ministry's workshops build the tools of total surveillance.
foci.o: Hub of the ministry-size choice.

e: Shield and Sword: Operative slots +1, Police costs +5 %
foci.d: From 43,000 officers in 1970 to 81,000 in 1982: the ministry grows faster than any other part of the state - and costs more every year.
foci.o: A second operative and a mighty MfS; police costs +5 %.

foci.d: Alt-history: the Central Committee's security department caps the ministry's growth. Fewer officers, more budget for the plan - and a Mielke who must ask before he acts.
foci.o: Cheaper police and money for the plan; the price is an offended MfS (-10).

e: Adds "Who Is Who?": Counter-intelligence +10 %, Enemy operative capture chance +5 %, Police costs +5 %
foci.d: Mielke's eternal question: who is who? By the 1980s the files fill more than a hundred kilometres of shelves - the ministry knows everything about everyone.
foci.o: Capstone of the MfS (no PP). Price inside the idea: police costs +5 %.

e: Shield and Sword: Intel network gain +10 %, Foreign subversive activities +10 %
foci.d: Alexander Schalck-Golodkowski, head of Commercial Coordination, is an MfS colonel on special assignment: the ministry protects KoKo's hard-currency deals - and takes its share.
foci.o: Cooperation with KoKo (no prerequisite: KoKo exists since 1966; the economy's Commercial Coordination foci expand it). Price: corruption +1 level.

foci.o: Society root and its one PP hub (five children).

e: The Party State: Ideological defence (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: Blue scarves for the six-year-olds, blue shirts for the fourteen-year-olds: almost every child marches in the Ernst Thälmann Pioneer Organisation and the Free German Youth.

e: The Party State: Ideology drift defence +5 %, Emerging drift +0.01
foci.d: At fourteen, nearly all young people pledge themselves to socialism in a secular ceremony, the Jugendweihe, that has all but replaced confirmation.
foci.o: The church loses its confirmands (Protestant Church -5).

foci.d: July-August 1973: the X World Festival of Youth and Students brings 25,000 foreign guests and eight million visitors to East Berlin - nine days in which the republic looks open and young.
foci.o: Named 'The Festival Generation' so that a leader tree can own the festival event itself; this focus fires the shared event key. Hub of the culture choice.

e: The Party State: Ideology drift defence -5 %
foci.d: December 1971: Honecker promises 'no taboos' in art for those who stand on firm socialist ground. Plenzdorf's 'The New Sufferings of Young W.' fills the theatres.
foci.o: The thaw: stability and creativity; less ideological control (drift defence -5 %).

e: The Party State: Ideological defence (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: Socialist realism or nothing: books are pulled, plays cancelled - and when Wolf Biermann is stripped of his citizenship, a stream of artists follows him west.
foci.o: Control and the cadres' approval; price: research speed -1 % (the brain drain of the artists and scientists).

foci.d: The Puhdys, Karat and City fill the stadiums with German-language rock; the state label Amiga presses the records, and the 60/40 rule keeps Western songs to a minimum on the radio.

e: The Socialist Camp: Opinion gain (same ideology) +3 %
foci.d: At the Olympic Games in Munich the GDR team, under its own flag and anthem, wins 66 medals and finishes third - ahead of the hosts.
foci.o: Hub of the sport choice.

e: Adds "Diplomats in Tracksuits": Stability +2 %, Opinion gain (same ideology) +5 %, Health costs +5 %
Event: Scandal risk: if the Inner-German course reaches 0.6 or a non-Emerging party governs, "The Doping Files" fires - the idea "Diplomats in Tracksuits" is removed and stability -5 %
foci.d: 1974: the leadership secretly makes 'supporting means' state policy. Thousands of athletes, many of them minors, receive anabolic steroids they are told are vitamins.
foci.o: Prestige now (no PP); health costs +5 % and a visible scandal risk later.

e: The Planned Economy: Health costs -10 %, Monthly population +0.03
foci.d: Alt-history: the doping plan is rejected. The money goes to mass sport - 'everyone, everywhere, once a week' - and the medals come a little more slowly.
foci.o: A healthier people; the cadres want medals, not sports grounds (Nomenklatura -5).

foci.d: Montreal 1976: the republic of seventeen million wins 40 gold medals - more than the United States, second only to the Soviet Union.
With almost nine in ten women at work, the state builds crèches and kindergartens on a scale no Western country matches.
9 March 1972: the Volkskammer legalises abortion in the first twelve weeks - and for the first time in its history, members of the CDU vote against a law.

e: The Planned Economy: Monthly population +0.05, Social costs +5 %
foci.d: From 1976 mothers get a paid year off after their second child, marriage loans that shrink with every birth, and priority for a flat.
foci.o: Births and loyalty; social costs +5 %.

foci.d: 1971: the Federation of Evangelical Churches in the GDR declares that it wants to be a church 'not alongside, not against, but in socialism'.
6 March 1978: Honecker receives Bishop Schönherr. The churches get airtime, prison chaplains and new church buildings; in return they stay out of politics - for a while.
foci.o: The church gains room it will later give to the peace and environmental circles (Church in Socialism popularity +3 %); new churches in the new towns (infrastructure).

e: The Party State: Foreign influence defence +5 %
foci.d: Every evening at eight the republic switches to the Tagesschau. The party must decide: fight the antennas or live with them.
foci.o: Hub of the West-television ladder.

e: Whichever form of The Window to the West is active is replaced by "The Antenna Raids": Western drift +0.01, Stability -3 %, Police costs +5 %, Expected welfare spending +5 %
foci.d: As in 'Operation Ochsenkopf' of 1961, FDJ brigades climb the roofs and saw off every antenna that points west. Fewer people watch - and everyone resents it.
foci.o: Ladder step (owner: society section): Western drift +0.02 -> +0.01, but stability -2 % -> -3 % and police costs +5 %.

e: Whichever form of The Window to the West is active is replaced by "The Tolerated Window": Western drift +0.02, Expected welfare spending +5 %
foci.d: 1973: Honecker concedes that anyone may switch Western television on and off as he likes. The raids stop; the comparison with the West stays.
foci.o: Ladder step (owner: society section): the stability malus is gone, the Western drift +0.02 stays; the cadres see a capitulation (Nomenklatura -5). Western governments can turn either variant into an asset.

e: The Party State: Ideological defence (Cold War) +5 %, Ideology drift defence +5 %
foci.d: Every Monday Karl-Eduard von Schnitzler cuts up West German news clips and explains what they really mean - the republic watches the enemy and argues back.

foci.a: "The Republic at Twenty" completed (`has_completed_focus`, no line - like every block root)
foci.d: 28 October 1969: Willy Brandt tells the Bundestag that there are two states in Germany - without recognising the second one. East Berlin must find an answer.
foci.o: Section root (block-root PP 50, MD style). The Inner-German course runs through the whole section; every course step rides on a real reward.

foci.b: `has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_ulb_erfurt_on_our_terms` (the Erfurt summit - no double reward)
e: Event: The Erfurt Summit: Brandt and Stoph talk for a day; the cheers for the Western chancellor shock the Politburo
Unlocks decisions: category "The German Question": Demarcation Campaign, Transit Talks, Raise the Minimum Exchange
foci.d: 19 March 1970: Willy Brandt steps off the train in Erfurt. Under the windows of the Erfurter Hof the crowd calls for the Western chancellor - and the MfS clears the square.
foci.o: No PP: the summit opens the decision category and a channel to Bonn; the 'Willy, Willy' shout costs stability (-2 %).

foci.b: `has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_ulb_kassel_recognition_first` (the Kassel meeting - no double reward)
e: Event: The Kassel Meeting: the talks stall; Moscow and Bonn will continue without East Berlin
foci.d: 21 May 1970: Willi Stoph in Kassel. Protesters tear down the flag of the republic, Brandt offers twenty points, Stoph insists on recognition - and both sides agree on a 'pause for reflection'.
foci.o: Hub of the first Abgrenzung-or-Annäherung choice.

e: The Socialist Camp: Research sharing +5 %, Trade opinion -3 %
foci.d: No treaty without full recognition under international law - and, Stoph added in Erfurt, 100 billion marks for the damage done by the open border before 1961.
foci.o: Moscow side (spec d T5): Moscow's favour and Comecon research; the West keeps its distance (trade opinion -3 %).

foci.d: Post, telephone, transit, trade: settle what can be settled and leave the big words to the communiqués. Moscow suspects East Berlin of running its own German policy.
foci.o: Bonn side (spec d T5): transit fees and Western trade; Moscow's Trust -2.

foci.d: 12 August 1970: Brandt and Kosygin sign the Moscow Treaty. The borders of the republic are declared inviolable - in a treaty nobody asked East Berlin about.
foci.o: The border guarantee is the reward; the humiliation is that Moscow signed it.

e: Western credit: treasury +1 % of GDP, debt +1 % of GDP
foci.d: Inner-German trade runs on an interest-free overdraft: the swing lets the republic buy in the West today and pay in goods later - 850 million units of account from 1975.
foci.o: Interest-free Western goods now; the debt and Moscow's Trust pay.

foci.a: Date from 03.09.1971 (the Four-Power Agreement on Berlin)
e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): Transit between West Germany and West Berlin through our territory without searches. If Bonn accepts: opinion +15 on both sides, Cold War tension -1, flag `COLDWAR_DDR_transit_agreement_accepted` (opens "The Transit Lump Sum"); Bonn gains secure access to West Berlin
foci.d: 17 December 1971: Michael Kohl and Egon Bahr sign the first agreement between the two German governments - sealed lorries and buses to West Berlin, no more random searches.
foci.o: Own side on sending: Western trade opinion (cost 7 -> 5: an offer focus).

e: Unlocks decisions: "Freikauf" in "The German Question" (course +0.05, income 0.3 % of GDP, stability -1 %)
foci.d: Freikauf - since 1963 Bonn has bought political prisoners free through the lawyer Wolfgang Vogel - some forty thousand marks a head, paid in goods through the Protestant church. The republic sells its own citizens.
foci.o: The prisoner ransom (Freikauf). The concept's decision "Freikauf" is gated on this focus id (COLDWAR_DDR_ger_freikauf).

foci.a: Bonn accepted the Transit Agreement (`has_country_flag = COLDWAR_DDR_transit_agreement_accepted`)
e: Shield and Sword: Civilian intel +5 %, Police costs +3 %
foci.d: Instead of tolls at the checkpoints Bonn pays a lump sum: 234.9 million marks a year at first, 525 million from 1980 - and the MfS watches every lay-by on the transit routes.
foci.o: Leaf gated on Bonn's acceptance, so a refusal blocks nothing else. The watching costs police money (+3 %).

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): Treaty on the Basis of Relations: equal sovereign states, an inviolable border, permanent missions in Bonn and East Berlin. If Bonn accepts: opinion +20 on both sides, Cold War tension -2, flag `COLDWAR_DDR_basic_treaty_accepted` (opens "Embassies in the West" at once); Bonn gains travel relief and family reunions for its citizens
foci.d: 21 December 1972: Bahr and Kohl sign in East Berlin. Two equal states and an inviolable border - but permanent missions instead of embassies, because Bonn still speaks of one nation.
foci.o: Ladder diplomatic_quarantine: the recognition step itself is "Embassies in the West" (rec), gated by this treaty's acceptance, a Western acceptance or 1976. Hub of the second Abgrenzung-or-Annäherung choice.

e: The Party State: Foreign influence defence +5 %, Ideology drift defence +5 %
foci.d: Two states, two nations: the socialist nation in the GDR has nothing in common with the bourgeois one in the FRG. Contacts with Westerners are reported, and in November 1973 the minimum exchange for visitors is doubled to twenty marks.
foci.o: Abgrenzung: the doubled minimum exchange, Moscow's favour and a closed society; the West trades less with us (-3 %). Honecker's leader tree has its own doctrine steps (Demarcation, Two Nations, The Gera Demands).

foci.d: Rapprochement instead of Demarcation: the two German states are foreign countries to each other only on paper. Trade, visits and credits flow - and Moscow starts counting them.
foci.o: Annäherung (alt-history: the road the leadership never took openly): inner-German trade money and calm; Moscow's Trust -5.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): A joint commission surveys and marks the whole inner-German border as a state border, the Elbe in mid-river. If Bonn accepts: opinion +10 on both sides, Cold War tension -1, our stability +2 %; Bonn gains agreed rules for border waters, fishing and accidents
foci.d: From 1973 a joint commission marks the inner-German border stone by stone. By 1978 it is done - except along the Elbe, where Bonn insists that the border runs on the eastern bank.
foci.o: Own side on sending: the NVA and the border troops like a surveyed border.

foci.d: 13 October 1980: every Western visitor must now change twenty-five marks a day at one to one - pensioners and children included. Visits from the West drop sharply; the treasury does not complain.
foci.o: The 1980 step of the minimum exchange (1973 step: The Policy of Demarcation). The concept's repeatable decision stays separate.

foci.a: Date from 01.01.1983; `COLDWAR_DDR_hon_the_billion_from_bavaria` not completed (one government-guaranteed credit per republic)
e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): A credit of one billion marks from a West German bank consortium, guaranteed by Bonn. If Bonn accepts: Western credit for us (treasury +2 % of GDP, debt +2 % of GDP), opinion +15 on both sides; in return we take the self-firing devices off the border fence (flag for the Border Troops) and exempt children from the minimum exchange
foci.d: June 1983: Franz Josef Strauss, the West's loudest anti-communist, arranges a bank credit of one billion marks with Bonn's guarantee. Schalck-Golodkowski negotiates; Moscow is told afterwards.
foci.o: Open after either side of the fork: the historical leadership practised Demarcation and still took Strauss's money. Leaf, so the one-credit guard blocks nothing else. Own side on sending: the banks lend cheaper at once (interest -5 %); Moscow's Trust -5.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): Exchanges of exhibitions, orchestras and scholars, the return of displaced art treasures and town twinnings. If Bonn accepts: opinion +15 on both sides; both sides gain research +2 % for 2 years
foci.d: 6 May 1986: after twelve years of talks the two states sign a cultural agreement - exhibitions, orchestras, art treasures scattered by the war - and Saarlouis twins with Eisenhüttenstadt, the first of some sixty town twinnings.

e: Offer to GER (they decide; no advance reward): A treaty on a chemical-weapons-free zone and a nuclear-free corridor in Central Europe, based on the SED-SPD drafts. If Bonn accepts: Cold War tension -2, opinion +20 on both sides; both sides gain defence budget costs -5 % for 3 years
The Party State: Ideological defence (Cold War) -5 %
foci.d: 1985-87: the SED and Bonn's Social Democrats draft a chemical-weapons-free zone, a nuclear-free corridor and a joint paper on 'the dispute of ideologies'. For once the party admits that the class enemy may also want peace.
foci.o: Alt-history as a state treaty (historically only party drafts; Bonn's government declined). No PP: the peace dividend is stability and influence in the West; the price is ideological ground and Moscow's Trust.

foci.a: "The Republic at Twenty" completed (`has_completed_focus`, no line - like every block root)
foci.d: Since 1955 Bonn has threatened every state that recognises the GDR with the loss of West German aid. In January 1970 barely half a dozen non-socialist capitals have dared.
foci.o: Section root (block-root PP 50).

e: Offer to EGY, SYR, IRQ, ALG (they decide; no advance reward): Agreements on friendship, trade and technical cooperation. If they accept: opinion +15 on both sides; they receive GDR engineers and teachers (construction speed +3 % for 2 years); we receive oil and cotton at fixed prices
Our influence in EGY, SYR, IRQ, ALG +2 %
foci.d: 1969 broke the doctrine: Iraq, Sudan, Syria, South Yemen and Egypt recognised the republic, Algeria follows in May 1970. Now the friendships need treaties.

e: Our influence in ITA, HOL, BEL +2 %
foci.d: The Thomanerchor, the Dresden Staatskapelle and the Berliner Ensemble tour capitals that do not recognise the republic - Bach and Brecht open doors that diplomats cannot.

e: Offer to RAJ (they decide; no advance reward): Full diplomatic relations and a trade agreement. If New Delhi accepts: opinion +20 on both sides, our influence in India +5 %; India receives machine tools and engineering scholarships
foci.d: India, the largest democracy of the Third World, keeps a trade mission in East Berlin and a treaty with Moscow. On 8 October 1972 it opens an embassy.
foci.o: Offer focus (cost 7 -> 5).

foci.d: Every spring and autumn Leipzig becomes the republic's shop window: Western ministers and industrialists who cannot be received in Berlin come to the fair.
foci.o: Fair contracts in hard currency; Moscow dislikes the Western guests (Moscow's Trust -2).

e: Diplomatic Quarantine eases by one step (whichever step is active)
Our influence in BAN, JAP, AST +2 %
foci.d: Between 1972 and 1974 the dam breaks: dozens of states establish relations with the republic, from Bangladesh to Japan and Australia.
foci.o: Ladder step 1 (owner: foreign policy). No PP: the ladder step is the reward.

e: Offer to ENG, FRA (they decide; no advance reward): Diplomatic relations with the GDR. If they accept: opinion +15 on both sides, flag `COLDWAR_DDR_west_recognition` (opens "Embassies in the West" at once); both sides gain a trade agreement
foci.d: 9 February 1973: Britain and France, two of the four powers responsible for Berlin, establish diplomatic relations with the republic on the same day.
foci.o: Offer focus (cost 7 -> 5).

e: Offer to FIN, SWE, AUS, SWI (they decide; no advance reward): Diplomatic relations and trade. If they accept: opinion +15 on both sides, flag `COLDWAR_DDR_west_recognition`; both sides gain a trade agreement
Our influence in FIN, SWE, AUS, SWI +2 %
foci.d: December 1972 and January 1973: Bern, Vienna, Stockholm and Helsinki recognise the republic - Finland on the same day as the Federal Republic.

foci.a: Bonn accepted the Basic Treaty (`COLDWAR_DDR_basic_treaty_accepted`) OR a Western capital accepted recognition (`COLDWAR_DDR_west_recognition`) OR date from 01.01.1976 (the West stops waiting for Bonn)
e: Diplomatic Quarantine eases by one step (whichever step is active)
The Party State: Foreign influence defence -5 %
Our influence in ITA, HOL, BEL +2 %
foci.d: The flag of the republic flies over embassies in London, Paris, Rome and The Hague. Recognised at last - and watched at last, because Western embassies talk to dissidents too.
foci.o: Ladder step 2. Recognition needs a Western yes (Basic Treaty, Paris and London, Neutral Capitals); the 1976 date keeps the ladder from dead-locking when the West refuses in multiplayer. Price: the embassies talk to dissidents (influence defence -5 %).

e: Ends Diplomatic Quarantine in every form
Our influence in RAJ, EGY, ALG +2 %
foci.d: 18 September 1973: the General Assembly admits both German states. The GDR becomes the 133rd member of the United Nations, one seat ahead of the Federal Republic.
foci.o: Ladder end: the quarantine is gone (no PP). No Security Council offer - the veto question is settled by the Western recognition step before it.

e: Offer to USA (they decide; no advance reward): Diplomatic relations between the United States and the GDR. If Washington accepts: opinion +15 on both sides, Cold War tension -1; the United States gains a consular agreement and talks on American property claims
foci.d: 4 September 1974: the United States, the last of the four powers, establishes diplomatic relations with the republic.
foci.o: Offer focus (cost 7 -> 5). Price: Moscow's Trust -3.

e: The Socialist Camp: Support campaigns (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: In the General Assembly the republic votes with the liberation movements and the non-aligned: against apartheid, against colonial wars, for a new international economic order.
foci.o: Bloc side: support campaigns and friends in Hanoi and Havana; the West hardens (tension +1).

e: Our influence in FIN, AUS, SWE +2 %
foci.d: The republic presents itself as the German state from which no war will ever start: disarmament proposals, conferences and a nuclear-free corridor through Central Europe.
foci.o: Neutral side: influence in the neutral capitals, calm and the church; Moscow distrusts a peace policy of its own (-3).

e: Event: The Exit Applications: citizens cite the Final Act; the MfS opens a file on every applicant
foci.d: 1 August 1975: the First Secretary and Chancellor Schmidt sign side by side. The borders are inviolable - and Basket Three promises freedom of movement. Within a year thousands quote Helsinki in their exit applications.
foci.o: Basket Two (trade) is the reward; Basket Three is the price (stability -2 %, the exit applications). No PP (cost 7 -> 5).

e: Shield and Sword: Enemy operative capture chance +4 %, Police costs +3 %
foci.d: The Final Act guarantees the border, not the right to cross it. Exit applicants lose their jobs, and the MfS sets up a central group against flight and emigration.
foci.o: Abgrenzung side: nobody leaves (workforce +2 %), Moscow is pleased; the central group costs police money (+3 %).

foci.d: Take the signature seriously: family reunions, visas for journalists, exit permits for those who insist. The pressure valve opens - and the West notices.
foci.o: Annäherung side (alt-history: Helsinki honoured instead of fought): family visits bring D-marks and the pressure valve calms; Moscow's Trust -3 and Western drift +0.01.

e: Adds "A State Among States": Trade opinion +5 %, Foreign influence +5 %
foci.d: January 1988: the head of the republic is received in Paris with full honours, and a GDR diplomat presides over the UN General Assembly. Recognition is complete - legitimacy is another matter.
foci.o: Recognition capstone (no PP).

foci.a: "The Republic at Twenty" completed (`has_completed_focus`, no line - like every block root)
foci.d: Twenty Soviet divisions, Soviet oil, Soviet protection: the republic owes its existence to Moscow and never forgets it - nor is it allowed to.
foci.o: Section root (block-root PP 50).

e: Unlocks decisions: category "Moscow": Report to the Kremlin, Host a Soviet Delegation, Request Soviet Credit
foci.d: Every summer the First Secretary flies to Brezhnev at Oreanda: a swim in the Black Sea, a long walk, and the year's quarrels settled between two men.
foci.o: Unlocks the Moscow's Trust tools (decision category "Moscow").

e: Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance for 25 years. If Moscow accepts: opinion +20 on both sides, Moscow's Trust +5; the Soviet Union gains the binding commitment of the NVA to the Unified Command
The Socialist Camp: Assistance effectiveness (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: 7 October 1975: a new treaty of friendship for twenty-five years. Unlike the treaty of 1964 it no longer speaks of German unity - only of the alliance.
foci.o: No PP. The NVA's binding to the Unified Command brings joint staff work (army experience).

foci.d: July 1971, Bucharest: Comecon adopts its Comprehensive Programme for socialist economic integration - joint plans, joint research, joint investment.
foci.o: Our participation only; the Soviet tree has its own Comprehensive Programme focus.

e: Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): We build our share of the Ust-Ilimsk pulp combine. If Moscow accepts: the Soviet Union gains the plant and construction speed +3 % for 2 years; we receive pulp and paper for ten years (our consumer goods -1 % via The Planned Economy)
foci.d: Builders and machines from the republic go to Siberia: the Ust-Ilimsk pulp combine is paid for with East German work and repaid with pulp and paper for years.
foci.o: Not the Soyuz pipeline (that is the Soviet tree's offer to us). Offer focus (cost 5 -> 3).

e: Event: The Bucharest Formula: Soviet oil follows the world price with a delay of a few years
Adds "Oil at World Prices": Tax revenue -4 %
foci.d: From 1975 Comecon prices follow a moving average of world prices. After the oil shock Soviet crude gets dearer every year - and the republic pays in goods it would rather sell for marks.
foci.o: The cost is the idea; the fork below converts it (Comecon integration or Western trade). Oil price/OPEC are not touched.

e: Replaces "Oil at World Prices" with "Oil for Hard Currency": Resource export revenue +5 %, Health costs +5 %
foci.d: Schwedt and Leuna crack Soviet crude into diesel and heating oil for Western customers while the republic heats with lignite. Moscow notices where its cheap oil ends up.
foci.o: Western-trade side: hard currency now; Moscow's Trust -3 and lignite smog at home (health costs +5 %).

e: Replaces "Oil at World Prices" with "Machines for Oil": Civilian factory output +5 %, Consumer goods +3 %
foci.d: Every tonne of oil is paid in sleeping cars from Ammendorf, ships from Rostock and machine tools from Karl-Marx-Stadt - goods the shops at home will never see.
foci.o: Comecon-integration side: full order books and Moscow's favour; the goods never reach the shops (consumer goods +3 %).

e: Offer to POL, CZE (they decide; no advance reward): Visa-free travel with identity cards both ways. If they accept: opinion +15 on both sides; both sides gain stability +2 % for 2 years from tourism and family visits
foci.d: 1 January 1972: an identity card is enough to cross the Oder or the Ore Mountains. Millions travel - and Polish shoppers empty the shelves of Frankfurt on the Oder.
foci.o: Price: shopping tourism (consumer goods +1 %).

e: Event: The Polish Crisis: Solidarity counts ten million members; a ruling party has lost the workers
Visa-free travel to Poland is suspended on our side of the border (our own rule; nothing changes in Poland)
foci.d: August 1980: the Lenin Shipyard in Gdansk strikes and Solidarity is born. On 30 October the republic closes its border to Polish visitors - the contagion must not cross the Oder.
foci.o: Hub of the Polish choice.

e: Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): We ask for joint Warsaw Pact action in Poland and offer three NVA divisions. If Moscow accepts: Moscow's Trust +5 more, army experience +25 for the NVA; what happens in Poland is the Soviet Union's decision
foci.d: 26 November 1980: the First Secretary writes to Brezhnev that Poland is lost without collective action. NVA divisions stand ready for the manoeuvre 'Soyuz-80'.
foci.o: Hard side: Moscow's favour and a ready NVA; tension +1 and Poland's enmity.

foci.d: The republic warns Moscow against a second Prague: the Poles must solve their crisis themselves - and the republic keeps its trade with the West.
foci.o: Alt-history, soft side: calm, Polish goodwill and Western trade; Moscow's Trust -3.

e: Event: The Euromissile Crisis: Pershing II in the West, Soviet operational-tactical missiles in the East
foci.d: November 1983: the Bundestag approves the Pershing II, the Soviet delegation walks out of Geneva, and Moscow announces new missiles for the GDR and Czechoslovakia.
foci.o: Hub of the missile choice.

e: Offer to SOV (they decide; no advance reward): Bases for Soviet operational-tactical missiles on our territory. If Moscow accepts: Moscow's Trust +5 more, Cold War tension +1; the Soviet Union gains forward missile positions
Adds the Cold War idea "Show of Strength" for 180 days
foci.d: Soviet OTR-22 missiles roll into Saxony and Mecklenburg; later the NVA receives its own OTR-23 launchers. The church's peace groups sew 'Swords into Ploughshares' onto their jackets.
foci.o: Hard side: a show of strength and the generals' approval; the peace circles turn against the state (Protestant Church -5).

foci.d: The missiles are 'the devil's work', the First Secretary says, and writes to Chancellor Kohl of a coalition of reason: the damage to German-German relations must be limited.
foci.o: Soft side: Western goodwill credit and calm at home; Moscow's Trust -5.

e: Adds "The Unbreakable Bond": Research sharing +5 %, Equipment costs -3 %
foci.d: Whatever the quarrels over oil, Poland or missiles, the republic stands where it was founded: in the first strategic echelon of the socialist community.
foci.o: Alliance capstone (no PP): Soviet licences build an arms factory.

foci.a: "The Republic at Twenty" completed (`has_completed_focus`, no line - like every block root)
e: The Socialist Camp: Support campaigns (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: Every trade unionist buys solidarity stamps: millions of marks a year for liberation movements and young states, handed out by the Afro-Asian Solidarity Committee.
foci.o: Section root without PP: the stamps are the price (0.3 % of GDP).

e: Offer to VIE (they decide; no advance reward): Solidarity shipments of medicine, trucks and hospital equipment, and university places. If Hanoi accepts: opinion +20 on both sides; Vietnam gains stability +3 % for 1 year
foci.d: The republic's most popular cause: medicine, trucks and hospital equipment for Hanoi, Vietnamese students in Dresden and Leipzig, schoolchildren collecting for 'the heroic Vietnamese people'.

e: Offer to VIE (they decide; no advance reward): Agreement on the employment and training of Vietnamese workers. If Hanoi accepts: we receive the idea "Contract Workers" (workforce +2 %; if already present it becomes "The Contract Worker Programme"); Vietnam gains trained workers and remittances (productivity growth +2 % for 3 years)
foci.d: Trainees from 1973, contract workers from 1980: tens of thousands of Vietnamese work in the Kombinate for four or five years, live in hostels and send goods home by the crate.
foci.o: "Contract Workers" is separate from the economy's labour-shortage ladder and stacks with it. Offer focus (cost 7 -> 5).

e: Offer to CUB (they decide; no advance reward): A long-term agreement: IFA trucks, machine tools and a cement works for sugar, citrus and nickel at fixed prices, and apprenticeships for Cuban workers. If Havana accepts: opinion +20 on both sides; we receive "Contract Workers" (as with Vietnam) and sugar; Cuba gains construction speed +3 % for 2 years
foci.d: June 1972: Fidel Castro names a small Caribbean cay after the murdered KPD leader. Trucks and machine tools go to Havana, sugar and oranges come back - and from 1978 Cuban apprentices follow.
foci.o: Cuban oranges for the shops. Offer focus (cost 5 -> 3).

foci.d: 11 September 1973: Pinochet's coup ends Allende's Chile. Some two thousand Chilean exiles find refuge in the republic, the Socialist leader Carlos Altamirano among them.

e: Offer to NIC (they decide; no advance reward): Doctors, teachers, a hospital and training for police and state security. If Managua accepts: opinion +20 on both sides; Nicaragua gains stability +3 % for 1 year and counter-intelligence +10 % for 2 years
foci.d: 19 July 1979: the Sandinistas enter Managua. Teachers, doctors and police instructors follow from the republic; in 1985 the Carlos Marx Hospital opens in Managua.

e: Our influence in AGL, MOZ, ETH +3 %
foci.d: 25 April 1974: the Carnation Revolution in Lisbon ends Portugal's empire. In Mozambique and Angola the movements the republic has supplied for a decade take power.
foci.o: Hub of the aid choice (no PP).

e: The Socialist Camp: Support campaigns (Cold War) +5 %, Assistance effectiveness (Cold War) +5 %
foci.d: Printing presses, radio transmitters, FDJ Friendship Brigades and thousands of scholarships: the republic exports teachers and textbooks rather than rifles.
foci.o: Civil side: support and assistance campaigns; the scholarships cost 0.3 % of GDP.

e: Shield and Sword: Foreign subversive activities +5 %
foci.d: NVA instructors, MfS advisers and rifles from army stocks: the republic builds armies and security services for its allies - discreetly, and in smaller numbers than the Cubans.
foci.o: Military side: experience, weapons know-how and subversion; the West notices (tension +1).

foci.b: Lamberz's "Comrades in Maputo" is completed (`has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_lam_comrades_in_maputo`): the treaty is already on the table OR `has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_lam_comrades_in_maputo` (the Mozambican commitment - no double reward)
e: Offer to MOZ (they decide; no advance reward): Treaty of friendship, the Moatize coal mine and a contract-worker agreement. If Maputo accepts: opinion +20 on both sides; we receive coal (energy +3 % via The Planned Economy) and "Contract Workers" (or "The Contract Worker Programme" if already present); Mozambique gains trucks, machinery and training (construction speed +5 % for 3 years)
foci.d: February 1979: a treaty of friendship with Samora Machel. The republic is to modernise the Moatize coal mine and train Mozambican workers - coal and labour for machines and know-how.
foci.o: Offer focus (cost 7 -> 3, no PP).

foci.d: The ANC's journal Sechaba is printed in the republic and its fighters train in Mecklenburg; from 1979 hundreds of Namibian children of SWAPO grow up in Bellin and Stassfurt.

e: Offer to AGL (they decide; no advance reward): Weapons, NVA instructors and trucks for the MPLA government, paid partly in coffee. If Luanda accepts: opinion +20 on both sides; Angola gains army organisation +5 % for 2 years; we receive coffee (stability +2 % for 1 year)
foci.d: 11 November 1975: Agostinho Neto proclaims independence while the guns of the civil war can be heard in Luanda. The republic sends weapons, instructors and IFA trucks - and takes coffee in return.
foci.o: Offer focus (cost 7 -> 5, no PP).

foci.b: Lamberz's "Comrades in Addis Ababa" is completed (`has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_lam_comrades_in_addis_ababa`): the treaty is already on the table OR `has_completed_focus = COLDWAR_DDR_lam_comrades_in_addis_ababa` (the Ethiopian commitment - no double reward)
e: Offer to ETH (they decide; no advance reward): MfS advisers for the Ethiopian state security, trucks and weapons for the Ogaden war, coffee in return. If Addis Ababa accepts: opinion +20 on both sides; Ethiopia gains counter-intelligence +10 % for 3 years; we receive coffee (stability +2 % for 1 year)
foci.d: 1977: Werner Lamberz flies to Addis Ababa. MfS officers build Mengistu's state security, trucks and weapons go to the Ogaden front, and Ethiopian coffee pays part of the bill.
foci.o: Offer focus (cost 7 -> 5, no PP).

foci.d: 1982: the republic is weeks away from insolvency in the West. In the Politburo someone finally asks what the trucks for Angola and the hostels for Hanoi really cost.
foci.o: Hub of the who-pays choice: the audit itself is the reward (corruption -1).

e: Offer to LBA, IRQ, SYR (they decide; no advance reward): Weapons, trucks and training for oil and hard currency. If they accept: we receive income 0.3 % of GDP a year for 3 years, opinion +10 on both sides; they gain army equipment
The Planned Economy: Resource export revenue +3 %
The Socialist Camp: Support campaigns (Cold War) -5 %
foci.d: From now on friends pay - in oil, coffee or hard currency. Weapons from army stocks go to Libya, Iraq and Syria; Werner Lamberz's last journey in 1978 was meant to arrange exactly that.
foci.o: The friends pay: hard currency and arms exports; the liberation movements notice (support campaigns -5 %).

sections.d: Trunk root (cost 1): January 1970. Ulbricht at 76, the Wall, the winter crisis, Brandt's Ostpolitik. Four directions hang from it, one per outlook; choosing one closes the other three.

Top: strengthen the Emerging outlook and hand power to another Emerging party (Havemann, Thälmann Guard, Mielke) or back to the SED. Bottom (gated, no line): open while an Emerging party governs - from day 1.
Top: the bloc parties and the underground strengthen the Western outlook; power to KoKo, CDU, LDPD or the SPD. Bottom (gated): open while a Western party governs.
Top: a third way between the blocs - planners, the church, directors, craftsmen, greens, farmers, Harich's neutralists. Bottom (gated): open while a Non-Aligned party governs.
Top: the national question - NDPD, the army, Prussia. Bottom (gated): open while a Nationalist party governs.

Alexander Schalck-Golodkowski's Commercial Coordination (KoKo, since 1966): the hard-currency empire of the MfS. As a ruling force: a pro-Western managerial dictatorship that sells the republic's loyalty to Bonn for credits - alt-hist.
The East CDU under Gerald Götting: a bloc party of the National Front. Freed from the bloc, it becomes a Christian democracy that seeks the road to Bonn - alt-hist (historically from 1989/90).

The LDPD under Manfred Gerlach: craftsmen, doctors, the old middle class. Gerlach was the first bloc leader to break with the SED in 1989; here he can do it earlier - rule of law, the market, confederation.

sections.t: Social Democratic Party in the GDR (3)
sections.d: The SPD was forced into the SED in 1946; its memory survives in the factories. Alt-hist: Friedrich Ebert Jr., son of the Reich President, returns to his roots and re-founds social democracy as Brandt's partner.
Robert Havemann, the dissident chemist ('Dialectics without Dogma'), and the democratic communists of the Prague Spring generation: socialism with a human face, councils and a free press.
The Thälmann Guard: the old KPD fighters and Spain veterans around Alfred Neumann. They want the hard 1950s back - mobilisation, purity, no Western credits, no consumer socialism.

sections.t: Shield and Sword of the Party (7)
sections.d: Erich Mielke's Ministry for State Security as a ruling power: the 'Shield and Sword of the Party' becomes the state itself.
Gerhard Schürer and the State Planning Commission: rule by planners and computers, beyond ideology - the honest balance sheet.
Bishop Albrecht Schönherr and the Federation of Evangelical Churches (1969): 'Church in socialism' - a neutral, pacifist, protestant republic.
The general directors of the Kombinate (Wolfgang Biermann, Carl Zeiss Jena) - the red barons take the state, plan becomes property.
The craftsmen, the 11,000 private and semi-state firms nationalised in 1972 - an alt-hist union of the small-business sector for free enterprise.
Reimar Gilsenbach and the nature conservation circles of the Kulturbund: against lignite, smog and the poisoned Elbe - alt-hist early green party.
The Democratic Farmers' Party (DBD) under Ernst Goldenbaum: the cooperative farmers as a neutral agrarian-socialist force.
Wolfgang Harich's 1956 platform: a 'special German road to socialism' - neutral, democratised, reunited. Harich was jailed for it; here he governs.
The NDPD under Lothar Bolz: the bloc party built in 1948 for former soldiers and the national middle class. Unleashed, it preaches the German nation above the class.
A national-revolutionary underground (collective leadership): dictatorship, purges, isolation. Player-only, small tree.
The Military Council of the NVA under Colonel General Heinz Keßler: the generals rule when the party fails.
Louis Ferdinand, Prince of Prussia, head of the House of Hohenzollern: the restoration of Prussia on the Spree. Player-only.

sections.t: The Party of the Working Class
sections.d: The SED's own tree (party 4), shared by every First Secretary: the party apparatus, the bloc parties, the FDJ, the party purge.

Changes of leadership. Ulbricht rules at the start. Every other candidate has a candidacy focus that only checks whether he is alive and in office and whether his backers stand behind him; nothing is mutually exclusive. The decision "Convene the Central Committee" then decides - with Moscow watching.

The founder at 76: his Economic System of Socialism, his own German policy, his lectures to Brezhnev. Survive Moscow's displeasure, consolidate the reform, or arrange the succession on your own terms.
The historical successor: Unity of Economic and Social Policy, the housing programme, Demarcation and recognition - and the debt that pays for it.
The Chairman of the Council of Ministers who met Brandt in Erfurt and Kassel: the government before the party, administration before ideology.
The economic czar: Kombinate, microelectronics, export at any price - the technocrat who trusts the balance sheet more than the Politburo.
The chief ideologist: purity of doctrine, Demarcation, culture under control - 'if your neighbour wallpapers, must you?'
The Army General and Minister of National Defence: the NVA as the school of the nation, the military-industrial republic.
The young star of the Politburo, head of agitation, Africa diplomat: a charismatic, modern socialism - if he avoids the Libyan desert.
Moscow's man: Werner Krolikowski reports directly to the Soviet embassy. Total loyalty to the Kremlin - and its rewards.
The FDJ generation: Egon Krenz, youth leader, security secretary, heir apparent - continuity with a younger face.
The Dresden reformer: Hans Modrow, never admitted to the Politburo - here the man of a careful reform from below.
Economy root (MD fan): the State Planning Commission, the Five-Year Plans 1971-85, the Kombinat reform, the 1972 nationalisation, hard currency.
'Chemistry gives bread, prosperity and beauty': Leuna, Buna, Schwedt; Eisenhüttenstadt steel; Rostock shipyards; machine tools and Trabant.
Robotron, ZMD Dresden, the 1-megabit chip, Carl Zeiss Jena, the Academy of Sciences - the race against COCOM.
King lignite, the Schwarze Pumpe, the Greifswald nuclear plant, the Druzhba oil and Soyuz gas pipelines, the 1981 oil cut.
LPG and the industrialisation of agriculture: crop and livestock specialisation, the KAP, fertiliser, meat for export.
Plattenbau and the housing programme, Intershop and Delikat, the Trabant waiting list, coffee, jeans and the 'Bückware' under the counter.
The NVA in the Warsaw Pact's first strategic echelon: motor-rifle divisions, the officer corps, the Political Main Administration, doctrine.
The Grenztruppen der DDR: the Wall, the inner-German border, the SM-70, the order to shoot - and its price.
The Volksmarine in the Baltic, the LSK/LV with MiG-21 and SA-2, the Fliegerkosmonaut - and Interkosmos.
The Kampfgruppen der Arbeiterklasse (400,000 men), the GST, civil defence, the 1978 'Wehrunterricht' in schools.
The Ministry for State Security: 43,000 officers in 1970, informers, the HV A of Markus Wolf, quiet 'Zersetzung' (decomposition) instead of open terror.
The FDJ and the Young Pioneers, sport and the 'miracle' of Munich 1972, culture between thaw and freeze, the church, women and the family.
Erfurt and Kassel, the Moscow Treaty, the Four-Power Agreement on Berlin, transit, the Basic Treaty, the Freikauf - Demarcation or Rapprochement.
From the Hallstein quarantine to UN membership: Third World recognitions, the Western capitals, Helsinki.
Brotherly alliance: the Soviet garrison, Comecon integration, the Orenburg pipeline, Interkosmos, Poland 1980.
The GDR in the Third World: Vietnam, Mozambique, Angola, Ethiopia, Nicaragua, the ANC, Stasi advisers and contract workers.

start_spirits.name: The Antifascist Protection Rampart
start_spirits.why: Since 13 August 1961 the Wall and 1,378 km of fortified border have stopped the exodus that cost the republic 2.7 million people. 47,000 border troops, mines and the order to shoot hold 17 million people in place - stability bought with the republic's reputation.
start_spirits.way_out: Border Troops: "The Modern Border" swaps it for "The Perfected Border" (cheaper, but the image does not improve). Rapprochement foci (travel relief) soften the drift; Western and Non-Aligned governments can open the border and remove it; hardliners harden it into "The Iron Border".

start_spirits.name: Overtaking Without Catching Up
start_spirits.why: Ulbricht's prestige programme: the 'structure-determining tasks' - petrochemistry, electronics, automation - swallow the investment budget. The hard winter of 1969/70 brings power cuts, delivery gaps and empty shelves.
start_spirits.way_out: Ulbricht consolidates it into "The Economic System of Socialism"; Honecker's "Unity of Economic and Social Policy" replaces it with a consumer course; Mittag's technocrats turn it into "Key Technologies"; the Five-Year Plan foci ease it.

start_spirits.name: The Group of Soviet Forces in Germany
start_spirits.why: Twenty Soviet divisions - some 380,000 men - are stationed between Wünsdorf and the Elbe. They protect the republic and they watch it: no decision in East Berlin is taken without a glance towards Karlshorst.
start_spirits.way_out: Stays as long as the republic is in the Warsaw Pact. Western and Non-Aligned governments can ask Moscow to withdraw the garrison (offer to the Soviet Union); a strong Moscow's Trust removes the political power malus ("Brothers in Arms").

start_spirits.name: Diplomatic Quarantine
start_spirits.why: Bonn's Hallstein Doctrine: whoever recognises the GDR loses West German aid. In January 1970 only the socialist states and a handful of Arab and Asian states recognise the republic.
start_spirits.way_out: Foreign policy: the recognition campaign (Third World recognitions, the Basic Treaty, UN membership) is a ladder that shrinks the quarantine step by step and removes it at UN membership.

start_spirits.name: The Labour Shortage
start_spirits.why: The exodus before 1961 took the young and the skilled. The population is old and shrinking; 86 % of women already work. Every new factory competes for the same hands.
start_spirits.way_out: Contract workers from Vietnam, Mozambique and Cuba, automation (Mittag), the natalist social policy (Honecker), the shift-work system - each removes one step of the ladder.

start_spirits.name: King Lignite
start_spirits.why: The republic runs on brown coal: over 250 million tonnes a year, the largest output in the world. Sulphur smog hangs over Bitterfeld, Espenhain and Leipzig; whole villages vanish into the open-cast mines.
start_spirits.way_out: Energy: nuclear power at Greifswald and the Soviet gas pipeline reduce it; "Coal Instead of Oil" (after the Soviet oil cut) doubles it; Green and church paths can remove it.

start_spirits.name: The Window to the West
start_spirits.why: ARD and ZDF reach 85 % of the republic - only the 'Valley of the Clueless' around Dresden is spared. Every evening 17 million people compare their lives with Western advertising.
start_spirits.way_out: Society: the campaign against Western antennas (lower drift, higher police costs) or Honecker's 1973 tolerance (stability malus removed, drift stays). Western governments turn it into an asset.

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_national_confederation.text: A German confederation under a joint national council; if Bonn accepts both states keep their armies and the inner-German border opens (course +0.30 for us)

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_koko_bavarian_credit.text: Bonn guarantees a bank credit of one billion D-Mark. If Bonn accepts: we receive treasury +1.5 % of GDP as debt and the course moves +0.10 towards Rapprochement; Bonn receives the dismantling of the SM-70 spring guns on the inner-German border and easier visits for families; Moscow's Trust -3 when the credit is signed. If Bonn refuses: nothing

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_cdu_accession.text: Accession of the five restored states to the Federal Republic under Article 23 of the Basic Law. If Bonn accepts: an accession treaty - the republic is peacefully integrated into the Federal Republic after a one-year transition (the Soviet garrison is settled in a separate treaty). If Bonn refuses: course +0.10, stability -3 %

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_cdu_garrison_withdrawa.text: A phased withdrawal of the Group of Soviet Forces in Germany over three years. If Moscow accepts: "The Group of Soviet Forces in Germany" is removed when the withdrawal ends, we pay the Soviet Union 1 % of GDP for housing the returning officers (as Bonn did in 1990), tension -2. If Moscow refuses: tension +2, Moscow's Trust -10

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_ldpd_confederation.text: A German confederation: customs and currency union and a joint council of ministers; both states keep their governments and alliances. If Bonn accepts: course +0.30 for us and the idea "The German Confederation" for both (trade opinion +15 %, research +3 %). If Bonn refuses: course +0.05

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_ldpd_accession.text: Accession to the Federal Republic. If Bonn accepts: the republic joins the Federal Republic after a one-year transition (peaceful integration; the Soviet garrison is settled in a separate treaty). If Bonn refuses: stability -3 %

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_spd_erfurt_revisited.text: A second Erfurt summit between two social-democratic governments. If Bonn accepts: course +0.10 for us, and both states receive the timed idea "The Erfurt Partnership" (trade opinion +10 %, research +2 % for 730 days). If Bonn refuses: nothing

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_spd_garrison_withdrawa.text: A staged withdrawal of the Group of Soviet Forces in Germany under a treaty of friendship and non-aggression; the republic stays in Comecon. If Moscow accepts: "The Group of Soviet Forces in Germany" is removed when the withdrawal ends, we pay the Soviet Union 1 % of GDP for barracks and housing, tension -2. If Moscow refuses: tension +1, Moscow's Trust -5

If Bonn accepts: unification after a one-year transition; the social rights of the GDR are kept for five years. If Bonn refuses: course +0.05, stability -2 %

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_kis_garrison_withdrawa.text: The Group of Soviet Forces in Germany withdraws within five years; if Moscow accepts: "The Group of Soviet Forces in Germany" is removed, tension -2, Moscow's Trust -10

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_kis_church_transfers.text: West German churches and Bonn pay in goods and hard currency for the church's hospitals and homes in the East; if Bonn accepts: income +0.5 % of GDP and Inner-German course +0.10 for us

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_kd_joint_ventures.text: West German firms may hold up to 49 % in joint ventures with the Kombinate; if Bonn accepts: two civilian factories are built in the republic at the investors' cost and Inner-German course +0.10

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_uct_open_trade.text: Inner-German trade without quotas and with free private contracts; if Bonn accepts: trade opinion +10 %, income +0.5 % of GDP and Inner-German course +0.10 for us

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_gl_elbe_commission.text: A joint Elbe commission: Hamburg pays part of the sewage plants upstream; if Bonn accepts: income +0.5 % of GDP and Inner-German course +0.05 for us

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_gl_clean_air_treaty.text: A Clean Air Treaty for the Ore Mountains: both sides fit desulphurisation to their border power stations; if Prague accepts: stability +2 % and agricultural productivity +2 % for both

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_dbd_grain_contract.text: A five-year grain supply contract at world-market prices; if accepted: stability +2 % and agricultural productivity +3 % for us, trade opinion +5 % for them

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_tws_yugoslav_partnersh.text: A partnership of two socialist states outside the blocs: advisers on self-management and preferential trade; if Belgrade accepts: trade opinion +5 % and research +2 % for both

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_tws_neutral_germany.text: A treaty of neutrality: both German states leave NATO and the Warsaw Pact, foreign troops leave, a joint commission prepares all-German elections; if Bonn accepts: Inner-German course +0.30 and tension -3 for us

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_tws_garrison_withdrawa.text: The Group of Soviet Forces in Germany withdraws in step with the Western armies; if Moscow accepts: "The Group of Soviet Forces in Germany" is removed and tension -2

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_tws_socialist_confeder.text: A confederation of the two German states with a joint council, free movement and a common market; if Bonn accepts: Inner-German course +0.20 and trade opinion +10 % for us

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_ldk_loyalty_pledge.text: The republic stays in the Warsaw Pact and Comecon, Moscow tolerates the internal reforms; if Moscow accepts: Moscow's Trust +10 for us

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_ldk_appeal_for_solidar.text: Belgrade and Bucharest publicly guarantee the Berlin Spring; if they accept: opinion +25 on both sides and tension +1

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_tg_soviet_advisers.text: Soviet advisers in every ministry and Kombinat; if Moscow accepts: research +3 % and factory efficiency growth +3 % for us, Moscow's Trust +5

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_ssp_security_advisers.text: MfS advisers build up the state security services of Aden and Damascus; if accepted: opinion +25 on both sides and intel network gain +5 % for us

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_hon_billion_credit.text: A bank credit of one billion DM guaranteed by the federal government. If they accept: Western credit for us (treasury +2 % of GDP, debt +2 % of GDP), Inner-German course +0.10 and Moscow's Trust -3; the automatic firing devices on the border are dismantled

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_hon_bonn_visit.text: A state visit with full honours. If they accept: stability +5 % and Inner-German course +0.10 for us, and both governments gain opinion of each other (+20)

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_sto_heads_of_governmen.text: A permanent channel between the two heads of government. If they accept: both governments gain opinion of each other (+15) and the Inner-German course moves +0.05

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_lam_ethiopia.text: Treaty of friendship: GDR security advisers and IFA trucks for Ethiopia. If Ethiopia accepts: it gains a timed idea (army organisation +3 %, police costs -10 %); we get Ethiopian coffee at friendship prices (timed idea: consumer goods -2 %, stability +2 %) and our opinion +15

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_lam_mozambique.text: Treaty of friendship: GDR engineers for the Moatize coal mines and teachers for FRELIMO schools. If Mozambique accepts: it gains a timed idea (education costs -10 %, resource gain +5 %); we get contract workers (timed idea: workforce +2 %) and our opinion +15

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_kro_confederation.text: A confederation of the GDR with the Soviet Union: joint foreign and defence policy and a joint currency board for the transferable rouble; the GDR keeps its own government. If the Soviet Union accepts: Moscow's Trust +25 and the idea "The Union Treaty" for us (stability +5 %, political power +10 %, energy +10 %); if it declines: Moscow's Trust +5 for the gesture

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_kre_travel_credit.text: West Germany finances a travel-currency fund and a large credit line; every GDR citizen may travel to the West. If Bonn accepts: treasury +1 % of GDP as a credit (debt +1 %), Inner-German course +0.10, our opinion +15; if it declines: course -0.05

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_mod_treaty_community.text: A Treaty Community of the two German states: joint commissions for economy, transport, environment and culture and a long-term trade and credit agreement. If Bonn accepts: Inner-German course +0.20, treasury +1 % of GDP as a credit (debt +1 %), timed idea trade opinion +15 %; if it declines: course -0.05

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_vw_engine_licence.text: A four-stroke engine plant in Karl-Marx-Stadt under Volkswagen licence, paid in counter-trade: if Bonn accepts, we build one civilian factory (paid) and Inner-German course +0.05; they gain influence in our country +3 % and the counter-trade deliveries

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_soviet_ship_orders.text: A long-term order for trawlers and freighters: if they accept, we gain Moscow's Trust +5 and dockyard output +5 % (The Planned Economy); they gain a timed naval production bonus (their own event effect)

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_soyuz_pipeline.text: We build our section of the Orenburg pipeline in return for natural gas: if they accept, we gain Moscow's Trust +5 and energy production +5 % (The Planned Economy) and set COLDWAR_DDR_soyuz_gas; they gain construction speed +5 % for two years from our builders (their own effect)

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_coffee_plantations.text: A coffee partnership: we finance plantations in Dak Lak and are paid in coffee - if they accept, consumer goods -2 % for us (The Planned Economy) and our opinion of them +15; they gain agricultural productivity +5 % for three years (their own event effect)

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_warning_shots.text: Bonn answers the end of the shootings with a goodwill trade credit: if they accept, we gain +0.5 % of GDP as income and the Inner-German course moves +0.05 towards Rapprochement

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_interkosmos_cosmonaut.text: A GDR cosmonaut flies on a Soyuz mission of the Interkosmos programme (historically Sigmund Jähn, Soyuz 31, 26 August 1978). If the Soviet Union accepts: our event "Our Man in Space" (stability +3 %, SED popularity +2 %, Moscow's Trust +3); the Soviet Union gains opinion of us +15. If it refuses: Moscow's Trust -2 for us, nothing for them

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_transit_agreement.text: Transit between West Germany and West Berlin through our territory without searches. If Bonn accepts: opinion +15 on both sides, Cold War tension -1, flag `COLDWAR_DDR_transit_agreement_accepted` (opens "The Transit Lump Sum"); Bonn gains secure access to West Berlin

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_basic_treaty.text: Treaty on the Basis of Relations: equal sovereign states, an inviolable border, permanent missions in Bonn and East Berlin. If Bonn accepts: opinion +20 on both sides, Cold War tension -2, flag `COLDWAR_DDR_basic_treaty_accepted` (opens "Embassies in the West" at once); Bonn gains travel relief and family reunions for its citizens

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_border_commission.text: A joint commission surveys and marks the whole inner-German border as a state border, the Elbe in mid-river. If Bonn accepts: opinion +10 on both sides, Cold War tension -1, our stability +2 %; Bonn gains agreed rules for border waters, fishing and accidents

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_billion_credit.text: A credit of one billion marks from a West German bank consortium, guaranteed by Bonn. If Bonn accepts: Western credit for us (treasury +2 % of GDP, debt +2 % of GDP), opinion +15 on both sides; in return we take the self-firing devices off the border fence (flag for the Border Troops) and exempt children from the minimum exchange

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_cultural_agreement.text: Exchanges of exhibitions, orchestras and scholars, the return of displaced art treasures and town twinnings. If Bonn accepts: opinion +15 on both sides; both sides gain research +2 % for 2 years

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_common_security.text: A treaty on a chemical-weapons-free zone and a nuclear-free corridor in Central Europe, based on the SED-SPD drafts. If Bonn accepts: Cold War tension -2, opinion +20 on both sides; both sides gain defence budget costs -5 % for 3 years

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_arab_friendship.text: Agreements on friendship, trade and technical cooperation. If they accept: opinion +15 on both sides; they receive GDR engineers and teachers (construction speed +3 % for 2 years); we receive oil and cotton at fixed prices

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_recognition_india.text: Full diplomatic relations and a trade agreement. If New Delhi accepts: opinion +20 on both sides, our influence in India +5 %; India receives machine tools and engineering scholarships

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_paris_and_london.text: Diplomatic relations with the GDR. If they accept: opinion +15 on both sides, flag `COLDWAR_DDR_west_recognition` (opens "Embassies in the West" at once); both sides gain a trade agreement

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_neutral_capitals.text: Diplomatic relations and trade. If they accept: opinion +15 on both sides, flag `COLDWAR_DDR_west_recognition`; both sides gain a trade agreement

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_washington.text: Diplomatic relations between the United States and the GDR. If Washington accepts: opinion +15 on both sides, Cold War tension -1; the United States gains a consular agreement and talks on American property claims

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_friendship_treaty_1975.text: Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance for 25 years. If Moscow accepts: opinion +20 on both sides, Moscow's Trust +5; the Soviet Union gains the binding commitment of the NVA to the Unified Command

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_ust_ilimsk.text: We build our share of the Ust-Ilimsk pulp combine. If Moscow accepts: the Soviet Union gains the plant and construction speed +3 % for 2 years; we receive pulp and paper for ten years (our consumer goods -1 % via The Planned Economy)

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_open_socialist_borders.text: Visa-free travel with identity cards both ways. If they accept: opinion +15 on both sides; both sides gain stability +2 % for 2 years from tourism and family visits

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_fraternal_assistance_p.text: We ask for joint Warsaw Pact action in Poland and offer three NVA divisions. If Moscow accepts: Moscow's Trust +5 more, army experience +25 for the NVA; what happens in Poland is the Soviet Union's decision

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_counter_deployment.text: Bases for Soviet operational-tactical missiles on our territory. If Moscow accepts: Moscow's Trust +5 more, Cold War tension +1; the Soviet Union gains forward missile positions

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_vietnam_aid.text: Solidarity shipments of medicine, trucks and hospital equipment, and university places. If Hanoi accepts: opinion +20 on both sides; Vietnam gains stability +3 % for 1 year

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_vietnam_contract_worke.text: Agreement on the employment and training of Vietnamese workers. If Hanoi accepts: we receive the idea "Contract Workers" (workforce +2 %; if already present it becomes "The Contract Worker Programme"); Vietnam gains trained workers and remittances (productivity growth +2 % for 3 years)

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_cuba_trade.text: A long-term agreement: IFA trucks, machine tools and a cement works for sugar, citrus and nickel at fixed prices, and apprenticeships for Cuban workers. If Havana accepts: opinion +20 on both sides; we receive "Contract Workers" (as with Vietnam) and sugar; Cuba gains construction speed +3 % for 2 years

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_nicaragua.text: Doctors, teachers, a hospital and training for police and state security. If Managua accepts: opinion +20 on both sides; Nicaragua gains stability +3 % for 1 year and counter-intelligence +10 % for 2 years

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_mozambique.text: Treaty of friendship, the Moatize coal mine and a contract-worker agreement. If Maputo accepts: opinion +20 on both sides; we receive coal (energy +3 % via The Planned Economy) and "Contract Workers" (or "The Contract Worker Programme" if already present); Mozambique gains trucks, machinery and training (construction speed +5 % for 3 years)

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_angola.text: Weapons, NVA instructors and trucks for the MPLA government, paid partly in coffee. If Luanda accepts: opinion +20 on both sides; Angola gains army organisation +5 % for 2 years; we receive coffee (stability +2 % for 1 year)

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_ethiopia.text: MfS advisers for the Ethiopian state security, trucks and weapons for the Ogaden war, coffee in return. If Addis Ababa accepts: opinion +20 on both sides; Ethiopia gains counter-intelligence +10 % for 3 years; we receive coffee (stability +2 % for 1 year)

COLDWAR_DDR_offer_arms_for_oil.text: Weapons, trucks and training for oil and hard currency. If they accept: we receive income 0.3 % of GDP a year for 3 years, opinion +10 on both sides; they gain army equipment

events.COLDWAR_DDR_intro: January 1970: The Republic at Twenty - Ulbricht, the Wall, the winter crisis, Brandt's Ostpolitik; explains Moscow's Trust, the Inner-German course and the start spirits
events.COLDWAR_DDR_ulbricht_resigns: 3 May 1971: Ulbricht resigns, Honecker is elected
events.COLDWAR_DDR_ldk_warsaw_pact_manoeuvres: Warsaw Pact Manoeuvres on the Border (30 days later): Soviet, Polish and Czechoslovak divisions exercise along our borders. Concede (Moscow's Trust +10, stability -5 %) or stand firm (war support +5 %, tension +3; if Moscow's Trust is below 20 the Soviet Union receives the decision "Fraternal Assistance" - its own choice)
events.COLDWAR_DDR_ssp_the_world_condemns: The World Condemns: Western capitals recall their ambassadors and freeze talks, the Non-Aligned protest; each country decides its own reaction through the event
events.COLDWAR_DDR_ulb_the_old_man_stays: Ambassador Abrasimov delivers Brezhnev's displeasure; the signatories of the letter must recant or lose their posts
events.COLDWAR_DDR_ulb_heart_attack: Spring 1973: a heart attack - the doctors save him, but the old man must rest at Lake Döllnsee
events.COLDWAR_DDR_kessler_succession: At Hoffmann's death the Central Committee is asked to elect Heinz Keßler; if it refuses, the Military Council of the NVA under Keßler may take power ("The Generals Step In" opens without its opinion condition)
events.COLDWAR_DDR_guillaume_affair: News event: the Guillaume affair - the Chancellor's aide unmasked, Willy Brandt resigns (flavour only, no effect in West Germany)
events.COLDWAR_DDR_x_world_festival: The X World Festival (28 July - 5 August 1973) in East Berlin
events.COLDWAR_DDR_the_doping_files: Scandal risk: if the Inner-German course reaches 0.6 or a non-Emerging party governs, "The Doping Files" fires - the idea "Diplomats in Tracksuits" is removed and stability -5 %
events.COLDWAR_DDR_erfurt_summit: The Erfurt Summit: Brandt and Stoph talk for a day; the cheers for the Western chancellor shock the Politburo
events.COLDWAR_DDR_kassel_meeting: The Kassel Meeting: the talks stall; Moscow and Bonn will continue without East Berlin
events.COLDWAR_DDR_helsinki_exit_applications: The Exit Applications: citizens cite the Final Act; the MfS opens a file on every applicant
events.COLDWAR_DDR_bucharest_formula: The Bucharest Formula: Soviet oil follows the world price with a delay of a few years
events.COLDWAR_DDR_polish_crisis: The Polish Crisis: Solidarity counts ten million members; a ruling party has lost the workers
events.COLDWAR_DDR_euromissiles: The Euromissile Crisis: Pershing II in the West, Soviet operational-tactical missiles in the East
